subPackages.name: Domain
subPackages.documentation:
The domain package defines primitive datatypes that are used by classes in other packages. Stereotypes are used to describe the datatypes. The following stereotypes are defined:
<<enumeration>> A list of permissible constant values.
<<Primitive>> The most basic data types used to compose all other data types.
<<CIMDatatype>> A datatype that contains a value attribute, an optional unit of measure and a unit multiplier. The unit and multiplier may be specified as a static variable initialized to the allowed value.
<<Compound>> A composite of Primitive, enumeration, CIMDatatype or other Compound classes, as long as the Compound classes do not recurse.
For all datatypes both positive and negative values are allowed unless stated otherwise for a particular datatype.

The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

classes.name: TimeInterval
classes.documentation: Interval between two times.

attributes.name: end
attributes.documentation: End time of this interval.

attributes.name: start
attributes.documentation: Start time of this interval.

classes.name: UnitMultiplier
classes.documentation:
The unit multipliers defined for the CIM.  When applied to unit symbols, the unit symbol is treated as a derived unit. Regardless of the contents of the unit symbol text, the unit symbol shall be treated as if it were a single-character unit symbol. Unit symbols should not contain multipliers, and it should be left to the multiplier to define the multiple for an entire data type. 

For example, if a unit symbol is "m2Pers" and the multiplier is "k", then the value is k(m**2/s), and the multiplier applies to the entire final value, not to any individual part of the value. This can be conceptualized by substituting a derived unit symbol for the unit type. If one imagines that the symbol "Ю" represents the derived unit "m2Pers", then applying the multiplier "k" can be conceptualized simply as "kЮ".

For example, the SI unit for mass is "kg" and not "g".  If the unit symbol is defined as "kg", then the multiplier is applied to "kg" as a whole and does not replace the "k" in front of the "g". In this case, the multiplier of "m" would be used with the unit symbol of "kg" to represent one gram.  As a text string, this violates the instructions in IEC 80000-1. However, because the unit symbol in CIM is treated as a derived unit instead of as an SI unit, it makes more sense to conceptualize the "kg" as if it were replaced by one of the proposed replacements for the SI mass symbol. If one imagines that the "kg" were replaced by a symbol "Ю", then it is easier to conceptualize the multiplier "m" as creating the proper unit "mЮ", and not the forbidden unit "mkg".

literals.name: none
literals.documentation: No multiplier or equivalently multiply by 1.

classes.name: UnitSymbol
classes.documentation:
The derived units defined for usage in the CIM. In some cases, the derived unit is equal to an SI unit. Whenever possible, the standard derived symbol is used instead of the formula for the derived unit. For example, the unit symbol Farad is defined as "F" instead of "CPerV". In cases where a standard symbol does not exist for a derived unit, the formula for the unit is used as the unit symbol. For example, density does not have a standard symbol and so it is represented as "kgPerm3". With the exception of the "kg", which is an SI unit, the unit symbols do not contain multipliers and therefore represent the base derived unit to which a multiplier can be applied as a whole. 
Every unit symbol is treated as an unparseable text as if it were a single-letter symbol. The meaning of each unit symbol is defined by the accompanying descriptive text and not by the text contents of the unit symbol.
To allow the widest possible range of serializations without requiring special character handling, several substitutions are made which deviate from the format described in IEC 80000-1. The division symbol "/" is replaced by the letters "Per". Exponents are written in plain text after the unit as "m3" instead of being formatted as "m" with a superscript of 3  or introducing a symbol as in "m^3". The degree symbol "°" is replaced with the letters "deg". Any clarification of the meaning for a substitution is included in the description for the unit symbol.
Non-SI units are included in list of unit symbols to allow sources of data to be correctly labelled with their non-SI units (for example, a GPS sensor that is reporting numbers that represent feet instead of meters). This allows software to use the unit symbol information correctly convert and scale the raw data of those sources into SI-based units. 
The integer values are used for harmonization with IEC 61850.

literals.name: none
literals.documentation: Dimension less quantity, e.g. count, per unit, etc.

literals.name: kg
literals.documentation: Mass in kilograms.  Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: degC
literals.documentation:
Relative temperature in degrees Celsius.
In the SI unit system the symbol is °C. Electric charge is measured in coulomb that has the unit symbol C. To distinguish degree Celsius from coulomb the symbol used in the UML is degC. The reason for not using °C is that the special character ° is difficult to manage in software.

literals.name: W
literals.documentation: Real power in watts (J/s). Electrical power may have real and reactive components. The real portion of electrical power (I²R or VIcos(phi)), is expressed in Watts. See also apparent power and reactive power.

literals.name: Pa
literals.documentation: Pressure in pascals (N/mІ). Note: the absolute or relative measurement of pressure is implied with this entry. See below for more explicit forms.

literals.name: mPers2
literals.documentation: Acceleration in metres per second squared (m/sІ).

literals.name: m3Pers
literals.documentation: Volumetric flow rate in cubic metres per second (mі/s).

literals.name: mPerm3
literals.documentation: Fuel efficiency in metres per cubic metres (m/mі).

literals.name: kgm
literals.documentation: Moment of mass in kilogram metres (kg·m) (first moment of mass). Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: kgPerm3
literals.documentation: Density in kilogram/cubic metres (kg/mі). Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: rotPers
literals.documentation: Rotations per second (1/s). See also Hz (1/s).

literals.name: radPers
literals.documentation: Angular velocity in radians per second (rad/s).

literals.name: WPerm2
literals.documentation: Heat flux density, irradiance, watts per square metre.

literals.name: JPerm2
literals.documentation: Insulation energy density, joules per square metre or watt second per square metre.

literals.name: KPers
literals.documentation: Temperature change rate in kelvins per second.

literals.name: PaPers
literals.documentation: Pressure change rate in pascals per second.

literals.name: JPerkgK
literals.documentation: Specific heat capacity, specific entropy, joules per kilogram Kelvin.

literals.name: VA
literals.documentation: Apparent power in volt amperes. See also real power and reactive power.

literals.name: VAr
literals.documentation:
Reactive power in volt amperes reactive. The “reactive” or “imaginary” component of electrical power (VIsin(phi)). (See also real power and apparent power).
Note: Different meter designs use different methods to arrive at their results. Some meters may compute reactive power as an arithmetic value, while others compute the value vectorially. The data consumer should determine the method in use and the suitability of the measurement for the intended purpose.

literals.name: cosPhi
literals.documentation:
Power factor, dimensionless.
Note 1: This definition of power factor only holds for balanced systems. See the alternative definition under code 153.
Note 2 : Beware of differing sign conventions in use between the IEC and EEI. It is assumed that the data consumer understands the type of meter in use and the sign convention in use by the utility.

literals.name: A2s
literals.documentation: Ampere squared time in square amperes (AІs).

literals.name: VAh
literals.documentation: Apparent energy in volt ampere hours.

literals.name: VArh
literals.documentation: Reactive energy in volt ampere reactive hours.

literals.name: VPerHz
literals.documentation: Magnetic flux in volt per hertz.

literals.name: HzPers
literals.documentation: Rate of change of frequency in hertz per second.

literals.name: charPers
literals.documentation: Data rate (baud) in characters per second.

literals.name: kgm2
literals.documentation: Moment of mass in kilogram square metres (kg·mІ) (Second moment of mass, commonly called the moment of inertia). Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: dB
literals.documentation: Sound pressure level in decibels. Note:  multiplier “d” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: WPers
literals.documentation: Ramp rate in watts per second.

literals.name: lPers
literals.documentation: Volumetric flow rate in litres per second.

literals.name: dBm
literals.documentation: Power level (logarithmic ratio of signal strength , Bel-mW), normalized to 1mW. Note:  multiplier “d” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: h
literals.documentation: Time in hours, hour = 60 min = 3600 s.

literals.name: APerm
literals.documentation: A/m, magnetic field strength, amperes per metre.

literals.name: m3Perh
literals.documentation: Volumetric flow rate, cubic metres per hour.

literals.name: gal
literals.documentation: Volume in gallons, US gallon (1 gal = 231 in3 = 128 fl ounce).

literals.name: l
literals.documentation: Volume in litres, litre = dm3 = m3/1000.

literals.name: lPerh
literals.documentation: Volumetric flow rate, litres per hour.

literals.name: lPerl
literals.documentation: Concentration, The ratio of the volume of a solute divided by the volume of  the solution. Note: Users may need use a prefix such a ‘µ’ to express a quantity such as ‘µL/L’.

literals.name: gPerg
literals.documentation: Concentration, The ratio of the mass of a solute divided by the mass of  the solution. Note: Users may need use a prefix such a ‘µ’ to express a quantity such as ‘µg/g’.

literals.name: molPerm3
literals.documentation: Concentration, The amount of substance concentration, (c), the amount of solvent in moles divided by the volume of solution in mі.

literals.name: molPermol
literals.documentation: Concentration, Molar fraction, the ratio of the molar amount of a solute divided by the molar amount of the solution.

literals.name: molPerkg
literals.documentation: Concentration, Molality, the amount of solute in moles and the amount of solvent in kilograms.

literals.name: sPers
literals.documentation: Time, Ratio of time.  Note: Users may need to supply a prefix such as ‘µ’ to show rates such as ‘µs/s’.

literals.name: HzPerHz
literals.documentation: Frequency, rate of frequency change.   Note: Users may need to supply a prefix such as ‘m’ to show rates such as ‘mHz/Hz’.

literals.name: VPerV
literals.documentation: Voltage, ratio of voltages.  Note: Users may need to supply a prefix such as ‘m’ to show rates such as ‘mV/V’.

literals.name: APerA
literals.documentation: Current, ratio of amperages.   Note: Users may need to supply a prefix such as ‘m’ to show rates such as ‘mA/A’.

literals.name: VPerVA
literals.documentation: Power factor, PF, the ratio of the active power to the apparent power.  Note: The sign convention used for power factor will differ between IEC meters and EEI (ANSI) meters. It is assumed that the data consumers understand the type of meter being used and agree on the sign convention in use at any given utility.

literals.name: m3Uncompensated
literals.documentation: Volume, cubic metres, with the value uncompensated for weather effects.

literals.name: m3Compensated
literals.documentation: Volume, cubic metres, with the value compensated for weather effects.

literals.name: WPerW
literals.documentation: Signal Strength, ratio of power.   Note: Users may need to supply a prefix such as ‘m’ to show rates such as ‘mW/W’.

literals.name: m3Perkg
literals.documentation: Specific volume, cubic metres per kilogram, v.

literals.name: radPers2
literals.documentation: Angular acceleration, radians per second squared.

literals.name: JPerm3
literals.documentation: Energy density, joules per cubic metre.

literals.name: VPerm
literals.documentation: Electric field strength, volts per metre.

literals.name: CPerm3
literals.documentation: Electric charge density, coulombs per cubic metre.

literals.name: CPerm2
literals.documentation: Surface charge density, coulombs per square metre.

literals.name: JPermolK
literals.documentation: Molar entropy, molar heat capacity, joules per mole kelvin.

literals.name: GyPers
literals.documentation: Absorbed dose rate, grays per second.

literals.name: WPerm2sr
literals.documentation: Radiance, watts per square metre steradian.

literals.name: katPerm3
literals.documentation: Catalytic activity concentration, katals per cubic metre.

literals.name: d
literals.documentation: Time in days, day = 24 h = 86400 s.

literals.name: tonne
literals.documentation: Mass in tons, “tonne” or “metric  ton” (1000 kg = 1 Mg).

literals.name: mmHg
literals.documentation: Pressure, millimetres of mercury (1 mmHg is approximately 133.3 Pa).

literals.name: G
literals.documentation: Magnetic flux density, gausses (1 G = 10-4 T).

literals.name: Oe
literals.documentation: Magnetic field in oersteds, (1 Oe = (103/4p) A/m).

literals.name: WPerA
literals.documentation: Active power per current flow, watts per Ampere.

literals.name: VPerVAr
literals.documentation: Power factor, PF, the ratio of the active power to the apparent power. Note: The sign convention used for power factor will differ between IEC meters and EEI (ANSI) meters. It is assumed that the data consumers understand the type of meter being used and agree on the sign convention in use at any given utility.

literals.name: ohmPerm
literals.documentation: Electric resistance per length in ohms per metre ((V/A)/m).

literals.name: kgPerJ
literals.documentation: Weight per energy in kilograms per joule (kg/J). Note: multiplier “k” is included in this unit symbol for compatibility with IEC 61850-7-3.

literals.name: JPers
literals.documentation: Energy rate in joules per second (J/s).

classes.name: Voltage
classes.documentation: Electrical voltage, can be both AC and DC.

classes.name: VoltagePerReactivePower
classes.documentation: Voltage variation with reactive power.

classes.name: Volume
classes.documentation: Volume.

classes.name: VolumeFlowRate
classes.documentation: Volume per time.

classes.name: WaterLevel
classes.documentation: Reservoir water level referred to a given datum such as mean sea level.

subPackages.name: Core
subPackages.documentation: Contains the core PowerSystemResource and ConductingEquipment entities shared by all applications plus common collections of those entities. Not all applications require all the Core entities.  This package does not depend on any other package except the Domain package, but most of the other packages have associations and generalizations that depend on it.

classes.name: ACDCTerminal
classes.documentation: An electrical connection point (AC or DC) to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

attributes.name: connected
attributes.documentation:
The connected status is related to a bus-branch model and the topological node to terminal relation.  True implies the terminal is connected to the related topological node and false implies it is not. 
In a bus-branch model, the connected status is used to tell if equipment is disconnected without having to change the connectivity described by the topological node to terminal relation. A valid case is that conducting equipment can be connected in one end and open in the other. In particular for an AC line segment, where the reactive line charging can be significant, this is a relevant case.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: The orientation of the terminal connections for a multiple terminal conducting equipment.  The sequence numbering starts with 1 and additional terminals should follow in increasing order.   The first terminal is the "starting point" for a two terminal branch.

classes.name: BaseFrequency
classes.documentation: The BaseFrequency class describes a base frequency for a power system network. In case of multiple power networks with different frequencies, e.g. 50 Hz or 60 Hz each network will have its own base frequency class. Hence it is assumed that power system objects having different base frequencies appear in separate documents where each document has a single base frequency instance.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.documentation: The base frequency.

classes.name: BasePower
classes.documentation: The BasePower class defines the base power used in the per unit calculations.

attributes.name: basePower
attributes.documentation: Value used as base power.

classes.name: BaseVoltage
classes.documentation: Defines a system base voltage which is referenced.

attributes.name: nominalVoltage
attributes.documentation: The power system resource's base voltage.  Shall be a positive value and not zero.

classes.name: BasicIntervalSchedule
classes.documentation: Schedule of values at points in time.

attributes.name: startTime
attributes.documentation: The time for the first time point.  The value can be a time of day, not a specific date.

attributes.name: value1Multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for value1.

attributes.name: value1Unit
attributes.documentation: Value1 units of measure.

attributes.name: value2Multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for value2.

attributes.name: value2Unit
attributes.documentation: Value2 units of measure.

classes.name: Bay
classes.documentation: A collection of power system resources (within a given substation) including conducting equipment, protection relays, measurements, and telemetry.  A bay typically represents a physical grouping related to modularization of equipment.

attributes.name: bayEnergyMeasFlag
attributes.documentation: Indicates the presence/absence of energy measurements.

attributes.name: bayPowerMeasFlag
attributes.documentation: Indicates the presence/absence of active/reactive power measurements.

attributes.name: breakerConfiguration
attributes.documentation: Breaker configuration.

attributes.name: busBarConfiguration
attributes.documentation: Busbar configuration.

classes.name: BreakerConfiguration
classes.documentation: Switching arrangement for bay.

classes.name: BusbarConfiguration
classes.documentation: Busbar layout for bay.

classes.name: ConductingEquipment
classes.documentation: The parts of the AC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through terminals.

classes.name: ConnectivityNode
classes.documentation: Connectivity nodes are points where terminals of AC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

classes.name: ConnectivityNodeContainer
classes.documentation: A base class for all objects that may contain connectivity nodes or topological nodes.

classes.name: Curve
classes.documentation: A multi-purpose curve or functional relationship between an independent variable (X-axis) and dependent (Y-axis) variables.

attributes.name: curveStyle
attributes.documentation: The style or shape of the curve.

attributes.name: xMultiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for X-axis.

attributes.name: xUnit
attributes.documentation: The X-axis units of measure.

attributes.name: y1Multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for Y1-axis.

attributes.name: y1Unit
attributes.documentation: The Y1-axis units of measure.

attributes.name: y2Multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for Y2-axis.

attributes.name: y2Unit
attributes.documentation: The Y2-axis units of measure.

attributes.name: y3Multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for Y3-axis.

attributes.name: y3Unit
attributes.documentation: The Y3-axis units of measure.

classes.name: CurveData
classes.documentation: Multi-purpose data points for defining a curve.  The use of this generic class is discouraged if a more specific class can be used to specify the X and Y axis values along with their specific data types.

attributes.name: xvalue
attributes.documentation: The data value of the X-axis variable,  depending on the X-axis units.

attributes.name: y1value
attributes.documentation: The data value of the  first Y-axis variable, depending on the Y-axis units.

attributes.name: y2value
attributes.documentation: The data value of the second Y-axis variable (if present), depending on the Y-axis units.

attributes.name: y3value
attributes.documentation: The data value of the third Y-axis variable (if present), depending on the Y-axis units.

classes.name: CurveStyle
classes.documentation: Style or shape of curve.

literals.name: constantYValue
literals.documentation: The Y-axis values are assumed constant until the next curve point and prior to the first curve point.

literals.name: straightLineYValues
literals.documentation: The Y-axis values are assumed to be a straight line between values.  Also known as linear interpolation.

classes.name: Equipment
classes.documentation: The parts of a power system that are physical devices, electronic or mechanical.

attributes.name: aggregate
attributes.documentation:
The aggregate flag provides an alternative way of representing an aggregated (equivalent) element. It is applicable in cases when the dedicated classes for equivalent equipment do not have all of the attributes necessary to represent the required level of detail.  In case the flag is set to “true” the single instance of equipment represents multiple pieces of equipment that have been modelled together as an aggregate equivalent obtained by a network reduction procedure. Examples would be power transformers or synchronous machines operating in parallel modelled as a single aggregate power transformer or aggregate synchronous machine.  
The attribute is not used for EquivalentBranch, EquivalentShunt and EquivalentInjection.

attributes.name: inService
attributes.documentation: Specifies the availability of the equipment. True means the equipment is available for topology processing, which determines if the equipment is energized or not. False means that the equipment is treated by network applications as if it is not in the model.

attributes.name: networkAnalysisEnabled
attributes.documentation: The equipment is enabled to participate in network analysis.  If unspecified, the value is assumed to be true.

attributes.name: normallyInService
attributes.documentation: Specifies the availability of the equipment under normal operating conditions. True means the equipment is available for topology processing, which determines if the equipment is energized or not. False means that the equipment is treated by network applications as if it is not in the model.

classes.name: EquipmentContainer
classes.documentation: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containing equipment.

classes.name: Feeder
classes.documentation:
A collection of equipment for organizational purposes, used for grouping distribution resources.
The organization a feeder does not necessarily reflect connectivity or current operation state.

classes.name: GeographicalRegion
classes.documentation: A geographical region of a power system network model.

classes.name: IdentifiedObject
classes.documentation: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

attributes.name: aliasName
attributes.documentation:
The aliasName is free text human readable name of the object alternative to IdentifiedObject.name. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.
The attribute aliasName is retained because of backwards compatibility between CIM relases. It is however recommended to replace aliasName with the Name class as aliasName is planned for retirement at a future time.

attributes.name: description
attributes.documentation: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

attributes.name: mRID
attributes.documentation:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

attributes.name: name
attributes.documentation: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

classes.name: IrregularIntervalSchedule
classes.documentation: The schedule has time points where the time between them varies.

classes.name: IrregularTimePoint
classes.documentation: TimePoints for a schedule where the time between the points varies.

attributes.name: time
attributes.documentation: The time is relative to the schedule starting time.

attributes.name: value1
attributes.documentation: The first value at the time. The meaning of the value is defined by the derived type of the associated schedule.

attributes.name: value2
attributes.documentation: The second value at the time. The meaning of the value is defined by the derived type of the associated schedule.

classes.name: Name
classes.documentation: The Name class provides the means to define any number of human readable names for an object. A name is not to be used for defining inter-object relationships. For inter-object relationships instead use the object identification 'mRID'.

attributes.name: name
attributes.documentation: Any free text that name the object.

classes.name: NameType
classes.documentation:
Type of name. Possible values for attribute 'name' are implementation dependent but standard profiles may specify types. An enterprise may have multiple IT systems each having its own local name for the same object, e.g. a planning system may have different names from an EMS. An object may also have different names within the same IT system, e.g. localName as defined in CIM version 14. The definition from CIM14 is:
The localName is a human readable name of the object. It is a free text name local to a node in a naming hierarchy similar to a file directory structure. A power system related naming hierarchy may be: Substation, VoltageLevel, Equipment etc. Children of the same parent in such a hierarchy have names that typically are unique among them.

attributes.name: description
attributes.documentation: Description of the name type.

attributes.name: name
attributes.documentation: Name of the name type.

classes.name: NameTypeAuthority
classes.documentation: Authority responsible for creation and management of names of a given type; typically an organization or an enterprise system.

attributes.name: description
attributes.documentation: Description of the name type authority.

attributes.name: name
attributes.documentation: Name of the name type authority.

classes.name: OperatingParticipant
classes.documentation: An operator of multiple power system resource objects. Note multple operating participants may operate the same power system resource object.   This can be used for modeling jointly owned units where each owner operates as a contractual share.

classes.name: OperatingShare
classes.documentation: Specifies the operations contract relationship between a power system resource and a contract participant.

attributes.name: percentage
attributes.documentation: Percentage operational ownership between the pair (power system resource and operating participant) associated with this share. The total percentage ownership for a power system resource should add to 100%.

classes.name: PSRType
classes.documentation: Classifying instances of the same class, e.g. overhead and underground ACLineSegments. This classification mechanism is intended to provide flexibility outside the scope of this document, i.e. provide customisation that is non standard.

classes.name: PhaseCode
classes.documentation:
An unordered enumeration of phase identifiers.  Allows designation of phases for both transmission and distribution equipment, circuits and loads.   The enumeration, by itself, does not describe how the phases are connected together or connected to ground.  Ground is not explicitly denoted as a phase.
Residential and small commercial loads are often served from single-phase, or split-phase, secondary circuits. For the example of s12N, phases 1 and 2 refer to hot wires that are 180 degrees out of phase, while N refers to the neutral wire. Through single-phase transformer connections, these secondary circuits may be served from one or two of the primary phases A, B, and C. For three-phase loads, use the A, B, C phase codes instead of s12N.
The integer values are from IEC 61968-9 to support revenue metering applications.

literals.name: ABCN
literals.documentation: Phases A, B, C, and N.

literals.name: XYN
literals.documentation: Two unknown non-neutral phases plus neutral.

classes.name: PowerSystemResource
classes.documentation: A power system resource (PSR) can be an item of equipment such as a switch, an equipment container containing many individual items of equipment such as a substation, or an organisational entity such as sub-control area. Power system resources can have measurements associated.

classes.name: RegularIntervalSchedule
classes.documentation: The schedule has time points where the time between them is constant.

attributes.name: endTime
attributes.documentation: The time for the last time point.  The value can be a time of day, not a specific date.

attributes.name: timeStep
attributes.documentation: The time between each pair of subsequent regular time points in sequence order.

classes.name: RegularTimePoint
classes.documentation: Time point for a schedule where the time between the consecutive points is constant.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: The position of the regular time point in the sequence. Note that time points don't have to be sequential, i.e. time points may be omitted. The actual time for a RegularTimePoint is computed by multiplying the associated regular interval schedule's time step with the regular time point sequence number and adding the associated schedules start time. To specify values for the start time, use sequence number 0.  The sequence number cannot be negative.

attributes.name: value1
attributes.documentation: The first value at the time. The meaning of the value is defined by the derived type of the associated schedule.

attributes.name: value2
attributes.documentation: The second value at the time. The meaning of the value is defined by the derived type of the associated schedule.

classes.name: ReportingGroup
classes.documentation: A reporting group is used for various ad-hoc groupings used for reporting.

classes.name: ReportingSuperGroup
classes.documentation: A reporting super group, groups reporting groups for a higher level report.

classes.name: SubGeographicalRegion
classes.documentation: A subset of a geographical region of a power system network model.

classes.name: Substation
classes.documentation: A collection of equipment for purposes other than generation or utilization, through which electric energy in bulk is passed for the purposes of switching or modifying its characteristics.

classes.name: Terminal
classes.documentation: An AC electrical connection point to a piece of conducting equipment. Terminals are connected at physical connection points called connectivity nodes.

attributes.name: phases
attributes.documentation:
Represents the normal network phasing condition. If the attribute is missing, three phases (ABC) shall be assumed, except for terminals of grounding classes (specializations of EarthFaultCompensator, GroundDisconnector, and Ground) which will be assumed to be N. Therefore, phase code ABCN is explicitly declared when needed, e.g. for star point grounding equipment.
The phase code on terminals connecting same ConnectivityNode or same TopologicalNode as well as for equipment between two terminals shall be consistent.

classes.name: VoltageLevel
classes.documentation: A collection of equipment at one common system voltage forming a switchgear. The equipment typically consists of breakers, busbars, instrumentation, control, regulation and protection devices as well as assemblies of all these.

attributes.name: highVoltageLimit
attributes.documentation:
The bus bar's high voltage limit.
The limit applies to all equipment and nodes contained in a given VoltageLevel. It is not required that it is exchanged in pair with lowVoltageLimit. It is preferable to use operational VoltageLimit, which prevails, if present.

attributes.name: lowVoltageLimit
attributes.documentation:
The bus bar's low voltage limit.
The limit applies to all equipment and nodes contained in a given VoltageLevel. It is not required that it is exchanged in pair with highVoltageLimit. It is preferable to use operational VoltageLimit, which prevails, if present.

subPackages.name: Wires
subPackages.documentation: An extension to the Core and Topology package that models information on the electrical characteristics of Transmission and Distribution networks. This package is used by network applications such as State Estimation, Load Flow and Optimal Power Flow.

classes.name: AsynchronousMachineKind
classes.documentation: Kind of Asynchronous Machine.

literals.name: generator
literals.documentation: The Asynchronous Machine is a generator.

literals.name: motor
literals.documentation: The Asynchronous Machine is a motor.

classes.name: ACLineSegment
classes.documentation:
A wire or combination of wires, with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry alternating current between points in the power system.
For symmetrical, transposed three phase lines, it is sufficient to use attributes of the line segment, which describe impedances and admittances for the entire length of the segment.  Additionally impedances can be computed by using length and associated per length impedances.
The BaseVoltage at the two ends of ACLineSegments in a Line shall have the same BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage. However, boundary lines may have slightly different BaseVoltage.nominalVoltages and variation is allowed. Larger voltage difference in general requires use of an equivalent branch.

attributes.name: b0ch
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

attributes.name: bch
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.  This value represents the full charging over the full length of the line.

attributes.name: g0ch
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence shunt (charging) conductance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

attributes.name: gch
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) conductance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence series resistance of the entire line section.

attributes.name: r0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence series resistance of the entire line section.

attributes.name: shortCircuitEndTemperature
attributes.documentation: Maximum permitted temperature at the end of SC for the calculation of minimum short-circuit currents. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: x
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence series reactance of the entire line section.

attributes.name: x0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence series reactance of the entire line section.

classes.name: ACLineSegmentPhase
classes.documentation: Represents a single wire of an alternating current line segment.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.documentation: The phase connection of the wire at both ends.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: Number designation for this line segment phase. Each line segment phase within a line segment should have a unique sequence number. This is useful for unbalanced modelling to bind the mathematical model (PhaseImpedanceData of PerLengthPhaseImpedance) with the connectivity model (this class) and the physical model (WirePosition) without tight coupling.

classes.name: AsynchronousMachine
classes.documentation: A rotating machine whose shaft rotates asynchronously with the electrical field.  Also known as an induction machine with no external connection to the rotor windings, e.g. squirrel-cage induction machine.

attributes.name: asynchronousMachineType
attributes.documentation: Indicates the type of Asynchronous Machine (motor or generator).

attributes.name: converterFedDrive
attributes.documentation: Indicates whether the machine is a converter fed drive. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: efficiency
attributes.documentation: Efficiency of the asynchronous machine at nominal operation as a percentage. Indicator for converter drive motors. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: iaIrRatio
attributes.documentation: Ratio of locked-rotor current to the rated current of the motor (Ia/Ir). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: nominalFrequency
attributes.documentation: Nameplate data indicates if the machine is 50 Hz or 60 Hz.

attributes.name: nominalSpeed
attributes.documentation: Nameplate data.  Depends on the slip and number of pole pairs.

attributes.name: polePairNumber
attributes.documentation: Number of pole pairs of stator. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: ratedMechanicalPower
attributes.documentation: Rated mechanical power (Pr in IEC 60909-0). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: reversible
attributes.documentation: Indicates for converter drive motors if the power can be reversible. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: rr1
attributes.documentation: Damper 1 winding resistance.

attributes.name: rr2
attributes.documentation: Damper 2 winding resistance.

attributes.name: rxLockedRotorRatio
attributes.documentation: Locked rotor ratio (R/X). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: tpo
attributes.documentation: Transient rotor time constant (greater than tppo).

attributes.name: tppo
attributes.documentation: Sub-transient rotor time constant (greater than 0).

attributes.name: xlr1
attributes.documentation: Damper 1 winding leakage reactance.

attributes.name: xlr2
attributes.documentation: Damper 2 winding leakage reactance.

attributes.name: xm
attributes.documentation: Magnetizing reactance.

attributes.name: xp
attributes.documentation: Transient reactance (unsaturated) (greater than or equal to xpp).

attributes.name: xpp
attributes.documentation: Sub-transient reactance (unsaturated).

attributes.name: xs
attributes.documentation: Synchronous reactance (greater than xp).

classes.name: Breaker
classes.documentation: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal circuit conditions and also making, carrying for a specified time, and breaking currents under specified abnormal circuit conditions e.g.  those of short circuit.

attributes.name: inTransitTime
attributes.documentation: The transition time from open to close.

classes.name: BusbarSection
classes.documentation:
A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation. 
Voltage measurements are typically obtained from voltage transformers that are connected to busbar sections. A bus bar section may have many physical terminals but for analysis is modelled with exactly one logical terminal.

attributes.name: ipMax
attributes.documentation:
Maximum allowable peak short-circuit current of busbar (Ipmax in IEC 60909-0). 
Mechanical limit of the busbar in the substation itself. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

classes.name: Clamp
classes.documentation:
A Clamp is a galvanic connection at a line segment where other equipment is connected. A Clamp does not cut the line segment. 
A Clamp is ConductingEquipment and has one Terminal with an associated ConnectivityNode. Any other ConductingEquipment can be connected to the Clamp ConnectivityNode.

attributes.name: lengthFromTerminal1
attributes.documentation: The length to the place where the clamp is located starting from side one of the line segment, i.e. the line segment terminal with sequence number equal to 1.

classes.name: CompositeSwitch
classes.documentation:
A model of a set of individual Switches normally enclosed within the same cabinet and possibly with interlocks that restrict the combination of switch positions. These are typically found in medium voltage distribution networks. 
A CompositeSwitch could represent a Ring-Main-Unit (RMU), or pad-mounted switchgear, with primitive internal devices such as an internal bus-bar plus 3 or 4 internal switches each of which may individually be open or closed. A CompositeSwitch and a set of contained Switches can also be used to represent a multi-position switch e.g. a switch that can connect a circuit to Ground, Open or Busbar.

attributes.name: compositeSwitchType
attributes.documentation: An alphanumeric code that can be used as a reference to extra information such as the description of the interlocking scheme if any.

classes.name: Conductor
classes.documentation: Combination of conducting material with consistent electrical characteristics, building a single electrical system, used to carry current between points in the power system.

attributes.name: length
attributes.documentation: Segment length for calculating line section capabilities.

classes.name: Connector
classes.documentation: A conductor, or group of conductors, with negligible impedance, that serve to connect other conducting equipment within a single substation and are modelled with a single logical terminal.

classes.name: CoolantType
classes.documentation: Method of cooling a machine.

classes.name: Cut
classes.documentation:
A cut separates a line segment into two parts. The cut appears as a switch inserted between these two parts and connects them together. As the cut is normally open there is no galvanic connection between the two line segment parts. But it is possible to close the cut to get galvanic connection.
The cut terminals are oriented towards the line segment terminals with the same sequence number. Hence the cut terminal with sequence number equal to 1 is oriented to the line segment's terminal with sequence number equal to 1.
The cut terminals also act as connection points for jumpers and other equipment, e.g. a mobile generator. To enable this, connectivity nodes are placed at the cut terminals. Once the connectivity nodes are in place any conducting equipment can be connected at them.

attributes.name: lengthFromTerminal1
attributes.documentation: The length to the place where the cut is located starting from side one of the cut line segment, i.e. the line segment Terminal with sequenceNumber equal to 1.

classes.name: Disconnector
classes.documentation: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for changing the connections in a circuit, or for isolating a circuit or equipment from a source of power. It is required to open or close circuits when negligible current is broken or made.

classes.name: DisconnectingCircuitBreaker
classes.documentation: A circuit breaking device including disconnecting function, eliminating the need for separate disconnectors.

classes.name: EarthFaultCompensator
classes.documentation: A conducting equipment used to represent a connection to ground which is typically used to compensate earth faults.   An earth fault compensator device modelled with a single terminal implies a second terminal solidly connected to ground.  If two terminals are modelled, the ground is not assumed and normal connection rules apply.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation: Nominal resistance of device.

classes.name: EnergyConnection
classes.documentation: A connection of energy generation or consumption on the power system model.

classes.name: EnergyConsumer
classes.documentation:
Generic user of energy - a  point of consumption on the power system model.
EnergyConsumer.pfixed, .qfixed, .pfixedPct and .qfixedPct have meaning only if there is no LoadResponseCharacteristic associated with EnergyConsumer or if LoadResponseCharacteristic.exponentModel is set to False.

attributes.name: customerCount
attributes.documentation: Number of individual customers represented by this demand.

attributes.name: grounded
attributes.documentation: Used for Yn and Zn connections. True if the neutral is solidly grounded.

attributes.name: p
attributes.documentation:
Active power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage.
Starting value for a steady state solution.

attributes.name: pfixed
attributes.documentation: Active power of the load that is a fixed quantity and does not vary as load group value varies. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: pfixedPct
attributes.documentation: Fixed active power as a percentage of load group fixed active power. Used to represent the time-varying components.  Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: phaseConnection
attributes.documentation: The type of phase connection, such as wye or delta.

attributes.name: q
attributes.documentation:
Reactive power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage.
Starting value for a steady state solution.

attributes.name: qfixed
attributes.documentation: Reactive power of the load that is a fixed quantity and does not vary as load group value varies. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: qfixedPct
attributes.documentation: Fixed reactive power as a percentage of load group fixed reactive power. Used to represent the time-varying components.  Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

classes.name: EnergyConsumerPhase
classes.documentation: A single phase of an energy consumer.

attributes.name: p
attributes.documentation:
Active power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage.
Starting value for a steady state solution.

attributes.name: pfixed
attributes.documentation: Active power of the load that is a fixed quantity. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: pfixedPct
attributes.documentation: Fixed active power as per cent of load group fixed active power. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.documentation: Phase of this energy consumer component.   If the energy consumer is wye connected, the connection is from the indicated phase to the central ground or neutral point.  If the energy consumer is delta connected, the phase indicates an energy consumer connected from the indicated phase to the next logical non-neutral phase.

attributes.name: q
attributes.documentation:
Reactive power of the load. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
For voltage dependent loads the value is at rated voltage.
Starting value for a steady state solution.

attributes.name: qfixed
attributes.documentation: Reactive power of the load that is a fixed quantity. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: qfixedPct
attributes.documentation: Fixed reactive power as per cent of load group fixed reactive power. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

classes.name: EnergySchedulingType
classes.documentation: Used to define the type of generation for scheduling purposes.

classes.name: EnergySource
classes.documentation: A generic equivalent for an energy supplier on a transmission or distribution voltage level.

attributes.name: activePower
attributes.documentation:
High voltage source active injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: nominalVoltage
attributes.documentation: Phase-to-phase nominal voltage.

attributes.name: pMax
attributes.documentation: This is the maximum active power that can be produced by the source. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

attributes.name: pMin
attributes.documentation: This is the minimum active power that can be produced by the source. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a TopologicalNode (bus) into the conducting equipment.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence Thevenin resistance.

attributes.name: r0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence Thevenin resistance.

attributes.name: reactivePower
attributes.documentation:
High voltage source reactive injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: rn
attributes.documentation: Negative sequence Thevenin resistance.

attributes.name: voltageAngle
attributes.documentation: Phase angle of a-phase open circuit used when voltage characteristics need to be imposed at the node associated with the terminal of the energy source, such as when voltages and angles from the transmission level are used as input to the distribution network. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

attributes.name: voltageMagnitude
attributes.documentation: Phase-to-phase open circuit voltage magnitude used when voltage characteristics need to be imposed at the node associated with the terminal of the energy source, such as when voltages and angles from the transmission level are used as input to the distribution network. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

attributes.name: x
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence Thevenin reactance.

attributes.name: x0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence Thevenin reactance.

attributes.name: xn
attributes.documentation: Negative sequence Thevenin reactance.

classes.name: EnergySourcePhase
classes.documentation: Represents the single phase information of an unbalanced energy source.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.documentation: Phase of this energy source component.   If the energy source wye connected, the connection is from the indicated phase to the central ground or neutral point.  If the energy source is delta connected, the phase indicates an energy source connected from the indicated phase to the next logical non-neutral phase.

classes.name: ExternalNetworkInjection
classes.documentation: This class represents the external network and it is used for IEC 60909 calculations.

attributes.name: governorSCD
attributes.documentation: Power Frequency Bias. This is the change in power injection divided by the change in frequency and negated.  A positive value of the power frequency bias provides additional power injection upon a drop in frequency.

attributes.name: ikSecond
attributes.documentation: Indicates whether initial symmetrical short-circuit current and power have been calculated according to IEC (Ik").  Used only if short circuit calculations are done according to superposition method.

attributes.name: maxInitialSymShCCurrent
attributes.documentation: Maximum initial symmetrical short-circuit currents (Ik" max) in A (Ik" = Sk"/(SQRT(3) Un)). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: maxP
attributes.documentation: Maximum active power of the injection.

attributes.name: maxQ
attributes.documentation: Maximum reactive power limit. It is used for modelling of infeed for load flow exchange and not for short circuit modelling.

attributes.name: maxR0ToX0Ratio
attributes.documentation: Maximum ratio of zero sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its zero sequence reactance (R(0)/X(0) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: maxR1ToX1Ratio
attributes.documentation: Maximum ratio of positive sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its positive sequence reactance (R(1)/X(1) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: maxZ0ToZ1Ratio
attributes.documentation: Maximum ratio of zero sequence impedance to its positive sequence impedance (Z(0)/Z(1) max). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: minInitialSymShCCurrent
attributes.documentation: Minimum initial symmetrical short-circuit currents (Ik" min) in A (Ik" = Sk"/(SQRT(3) Un)). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: minP
attributes.documentation: Minimum active power of the injection.

attributes.name: minQ
attributes.documentation: Minimum reactive power limit. It is used for modelling of infeed for load flow exchange and not for short circuit modelling.

attributes.name: minR0ToX0Ratio
attributes.documentation: Indicates whether initial symmetrical short-circuit current and power have been calculated according to IEC (Ik"). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 6090.

attributes.name: minR1ToX1Ratio
attributes.documentation: Minimum ratio of positive sequence resistance of Network Feeder to its positive sequence reactance (R(1)/X(1) min). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: minZ0ToZ1Ratio
attributes.documentation: Minimum ratio of zero sequence impedance to its positive sequence impedance (Z(0)/Z(1) min). Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.

attributes.name: p
attributes.documentation:
Active power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: q
attributes.documentation:
Reactive power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: referencePriority
attributes.documentation: Priority of unit for use as powerflow voltage phase angle reference bus selection. 0 = don t care (default) 1 = highest priority. 2 is less than 1 and so on.

attributes.name: voltageFactor
attributes.documentation: Voltage factor in pu, which was used to calculate short-circuit current Ik" and power Sk".  Used only if short circuit calculations are done according to superposition method.

classes.name: FrequencyConverter
classes.documentation: A device to convert from one frequency to another (e.g., frequency F1 to F2) comprises a pair of FrequencyConverter instances. One converts from F1 to DC, the other converts the DC to F2.

attributes.name: frequency
attributes.documentation: Frequency on the AC side.

attributes.name: maxP
attributes.documentation: The maximum active power on the DC side at which the frequency converter should operate.

attributes.name: maxU
attributes.documentation: The maximum voltage on the DC side at which the frequency converter should operate.

attributes.name: minP
attributes.documentation: The minimum active power on the DC side at which the frequency converter should operate.

attributes.name: minU
attributes.documentation: The minimum voltage on the DC side at which the frequency converter should operate.

classes.name: Fuse
classes.documentation: An overcurrent protective device with a circuit opening fusible part that is heated and severed by the passage of overcurrent through it. A fuse is considered a switching device because it breaks current.

classes.name: Ground
classes.documentation: A point where the system is grounded used for connecting conducting equipment to ground. The power system model can have any number of grounds.

classes.name: GroundingImpedance
classes.documentation: A fixed impedance device used for grounding.

attributes.name: x
attributes.documentation: Reactance of device.

classes.name: GroundDisconnector
classes.documentation: A manually operated or motor operated mechanical switching device used for isolating a circuit or equipment from ground.

classes.name: Jumper
classes.documentation: A short section of conductor with negligible impedance which can be manually removed and replaced if the circuit is de-energized. Note that zero-impedance branches can potentially be modelled by other equipment types.

classes.name: Junction
classes.documentation: A point where one or more conducting equipments are connected with zero resistance.

classes.name: Line
classes.documentation: Contains equipment beyond a substation belonging to a power transmission line.

classes.name: LinearShuntCompensator
classes.documentation: A linear shunt compensator has banks or sections with equal admittance values.

attributes.name: b0PerSection
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence shunt (charging) susceptance per section.

attributes.name: bPerSection
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance per section.

attributes.name: g0PerSection

attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) conductance per section.

classes.name: LinearShuntCompensatorPhase
classes.documentation: A per phase linear shunt compensator has banks or sections with equal admittance values.

attributes.name: bPerSection

attributes.name: gPerSection
attributes.documentation: Conductance per section for this phase if shunt compensator is wye connected.  Conductance per section phase to phase if shunt compensator is delta connected.

classes.name: LoadBreakSwitch
classes.documentation: A mechanical switching device capable of making, carrying, and breaking currents under normal operating conditions.

classes.name: MutualCoupling
classes.documentation: This class represents the zero sequence line mutual coupling.

attributes.name: b0ch
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence mutual coupling shunt (charging) susceptance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

attributes.name: distance11
attributes.documentation: Distance to the start of the coupled region from the first line's terminal having sequence number equal to 1.

attributes.name: distance12
attributes.documentation: Distance to the end of the coupled region from the first line's terminal with sequence number equal to 1.

attributes.name: distance21
attributes.documentation: Distance to the start of coupled region from the second line's terminal with sequence number equal to 1.

attributes.name: distance22
attributes.documentation: Distance to the end of coupled region from the second line's terminal with sequence number equal to 1.

attributes.name: g0ch
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence mutual coupling shunt (charging) conductance, uniformly distributed, of the entire line section.

attributes.name: r0

attributes.name: x0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence branch-to-branch mutual impedance coupling, reactance.

The attributes g and b of the associated NonlinearShuntCompensatorPhasePoint describe the total conductance and admittance of a NonlinearShuntCompensatorPhasePoint at a section number specified by NonlinearShuntCompensatorPhasePoint.sectionNumber.

classes.name: NonlinearShuntCompensatorPhasePoint

attributes.name: b
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance per section.

attributes.name: g
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) conductance per section.

attributes.name: sectionNumber
attributes.documentation: The number of the section.

classes.name: NonlinearShuntCompensatorPoint
classes.documentation: A non linear shunt compensator bank or section admittance value. The number of NonlinearShuntCompenstorPoint instances associated with a NonlinearShuntCompensator shall be equal to ShuntCompensator.maximumSections. ShuntCompensator.sections shall only be set to one of the NonlinearShuntCompenstorPoint.sectionNumber. There is no interpolation between NonlinearShuntCompenstorPoint-s.

attributes.name: b
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance per section.

attributes.name: b0
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence shunt (charging) susceptance per section.

attributes.name: g
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) conductance per section.

classes.name: PerLengthLineParameter
classes.documentation: Common type for per-length electrical catalogues describing line parameters.

classes.name: PerLengthPhaseImpedance
classes.documentation: Impedance and admittance parameters per unit length for n-wire unbalanced lines, in matrix form.

attributes.name: conductorCount
attributes.documentation: Number of phase, neutral, and other wires retained. Constrains the number of matrix elements and the phase codes that can be used with this matrix.

attributes.name: b0ch
attributes.documentation: Zero sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, per unit of length.

attributes.name: bch
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt (charging) susceptance, per unit of length.

attributes.name: g0ch

classes.name: PetersenCoil
classes.documentation: A variable impedance device normally used to offset line charging during single line faults in an ungrounded section of network.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.documentation: The mode of operation of the Petersen coil.

attributes.name: nominalU
attributes.documentation: The nominal voltage for which the coil is designed.

attributes.name: offsetCurrent
attributes.documentation: The offset current that the Petersen coil controller is operating from the resonant point.  This is normally a fixed amount for which the controller is configured and could be positive or negative.  Typically 0 to 60 A depending on voltage and resonance conditions.

attributes.name: positionCurrent
attributes.documentation: The control current used to control the Petersen coil also known as the position current.  Typically in the range of 20 mA to 200 mA.

attributes.name: xGroundMax

attributes.name: xGroundMin

classes.name: PetersenCoilModeKind

The matrix can also be stored in symmetric lower triangular format using the row and column attributes, which map to ACLineSegmentPhase.sequenceNumber.

attributes.name: toPhase
attributes.documentation: Refer to the class description.

literals.name: Yn

literals.name: G

classes.name: PhaseTapChanger
