attributes.name: coldLegFBLeadTC2
attributes.documentation: Cold leg feedback lead time constant.

attributes.name: coldLegFG1
attributes.documentation: Cold leg feedback gain 1.

attributes.name: coldLegFG2
attributes.documentation: Cold leg feedback gain 2.

attributes.name: coldLegLagTC
attributes.documentation: Cold leg lag time constant.

attributes.name: coreHTLagTC1
attributes.documentation: Core heat transfer lag time constant.

attributes.name: coreHTLagTC2
attributes.documentation: Core heat transfer lag time constant.

attributes.name: coreNeutronicsEffTC
attributes.documentation: Core neutronics effective time constant.

attributes.name: coreNeutronicsHT
attributes.documentation: Core neutronics and heat transfer.

attributes.name: feedbackFactor
attributes.documentation: Feedback factor.

attributes.name: hotLegLagTC
attributes.documentation: Hot leg lag time constant.

attributes.name: hotLegSteamGain
attributes.documentation: Hot leg steam gain.

attributes.name: hotLegToColdLegGain
attributes.documentation: Hot leg to cold leg gain.

attributes.name: pressureCG
attributes.documentation: Pressure control gain.

attributes.name: steamFlowFG
attributes.documentation: Steam flow feedback gain.

attributes.name: steamPressureDropLagTC
attributes.documentation: Steam pressure drop lag time constant.

attributes.name: steamPressureFG
attributes.documentation: Steam pressure feedback gain.

attributes.name: throttlePressureFactor
attributes.documentation: Throttle pressure factor.

attributes.name: throttlePressureSP
attributes.documentation: Throttle pressure setpoint.

classes.name: PrimeMover
classes.documentation: The machine used to develop mechanical energy used to drive a generator.

attributes.name: primeMoverRating
attributes.documentation: Rating of prime mover.

classes.name: SteamSupply
classes.documentation: Steam supply for steam turbine.

attributes.name: steamSupplyRating
attributes.documentation: Rating of steam supply.

classes.name: SteamTurbine
classes.documentation: Steam turbine.

attributes.name: crossoverTC
attributes.documentation: Crossover time constant.

attributes.name: reheater1TC
attributes.documentation: First reheater time constant.

attributes.name: reheater2TC
attributes.documentation: Second reheater time constant.

attributes.name: shaft1PowerHP
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 1 high pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft1PowerIP
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 1 intermediate pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft1PowerLP1
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 1 first low pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft1PowerLP2
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 1 second low pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft2PowerHP
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 2 high pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft2PowerIP
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 2 intermediate pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft2PowerLP1
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 2 first low pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: shaft2PowerLP2
attributes.documentation: Fraction of power from shaft 2 second low pressure turbine output.

attributes.name: steamChestTC
attributes.documentation: Steam chest time constant.

classes.name: Subcritical
classes.documentation: Once-through subcritical boiler.

classes.name: Supercritical
classes.documentation: Once-through supercritical boiler.

classes.name: HydroTurbineKind
classes.documentation: Type of turbine.

subPackages.name: Production
subPackages.documentation: The production package is responsible for classes which describe various kinds of generators. These classes also provide production costing information which is used to economically allocate demand among committed units and calculate reserve quantities.

classes.name: AirCompressor
classes.documentation: Combustion turbine air compressor which is an integral part of a compressed air energy storage (CAES) plant.

attributes.name: airCompressorRating
attributes.documentation: Rating of the CAES air compressor.

classes.name: BatteryStateKind
classes.documentation: The state of the battery unit.

literals.name: full
literals.documentation: Unable to charge, and not discharging.

literals.name: waiting
literals.documentation: Neither charging nor discharging, but able to do so.

literals.name: empty
literals.documentation: Unable to discharge, and not charging.

classes.name: BatteryUnit
classes.documentation: An electrochemical energy storage device.

attributes.name: batteryState
attributes.documentation: The current state of the battery (charging, full, etc.).

attributes.name: ratedE
attributes.documentation: Full energy storage capacity of the battery. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: storedE
attributes.documentation: Amount of energy currently stored. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero and lower than BatteryUnit.ratedE.

classes.name: CAESPlant
classes.documentation: Compressed air energy storage plant.

attributes.name: energyStorageCapacity
attributes.documentation: The rated energy storage capacity. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: ratedCapacityP
attributes.documentation: The CAES plant's gross rated generating capacity. The attribute shall be a positive value.

classes.name: CogenerationPlant
classes.documentation: A set of thermal generating units for the production of electrical energy and process steam (usually from the output of the steam turbines). The steam sendout is typically used for industrial purposes or for municipal heating and cooling.

attributes.name: cogenHPSendoutRating
attributes.documentation: The high pressure steam sendout.

attributes.name: cogenHPSteamRating
attributes.documentation: The high pressure steam rating.

attributes.name: cogenLPSendoutRating
attributes.documentation: The low pressure steam sendout.

attributes.name: cogenLPSteamRating
attributes.documentation: The low pressure steam rating.

attributes.name: ratedP
attributes.documentation:
The rated output active power of the cogeneration plant.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

classes.name: CombinedCyclePlant
classes.documentation: A set of combustion turbines and steam turbines where the exhaust heat from the combustion turbines is recovered to make steam for the steam turbines, resulting in greater overall plant efficiency.

attributes.name: combCyclePlantRating
attributes.documentation: The combined cycle plant's active power output rating.

classes.name: EmissionAccount
classes.documentation: Accounts for tracking emissions usage and credits for thermal generating units. A unit may have zero or more emission accounts, and will typically have one for tracking usage and one for tracking credits.

attributes.name: emissionType
attributes.documentation: The type of emission, for example sulfur dioxide (SO2). The y1AxisUnits of the curve contains the unit of measure (e.g. kg) and the emissionType is the type of emission (e.g. sulfur dioxide).

attributes.name: emissionValueSource
attributes.documentation: The source of the emission value.

classes.name: EmissionCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between the unit's emission rate in units of mass per hour (Y-axis) and output active power (X-axis) for a given type of emission. This curve applies when only one type of fuel is being burned.

attributes.name: emissionContent
attributes.documentation: The emission content per quantity of fuel burned.

attributes.name: emissionType
attributes.documentation: The type of emission, which also gives the production rate measurement unit. The y1AxisUnits of the curve contains the unit of measure (e.g. kg) and the emissionType is the type of emission (e.g. sulfur dioxide).

attributes.name: isNetGrossP
attributes.documentation: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

classes.name: EmissionType
classes.documentation: The type of emission.

classes.name: WindGenUnitKind
classes.documentation: Kind of wind generating unit.

literals.name: offshore
literals.documentation: The wind generating unit is located offshore.

literals.name: onshore
literals.documentation: The wind generating unit is located onshore.

classes.name: EmissionValueSource
classes.documentation: The source of the emission value.

classes.name: FossilFuel
classes.documentation: The fossil fuel consumed by the non-nuclear thermal generating unit.   For example, coal, oil, gas, etc.   These are the specific fuels that the generating unit can consume.

attributes.name: fossilFuelType
attributes.documentation: The type of fossil fuel, such as coal, oil, or gas.

attributes.name: fuelCost
attributes.documentation: The cost in terms of heat value for the given type of fuel.

attributes.name: fuelDispatchCost
attributes.documentation: The cost of fuel used for economic dispatching which includes: fuel cost, transportation cost,  and incremental maintenance cost.

attributes.name: fuelEffFactor
attributes.documentation: The efficiency factor for the fuel (per unit) in terms of the effective energy absorbed.

attributes.name: fuelHandlingCost
attributes.documentation: Handling and processing cost associated with this fuel.

attributes.name: fuelHeatContent
attributes.documentation: The amount of heat per weight (or volume) of the given type of fuel.

attributes.name: fuelMixture
attributes.documentation: Relative amount of the given type of fuel, when multiple fuels are being consumed.

attributes.name: fuelSulfur
attributes.documentation: The fuel's fraction of pollution credit per unit of heat content.

attributes.name: highBreakpointP
attributes.documentation: The active power output level of the unit at which the given type of fuel is switched on. This fuel (e.g., oil) is sometimes used to supplement the base fuel (e.g., coal) at high active power output levels.

attributes.name: lowBreakpointP
attributes.documentation: The active power output level of the unit at which the given type of fuel is switched off. This fuel (e.g., oil) is sometimes used to stabilize the base fuel (e.g., coal) at low active power output levels.

classes.name: FuelAllocationSchedule
classes.documentation: The amount of fuel of a given type which is allocated for consumption over a specified period of time.

attributes.name: fuelAllocationEndDate
attributes.documentation: The end time and date of the fuel allocation schedule.

attributes.name: fuelAllocationStartDate
attributes.documentation: The start time and date of the fuel allocation schedule.

attributes.name: fuelType
attributes.documentation: The type of fuel, which also indicates the corresponding measurement unit.

attributes.name: maxFuelAllocation
attributes.documentation: The maximum amount of fuel that is allocated for consumption for the scheduled time period.

attributes.name: minFuelAllocation
attributes.documentation: The minimum amount of fuel that is allocated for consumption for the scheduled time period, e.g., based on a "take-or-pay" contract.

classes.name: FuelType
classes.documentation: Type of fuel.

literals.name: coal
literals.documentation: Generic coal, not including lignite type.

literals.name: lignite
literals.documentation: The fuel is lignite coal.  Note that this is a special type of coal, so the other enum of coal is reserved for hard coal types or if the exact type of coal is not known.

literals.name: other
literals.documentation: Any fuel type not included in the rest of the enumerated value.

classes.name: GenUnitOpCostCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between unit operating cost (Y-axis) and unit output active power (X-axis). The operating cost curve for thermal units is derived from heat input and fuel costs. The operating cost curve for hydro units is derived from water flow rates and equivalent water costs.

attributes.name: isNetGrossP
attributes.documentation: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

classes.name: GenUnitOpSchedule
classes.documentation: The generating unit's Operator-approved current operating schedule (or plan), typically produced with the aid of unit commitment type analyses. The X-axis represents absolute time. The Y1-axis represents the status (0=off-line and unavailable: 1=available: 2=must run: 3=must run at fixed power value: etc.). The Y2-axis represents the must run fixed power value where required.

classes.name: GeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A single or set of synchronous machines for converting mechanical power into alternating-current power. For example, individual machines within a set may be defined for scheduling purposes while a single control signal is derived for the set. In this case there would be a GeneratingUnit for each member of the set and an additional GeneratingUnit corresponding to the set.

attributes.name: allocSpinResP
attributes.documentation: The planned unused capacity (spinning reserve) which can be used to support emergency load.

attributes.name: autoCntrlMarginP
attributes.documentation: The planned unused capacity which can be used to support automatic control overruns.

attributes.name: baseP
attributes.documentation: For dispatchable units, this value represents the economic active power basepoint, for units that are not dispatchable, this value represents the fixed generation value. The value shall be between the operating low and high limits.

attributes.name: controlDeadband
attributes.documentation: Unit control error deadband. When a unit's desired active power change is less than this deadband, then no control pulses will be sent to the unit.

attributes.name: controlPulseHigh
attributes.documentation: Pulse high limit which is the largest control pulse that the unit can respond to.

attributes.name: controlPulseLow
attributes.documentation: Pulse low limit which is the smallest control pulse that the unit can respond to.

attributes.name: controlResponseRate
attributes.documentation: Unit response rate which specifies the active power change for a control pulse of one second in the most responsive loading level of the unit.

attributes.name: efficiency
attributes.documentation: The efficiency of the unit in converting mechanical energy, from the prime mover, into electrical energy.

attributes.name: genControlMode
attributes.documentation: The unit control mode.

attributes.name: genControlSource
attributes.documentation: The source of controls for a generating unit.  Defines the control status of the generating unit.

attributes.name: governorMPL
attributes.documentation: Governor motor position limit.

attributes.name: governorSCD
attributes.documentation: Governor Speed Changer Droop.   This is the change in generator power output divided by the change in frequency normalized by the nominal power of the generator and the nominal frequency and expressed in percent and negated. A positive value of speed change droop provides additional generator output upon a drop in frequency.

attributes.name: highControlLimit
attributes.documentation: High limit for secondary (AGC) control.

attributes.name: initialP
attributes.documentation: Default initial active power  which is used to store a powerflow result for the initial active power for this unit in this network configuration.

attributes.name: longPF
attributes.documentation: Generating unit long term economic participation factor.

attributes.name: lowControlLimit
attributes.documentation: Low limit for secondary (AGC) control.

attributes.name: lowerRampRate
attributes.documentation: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be lowered by control actions.

attributes.name: maxEconomicP
attributes.documentation: Maximum high economic active power limit, that should not exceed the maximum operating active power limit.

attributes.name: maximumAllowableSpinningReserve
attributes.documentation: Maximum allowable spinning reserve. Spinning reserve will never be considered greater than this value regardless of the current operating point.

attributes.name: maxOperatingP
attributes.documentation: This is the maximum operating active power limit the dispatcher can enter for this unit.

attributes.name: minEconomicP
attributes.documentation: Low economic active power limit that shall be greater than or equal to the minimum operating active power limit.

attributes.name: minimumOffTime
attributes.documentation: Minimum time interval between unit shutdown and startup.

attributes.name: minOperatingP
attributes.documentation: This is the minimum operating active power limit the dispatcher can enter for this unit.

attributes.name: modelDetail
attributes.documentation: Detail level of the generator model data.

attributes.name: nominalP
attributes.documentation:
The nominal power of the generating unit.  Used to give precise meaning to percentage based attributes such as the governor speed change droop (governorSCD attribute).
The attribute shall be a positive value equal to or less than RotatingMachine.ratedS.

attributes.name: normalPF
attributes.documentation: Generating unit economic participation factor.  The sum of the participation factors across generating units does not have to sum to one.  It is used for representing distributed slack participation factor. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

attributes.name: penaltyFactor
attributes.documentation: Defined as: 1 / ( 1 - Incremental Transmission Loss); with the Incremental Transmission Loss expressed as a plus or minus value. The typical range of penalty factors is (0.9 to 1.1).

attributes.name: raiseRampRate
attributes.documentation: The normal maximum rate the generating unit active power output can be raised by control actions.

attributes.name: ratedGrossMaxP
attributes.documentation:
The unit's gross rated maximum capacity (book value).
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: ratedGrossMinP
attributes.documentation:
The gross rated minimum generation level which the unit can safely operate at while delivering power to the transmission grid.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: ratedNetMaxP
attributes.documentation:
The net rated maximum capacity determined by subtracting the auxiliary power used to operate the internal plant machinery from the rated gross maximum capacity.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: shortPF
attributes.documentation: Generating unit short term economic participation factor.

attributes.name: startupCost
attributes.documentation: The initial startup cost incurred for each start of the GeneratingUnit.

attributes.name: startupTime
attributes.documentation: Time it takes to get the unit on-line, from the time that the prime mover mechanical power is applied.

attributes.name: tieLinePF
attributes.documentation: Generating unit economic participation factor.

attributes.name: totalEfficiency
attributes.documentation: The efficiency of the unit in converting the fuel into electrical energy.

attributes.name: variableCost
attributes.documentation: The variable cost component of production per unit of ActivePower.

classes.name: GeneratorControlMode
classes.documentation: Unit control modes.

classes.name: GeneratorControlSource
classes.documentation: The source of controls for a generating unit.

classes.name: GrossToNetActivePowerCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between the generating unit's gross active power output on the X-axis (measured at the terminals of the machine(s)) and the generating unit's net active power output on the Y-axis (based on utility-defined measurements at the power station). Station service loads, when modelled, should be treated as non-conforming bus loads. There may be more than one curve, depending on the auxiliary equipment that is in service.

classes.name: HeatInputCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between unit heat input in energy per time for main fuel (Y1-axis) and supplemental fuel (Y2-axis) versus unit output in active power (X-axis). The quantity of main fuel used to sustain generation at this output level is prorated for throttling between definition points. The quantity of supplemental fuel used at this output level is fixed and not prorated.

attributes.name: auxPowerMult
attributes.documentation: Power output - auxiliary power multiplier adjustment factor.

attributes.name: auxPowerOffset
attributes.documentation: Power output - auxiliary power offset adjustment factor.

attributes.name: heatInputEff
attributes.documentation: Heat input - efficiency multiplier adjustment factor.

attributes.name: heatInputOffset
attributes.documentation: Heat input - offset adjustment factor.

attributes.name: isNetGrossP
attributes.documentation: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

classes.name: HeatRateCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between unit heat rate per active power (Y-axis) and  unit output (X-axis). The heat input is from all fuels.

attributes.name: isNetGrossP
attributes.documentation: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

classes.name: HydroEnergyConversionKind
classes.documentation: Specifies the capability of the hydro generating unit to convert energy as a generator or pump.

literals.name: generator
literals.documentation: Able to generate power, but not able to pump water for energy storage.

literals.name: pumpAndGenerator
literals.documentation: Able to both generate power and pump water for energy storage.

classes.name: HydroGeneratingEfficiencyCurve
classes.documentation:
Relationship between unit efficiency as percentage and unit output active power for a given net head in meters. The relationship between efficiency, discharge, head, and power output is expressed as follows:   E =KP/HQ
where:  E is the efficiency, as a percentage; P is the active power; H is the height; Q is the discharge, volume/time unit; K is a constant.
For example, a curve instance for a given net head could show efficiency (Y-axis) versus active power output (X-axis) or versus discharge on the X-axis.

classes.name: HydroGeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A generating unit whose prime mover is a hydraulic turbine (e.g., Francis, Pelton, Kaplan).

attributes.name: dropHeight
attributes.documentation: The height water drops from the reservoir mid-point to the turbine.

attributes.name: energyConversionCapability
attributes.documentation: Energy conversion capability for generating.

attributes.name: hydroUnitWaterCost
attributes.documentation: The equivalent cost of water that drives the hydro turbine.

attributes.name: turbineType
attributes.documentation: Type of turbine.

classes.name: HydroPlantStorageKind
classes.documentation: The type of hydro power plant.

classes.name: HydroPowerPlant
classes.documentation: A hydro power station which can generate or pump. When generating, the generator turbines receive water from an upper reservoir. When pumping, the pumps receive their water from a lower reservoir.

attributes.name: dischargeTravelDelay
attributes.documentation: Water travel delay from tailbay to next downstream hydro power station.

attributes.name: genRatedP
attributes.documentation:
The hydro plant's generating rating active power for rated head conditions.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: hydroPlantStorageType
attributes.documentation: The type of hydro power plant water storage.

attributes.name: penstockType
attributes.documentation: Type and configuration of hydro plant penstock(s).

attributes.name: plantDischargeCapacity
attributes.documentation: Total plant discharge capacity.

attributes.name: plantRatedHead
attributes.documentation:
The plant's rated gross head.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: pumpRatedP
attributes.documentation:
The hydro plant's pumping rating active power for rated head conditions.
The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: surgeTankCode
attributes.documentation: A code describing the type (or absence) of surge tank that is associated with the hydro power plant.

attributes.name: surgeTankCrestLevel
attributes.documentation: The level at which the surge tank spills.

classes.name: HydroPump
classes.documentation: A synchronous motor-driven pump, typically associated with a pumped storage plant.

attributes.name: pumpDischAtMaxHead
attributes.documentation: The pumping discharge under maximum head conditions, usually at full gate.

attributes.name: pumpDischAtMinHead
attributes.documentation: The pumping discharge under minimum head conditions, usually at full gate.

attributes.name: pumpPowerAtMaxHead
attributes.documentation: The pumping power under maximum head conditions, usually at full gate.

attributes.name: pumpPowerAtMinHead
attributes.documentation: The pumping power under minimum head conditions, usually at full gate.

classes.name: HydroPumpOpSchedule
classes.documentation: The hydro pump's Operator-approved current operating schedule (or plan), typically produced with the aid of unit commitment type analyses. The unit's operating schedule status is typically given as: (0=unavailable) (1=available to startup or shutdown)  (2=must pump).

classes.name: IncrementalHeatRateCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between unit incremental heat rate in (delta energy/time) per (delta active power) and unit output in active power. The IHR curve represents the slope of the HeatInputCurve. Note that the "incremental heat rate" and the "heat rate" have the same engineering units.

attributes.name: isNetGrossP
attributes.documentation: Flag is set to true when output is expressed in net active power.

classes.name: InflowForecast
classes.documentation: Natural water inflow to a reservoir, usually forecasted from predicted rain and snowmelt. Typically in one hour increments for up to 10 days. The forecast is given in average cubic meters per second over the time increment.

classes.name: LevelVsVolumeCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between reservoir volume and reservoir level. The  volume is at the Y-axis and the reservoir level at the X-axis.

classes.name: NuclearGeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A nuclear generating unit.

classes.name: PenstockLossCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between penstock head loss (in meters) and  total discharge through the penstock (in cubic meters per second). One or more turbines may be connected to the same penstock.

classes.name: PhotoVoltaicUnit
classes.documentation: A photovoltaic device or an aggregation of such devices.

classes.name: PowerElectronicsUnit
classes.documentation: A generating unit or battery or aggregation that connects to the AC network using power electronics rather than rotating machines.

attributes.name: maxP
attributes.documentation: Maximum active power limit. This is the maximum (nameplate) limit for the unit.

attributes.name: minP
attributes.documentation: Minimum active power limit. This is the minimum (nameplate) limit for the unit.

classes.name: PowerElectronicsWindUnit
classes.documentation: A wind generating unit that connects to the AC network with power electronics rather than rotating machines or an aggregation of such units.

classes.name: Reservoir
classes.documentation: A water storage facility within a hydro system, including: ponds, lakes, lagoons, and rivers. The storage is usually behind some type of dam.

attributes.name: activeStorageCapacity
attributes.documentation: Storage volume between the full supply level and the normal minimum operating level.

attributes.name: energyStorageRating
attributes.documentation: The reservoir's energy storage rating in energy for given head conditions.

attributes.name: fullSupplyLevel
attributes.documentation: Full supply level, above which water will spill. This can be the spillway crest level or the top of closed gates.

attributes.name: grossCapacity
attributes.documentation: Total capacity of reservoir.

attributes.name: normalMinOperateLevel
attributes.documentation: Normal minimum operating level below which the penstocks will draw air.

attributes.name: riverOutletWorks
attributes.documentation: River outlet works for riparian right releases or other purposes.

attributes.name: spillTravelDelay
attributes.documentation: The spillway water travel delay to the next downstream reservoir.

attributes.name: spillwayCapacity
attributes.documentation: The flow capacity of the spillway in cubic meters per second.

attributes.name: spillwayCrestLength
attributes.documentation: The length of the spillway crest.

attributes.name: spillwayCrestLevel
attributes.documentation: Spillway crest level above which water will spill.

attributes.name: spillWayGateType
attributes.documentation: Type of spillway gate, including parameters.

classes.name: ShutdownCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between the rate in gross active power/minute (Y-axis) at which a unit should be shutdown and its present gross MW output (X-axis).

attributes.name: shutdownCost
attributes.documentation: Fixed shutdown cost.

attributes.name: shutdownDate
attributes.documentation: The date and time of the most recent generating unit shutdown.

classes.name: SolarGeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A solar thermal generating unit, connected to the grid by means of a rotating machine.  This class does not represent photovoltaic (PV) generation.

classes.name: StartIgnFuelCurve
classes.documentation: The quantity of ignition fuel (Y-axis) used to restart and repay the auxiliary power consumed versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

attributes.name: ignitionFuelType
attributes.documentation: Type of ignition fuel.

classes.name: StartMainFuelCurve
classes.documentation: The quantity of main fuel (Y-axis) used to restart and repay the auxiliary power consumed versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

attributes.name: mainFuelType
attributes.documentation: Type of main fuel.

classes.name: StartRampCurve
classes.documentation: Rate in gross active power per minute (Y-axis) at which a unit can be loaded versus the number of hours (X-axis) the unit was off line.

attributes.name: hotStandbyRamp
attributes.documentation: The startup ramp rate in gross for a unit that is on hot standby.

classes.name: StartupModel
classes.documentation: Unit start up characteristics depending on how long the unit has been off line.

attributes.name: fixedMaintCost
attributes.documentation: Fixed maintenance cost.

attributes.name: hotStandbyHeat
attributes.documentation: The amount of heat input per time unit required for hot standby operation.

attributes.name: incrementalMaintCost
attributes.documentation: Incremental maintenance cost.

attributes.name: minimumDownTime
attributes.documentation: The minimum number of hours the unit must be down before restart.

attributes.name: minimumRunTime
attributes.documentation: The minimum number of hours the unit must be operating before being allowed to shut down.

attributes.name: riskFactorCost
attributes.documentation: The opportunity cost associated with the return in monetary unit. This represents the restart's "share" of the unit depreciation and risk of an event which would damage the unit.

attributes.name: startupCost
attributes.documentation: Total miscellaneous start up costs.

attributes.name: startupDate
attributes.documentation: The date and time of the most recent generating unit startup.

attributes.name: startupPriority
attributes.documentation: Startup priority within control area where lower numbers indicate higher priorities.  More than one unit in an area may be assigned the same priority.

attributes.name: stbyAuxP
attributes.documentation: The unit's auxiliary active power consumption to maintain standby mode.

classes.name: SteamSendoutSchedule
classes.documentation: The cogeneration plant's steam sendout schedule in volume per time unit.

classes.name: TailbayLossCurve
classes.documentation: Relationship between tailbay head loss height (Y-axis) and the total discharge into the power station's tailbay volume per time unit (X-axis) . There could be more than one curve depending on the level of the tailbay reservoir or river level.

classes.name: TargetLevelSchedule
classes.documentation: Reservoir water level targets from advanced studies or "rule curves". Typically in one hour increments for up to 10 days.

attributes.name: highLevelLimit
attributes.documentation: High target level limit, above which the reservoir operation will be penalized.

attributes.name: lowLevelLimit
attributes.documentation: Low target level limit, below which the reservoir operation will be penalized.

classes.name: ThermalGeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A generating unit whose prime mover could be a steam turbine, combustion turbine, or diesel engine.

attributes.name: oMCost
attributes.documentation: Operating and maintenance cost for the thermal unit.

classes.name: WindGeneratingUnit
classes.documentation: A wind driven generating unit, connected to the grid by means of a rotating machine.  May be used to represent a single turbine or an aggregation.

attributes.name: windGenUnitType
attributes.documentation: The kind of wind generating unit.

subPackages.name: DC
subPackages.documentation: This package contains model for direct current equipment and controls.

classes.name: ACDCConverter
classes.documentation: A unit with valves for three phases, together with unit control equipment, essential protective and switching devices, DC storage capacitors, phase reactors and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

attributes.name: baseS
attributes.documentation: Base apparent power of the converter pole. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: idc
attributes.documentation: Converter DC current, also called Id. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow.

attributes.name: idleLoss
attributes.documentation: Active power loss in pole at no power transfer. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: maxP
attributes.documentation: Maximum active power limit. The value is overwritten by values of VsCapabilityCurve, if present.

attributes.name: maxUdc
attributes.documentation: The maximum voltage on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: minP
attributes.documentation: Minimum active power limit. The value is overwritten by values of VsCapabilityCurve, if present.

attributes.name: minUdc
attributes.documentation: The minimum voltage on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: numberOfValves
attributes.documentation: Number of valves in the converter. Used in loss calculations.

attributes.name: p
attributes.documentation:
Active power at the point of common coupling. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for a steady state solution in the case a simplified power flow model is used.

attributes.name: poleLossP
attributes.documentation:
The active power loss at a DC Pole 
= idleLoss + switchingLoss*|Idc| + resitiveLoss*Idc^2.
For lossless operation Pdc=Pac.
For rectifier operation with losses Pdc=Pac-lossP.
For inverter operation with losses Pdc=Pac+lossP.
It is converter’s state variable used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: q
attributes.documentation:
Reactive power at the point of common coupling. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for a steady state solution in the case a simplified power flow model is used.

attributes.name: ratedUdc
attributes.documentation: Rated converter DC voltage, also called UdN. The attribute shall be a positive value. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. For instance a bipolar HVDC link with value  200 kV has a 400kV difference between the dc lines.

attributes.name: resistiveLoss
attributes.documentation: It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. Refer to poleLossP. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: switchingLoss
attributes.documentation: Switching losses, relative to the base apparent power 'baseS'. Refer to poleLossP. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetPpcc
attributes.documentation: Real power injection target in AC grid, at point of common coupling.  Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: targetUdc
attributes.documentation: Target value for DC voltage magnitude. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: uc
attributes.documentation: Line-to-line converter voltage, the voltage at the AC side of the valve. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: udc
attributes.documentation: Converter voltage at the DC side, also called Ud. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: valveU0
attributes.documentation: Valve threshold voltage, also called Uvalve. Forward voltage drop when the valve is conducting. Used in loss calculations, i.e. the switchLoss depend on numberOfValves * valveU0.

classes.name: ACDCConverterDCTerminal
classes.documentation: A DC electrical connection point at the AC/DC converter. The AC/DC converter is electrically connected also to the AC side. The AC connection is inherited from the AC conducting equipment in the same way as any other AC equipment. The AC/DC converter DC terminal is separate from generic DC terminal to restrict the connection with the AC side to AC/DC converter and so that no other DC conducting equipment can be connected to the AC side.

attributes.name: polarity
attributes.documentation:
Represents the normal network polarity condition. Depending on the converter configuration the value shall be set as follows:
- For a monopole with two converter terminals use DCPolarityKind “positive” and “negative”.
- For a bi-pole or symmetric monopole with three converter terminals use DCPolarityKind “positive”, “middle” and “negative”.

classes.name: CsConverter
classes.documentation:
DC side of the current source converter (CSC).
The firing angle controls the dc voltage at the converter, both for rectifier and inverter. The difference between the dc voltages of the rectifier and inverter determines the dc current. The extinction angle is used to limit the dc voltage at the inverter, if needed, and is not used in active power control. The firing angle, transformer tap position and number of connected filters are the primary means to control a current source dc line. Higher level controls are built on top, e.g. dc voltage, dc current and active power. From a steady state perspective it is sufficient to specify the wanted active power transfer (ACDCConverter.targetPpcc) and the control functions will set the dc voltage, dc current, firing angle, transformer tap position and number of connected filters to meet this. Therefore attributes targetAlpha and targetGamma are not applicable in this case.
The reactive power consumed by the converter is a function of the firing angle, transformer tap position and number of connected filter, which can be approximated with half of the active power. The losses is a function of the dc voltage and dc current.
The attributes minAlpha and maxAlpha define the range of firing angles for rectifier operation between which no discrete tap changer action takes place. The range is typically 10-18 degrees.
The attributes minGamma and maxGamma define the range of extinction angles for inverter operation between which no discrete tap changer action takes place. The range is typically 17-20 degrees.

attributes.name: alpha
attributes.documentation: Firing angle that determines the dc voltage at the converter dc terminal. Typical value between 10 degrees and 18 degrees for a rectifier. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: gamma
attributes.documentation: Extinction angle. It is used to limit the dc voltage at the inverter if needed. Typical value between 17 degrees and 20 degrees for an inverter. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: maxAlpha
attributes.documentation: Maximum firing angle. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: maxGamma
attributes.documentation: Maximum extinction angle. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: maxIdc
attributes.documentation: The maximum direct current (Id) on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data use in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: minAlpha
attributes.documentation: Minimum firing angle. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: minGamma
attributes.documentation: Minimum extinction angle. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: minIdc
attributes.documentation: The minimum direct current (Id) on the DC side at which the converter should operate. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: operatingMode
attributes.documentation: Indicates whether the DC pole is operating as an inverter or as a rectifier. It is converter’s control variable used in power flow.

attributes.name: pPccControl
attributes.documentation: Kind of active power control.

attributes.name: ratedIdc
attributes.documentation: Rated converter DC current, also called IdN. The attribute shall be a positive value. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow.

attributes.name: targetAlpha
attributes.documentation: Target firing angle. It is converter’s control variable used in power flow. It is only applicable for rectifier if continuous tap changer control is used. Allowed values are within the range minAlpha<=targetAlpha<=maxAlpha. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetGamma
attributes.documentation: Target extinction angle. It is converter’s control variable used in power flow. It is only applicable for inverter if continuous tap changer control is used. Allowed values are within the range minGamma<=targetGamma<=maxGamma. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetIdc
attributes.documentation: DC current target value. It is converter’s control variable used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

classes.name: DCTopologicalNode
classes.documentation: DC bus.

classes.name: CsOperatingModeKind
classes.documentation: Operating mode for HVDC line operating as Current Source Converter.

literals.name: inverter
literals.documentation: Operating as inverter, which is the power receiving end.

literals.name: rectifier
literals.documentation: Operating as rectifier, which is the power sending end.

classes.name: CsPpccControlKind
classes.documentation: Active power control modes for HVDC line operating as Current Source Converter.

literals.name: activePower
literals.documentation: Control is active power control at AC side, at point of common coupling. Target is provided by ACDCConverter.targetPpcc.

literals.name: dcVoltage
literals.documentation: Control is DC voltage  with target value provided by ACDCConverter.targetUdc.

literals.name: dcCurrent
literals.documentation: Control is DC current  with target value provided by CsConverter.targetIdc.

classes.name: DCBaseTerminal
classes.documentation: An electrical connection point at a piece of DC conducting equipment. DC terminals are connected at one physical DC node that may have multiple DC terminals connected. A DC node is similar to an AC connectivity node. The model requires that DC connections are distinct from AC connections.

classes.name: DCBreaker
classes.documentation: A breaker within a DC system.

classes.name: DCBusbar
classes.documentation: A busbar within a DC system.

classes.name: DCChopper
classes.documentation: Low resistance equipment used in the internal DC circuit to balance voltages. It has typically positive and negative pole terminals and a ground.

classes.name: DCConductingEquipment
classes.documentation: The parts of the DC power system that are designed to carry current or that are conductively connected through DC terminals.

attributes.name: ratedUdc
attributes.documentation: Rated DC device voltage. The attribute shall be a positive value. It is configuration data used in power flow.

classes.name: DCConverterOperatingModeKind
classes.documentation: The operating mode of an HVDC bipole.

classes.name: DCConverterUnit
classes.documentation: Indivisible operative unit comprising all equipment between the point of common coupling on the AC side and the point of common coupling – DC side, essentially one or more converters, together with one or more converter transformers, converter control equipment, essential protective and switching devices and auxiliaries, if any, used for conversion.

attributes.name: operationMode
attributes.documentation: The operating mode of an HVDC bipole (bipolar, monopolar metallic return, etc).

classes.name: DCDisconnector
classes.documentation: A disconnector within a DC system.

classes.name: DCEquipmentContainer
classes.documentation: A modelling construct to provide a root class for containment of DC as well as AC equipment. The class differ from the EquipmentContaner for AC in that it may also contain DCNode-s. Hence it can contain both AC and DC equipment.

classes.name: DCGround
classes.documentation: A ground within a DC system.

attributes.name: inductance
attributes.documentation: Inductance to ground.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation: Resistance to ground.

classes.name: DCLine
classes.documentation: Overhead lines and/or cables connecting two or more HVDC substations.

classes.name: DCLineSegment
classes.documentation: A wire or combination of wires not insulated from one another, with consistent electrical characteristics, used to carry direct current between points in the DC region of the power system.

attributes.name: capacitance
attributes.documentation: Capacitance of the DC line segment. Significant for cables only.

attributes.name: inductance
attributes.documentation: Inductance of the DC line segment. Negligible compared with DCSeriesDevice used for smoothing.

attributes.name: length
attributes.documentation: Segment length for calculating line section capabilities.

attributes.name: resistance
attributes.documentation: Resistance of the DC line segment.

classes.name: DCNode
classes.documentation: DC nodes are points where terminals of DC conducting equipment are connected together with zero impedance.

classes.name: DCPolarityKind
classes.documentation: Polarity for DC circuits.

literals.name: positive
literals.documentation: Positive pole. The converter terminal is intended to operate at a positive voltage relative the midpoint or negative terminal.

literals.name: middle
literals.documentation: Middle pole. The converter terminal is the midpoint in a bipolar or symmetric monopole configuration. The midpoint can be grounded and/or have a metallic return.

literals.name: negative
literals.documentation: Negative pole. The converter terminal is intended to operate at a negative voltage relative the midpoint or positive terminal.

classes.name: DCSeriesDevice
classes.documentation: A series device within the DC system, typically a reactor used for filtering or smoothing.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

attributes.name: inductance
attributes.documentation: Inductance of the device.

attributes.name: resistance
attributes.documentation: Resistance of the DC device.

classes.name: DCShunt
classes.documentation: A shunt device within the DC system, typically used for filtering.  Needed for transient and short circuit studies.

attributes.name: capacitance
attributes.documentation: Capacitance of the DC shunt.

attributes.name: resistance
attributes.documentation: Resistance of the DC device.

classes.name: DCSwitch
classes.documentation: A switch within the DC system.

classes.name: DCTerminal
classes.documentation: An electrical connection point to generic DC conducting equipment.

classes.name: DCTopologicalIsland
classes.documentation:
An electrically connected subset of the network. DC topological islands can change as the current network state changes, e.g. due to: 
- disconnect switches or breakers changing state in a SCADA/EMS.
- manual creation, change or deletion of topological nodes in a planning tool.
Only energised TopologicalNode-s shall be part of the topological island.

classes.name: PerLengthDCLineParameter
classes.documentation: Common type for per-length electrical catalogues describing DC line parameters.

attributes.name: capacitance
attributes.documentation: Capacitance per unit of length of the DC line segment; significant for cables only.

attributes.name: inductance
attributes.documentation: Inductance per unit of length of the DC line segment.

attributes.name: resistance
attributes.documentation: Resistance per length of the DC line segment.

classes.name: VsCapabilityCurve
classes.documentation: The P-Q capability curve for a voltage source converter, with P on X-axis and Qmin and Qmax on Y1-axis and Y2-axis.

classes.name: VsConverter
classes.documentation: DC side of the voltage source converter (VSC).

attributes.name: delta
attributes.documentation: Angle between VsConverter.uv and ACDCConverter.uc. It is converter’s state variable used in power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

attributes.name: droop
attributes.documentation: Droop constant. The pu value is obtained as D [kV/MW] x Sb / Ubdc. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: droopCompensation
attributes.documentation: Compensation constant. Used to compensate for voltage drop when controlling voltage at a distant bus. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: maxModulationIndex
attributes.documentation: The maximum quotient between the AC converter voltage (Uc) and DC voltage (Ud). A factor typically less than 1. It is converter’s configuration data used in power flow.

attributes.name: maxValveCurrent
attributes.documentation: The maximum current through a valve. It is converter’s configuration data.

attributes.name: pPccControl
attributes.documentation: Kind of control of real power and/or DC voltage.

attributes.name: qPccControl
attributes.documentation: Kind of reactive power control.

attributes.name: qShare
attributes.documentation: Reactive power sharing factor among parallel converters on Uac control. The attribute shall be a positive value or zero.

attributes.name: targetPhasePcc
attributes.documentation: Phase target at AC side, at point of common coupling. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetPowerFactorPcc
attributes.documentation: Power factor target at the AC side, at point of common coupling. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetPWMfactor
attributes.documentation: Magnitude of pulse-modulation factor. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: targetQpcc
attributes.documentation: Reactive power injection target in AC grid, at point of common coupling.  Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.

attributes.name: targetUpcc
attributes.documentation: Voltage target in AC grid, at point of common coupling. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: uv
attributes.documentation: Line-to-line voltage on the valve side of the converter transformer. It is converter’s state variable, result from power flow. The attribute shall be a positive value.

classes.name: VsPpccControlKind
classes.documentation: Types applicable to the control of real power and/or DC voltage by voltage source converter.

literals.name: pPcc
literals.documentation: Control is real power at point of common coupling. The target value is provided by ACDCConverter.targetPpcc.

literals.name: udc
literals.documentation: Control is DC voltage  with target value provided by ACDCConverter.targetUdc.

literals.name: pPccAndUdcDroop
literals.documentation: Control is active power at point of common coupling and local DC voltage, with the droop. Target values are provided by ACDCConverter.targetPpcc, ACDCConverter.targetUdc and VsConverter.droop.

literals.name: pPccAndUdcDroopWithCompensation
literals.documentation: Control is active power at point of common coupling and compensated DC voltage, with the droop. Compensation factor is the resistance, as an approximation of the DC voltage of a common (real or virtual) node in the DC network. Targets are provided by ACDCConverter.targetPpcc, ACDCConverter.targetUdc, VsConverter.droop and VsConverter.droopCompensation.

literals.name: pPccAndUdcDroopPilot
literals.documentation: Control is active power at point of common coupling and the pilot DC voltage, with the droop. The mode is used for Multi Terminal High Voltage DC (MTDC) systems where multiple HVDC Substations are connected to the HVDC transmission lines. The pilot voltage is then used to coordinate the control the DC voltage across the HVDC substations. Targets are provided by ACDCConverter.targetPpcc, ACDCConverter.targetUdc and  VsConverter.droop.

literals.name: phasePcc
literals.documentation: Control is phase at point of common coupling. Target is provided by VsConverter.targetPhasePcc.

classes.name: VsQpccControlKind
classes.documentation: Kind of reactive power control at point of common coupling for a voltage source converter.

literals.name: reactivePcc
literals.documentation: Control is reactive power at point of common coupling. Target is provided by VsConverter.targetQpcc.

literals.name: voltagePcc
literals.documentation: Control is voltage at point of common coupling. Target is provided by VsConverter.targetUpcc.

literals.name: powerFactorPcc
literals.documentation: Control is power factor at point of common coupling. Target is provided by VsConverter.targetPowerFactorPcc.

literals.name: pulseWidthModulation
literals.documentation: No explicit control. Pulse-modulation factor is directly set in magnitude (VsConverter.targetPWMfactor) and phase (VsConverter.targetPhasePcc).

subPackages.name: DetailedDiagrams
subPackages.documentation: This package contains instances used in instance diagrams for DC sample modelling.

classes.name: EquivalentBranch
classes.documentation: The class represents equivalent branches. In cases where a transformer phase shift is modelled and the EquivalentBranch is spanning the same nodes, the impedance quantities for the EquivalentBranch shall consider the needed phase shift.

attributes.name: negativeR12
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence series resistance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: negativeR21
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence series resistance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: negativeX12
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence series reactance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: negativeX21
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence series reactance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage: EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: positiveR12
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence series resistance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2 . Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909. 
EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: positiveR21
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence series resistance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: positiveX12
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence series reactance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: positiveX21
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence series reactance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence series resistance of the reduced branch.

attributes.name: r21
attributes.documentation:
Resistance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1 .Used for steady state power flow. This attribute is optional and represent unbalanced network such as off-nominal phase shifter. If only EquivalentBranch.r is given, then EquivalentBranch.r21 is assumed equal to EquivalentBranch.r.
Usage rule : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: x
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence series reactance of the reduced branch.

attributes.name: x21
attributes.documentation:
Reactance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for steady state power flow. This attribute is optional and represents an unbalanced network such as off-nominal phase shifter. If only EquivalentBranch.x is given, then EquivalentBranch.x21 is assumed equal to EquivalentBranch.x.
Usage rule: EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: zeroR12
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence series resistance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: zeroR21
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence series resistance from terminal sequence  2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: zeroX12
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence series reactance from terminal sequence  1 to terminal sequence 2. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: zeroX21
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence series reactance from terminal sequence 2 to terminal sequence 1. Used for short circuit data exchange according to IEC 60909.
Usage : EquivalentBranch is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

classes.name: EquivalentEquipment
classes.documentation: The class represents equivalent objects that are the result of a network reduction. The class is the base for equivalent objects of different types.

classes.name: EquivalentInjection
classes.documentation: This class represents equivalent injections (generation or load).  Voltage regulation is allowed only at the point of connection.

attributes.name: maxP
attributes.documentation: Maximum active power of the injection.

attributes.name: maxQ
attributes.documentation: Maximum reactive power of the injection.  Used for modelling of infeed for load flow exchange. Not used for short circuit modelling.  If maxQ and minQ are not used ReactiveCapabilityCurve can be used.

attributes.name: minP
attributes.documentation: Minimum active power of the injection.

attributes.name: minQ
attributes.documentation: Minimum reactive power of the injection.  Used for modelling of infeed for load flow exchange. Not used for short circuit modelling.  If maxQ and minQ are not used ReactiveCapabilityCurve can be used.

attributes.name: p
attributes.documentation:
Equivalent active power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: q
attributes.documentation:
Equivalent reactive power injection. Load sign convention is used, i.e. positive sign means flow out from a node.
Starting value for steady state solutions.

attributes.name: r
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence resistance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: r0
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence resistance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: r2
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence resistance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: regulationCapability
attributes.documentation: Specifies whether or not the EquivalentInjection has the capability to regulate the local voltage. If true the EquivalentInjection can regulate. If false the EquivalentInjection cannot regulate. ReactiveCapabilityCurve can only be associated with EquivalentInjection  if the flag is true.

attributes.name: regulationStatus
attributes.documentation: Specifies the regulation status of the EquivalentInjection.  True is regulating.  False is not regulating.

attributes.name: regulationTarget
attributes.documentation: The target voltage for voltage regulation. The attribute shall be a positive value.

attributes.name: x
attributes.documentation:
Positive sequence reactance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: x0
attributes.documentation:
Zero sequence reactance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

attributes.name: x2
attributes.documentation:
Negative sequence reactance. Used to represent Extended-Ward (IEC 60909).
Usage : Extended-Ward is a result of network reduction prior to the data exchange.

classes.name: EquivalentNetwork
classes.documentation: A class that groups electrical equivalents, including internal nodes, of a network that has been reduced. The ConnectivityNodes contained in the equivalent are intended to reflect internal nodes of the equivalent. The boundary Connectivity nodes where the equivalent connects outside itself are not contained by the equivalent.

classes.name: EquivalentShunt
classes.documentation: The class represents equivalent shunts.

attributes.name: b
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt susceptance.

attributes.name: g
attributes.documentation: Positive sequence shunt conductance.

subPackages.name: AuxiliaryEquipment
subPackages.documentation: Contains equipment which is not normal conducting equipment such as sensors, fault locators, and surge protectors.  These devices do not define power carrying topological connections as conducting equipment, but are associated to terminals of other conducting equipment.

classes.name: AuxiliaryEquipment
classes.documentation:
AuxiliaryEquipment describe equipment that is not performing any primary functions but support for the equipment performing the primary function.
AuxiliaryEquipment is attached to primary equipment via an association with Terminal.

classes.name: CurrentTransformer
classes.documentation: Instrument transformer used to measure electrical qualities of the circuit that is being protected and/or monitored. Typically used as current transducer for the purpose of metering or protection. A typical secondary current rating would be 5A.

attributes.name: accuracyClass
attributes.documentation: CT accuracy classification.

attributes.name: accuracyLimit
attributes.documentation: Percent of rated current for which the CT remains accurate within specified limits.

attributes.name: coreBurden
attributes.documentation: Power burden of the CT core.

attributes.name: ctClass
attributes.documentation: CT classification; i.e. class 10P.

attributes.name: usage
attributes.documentation: Intended usage of the CT; i.e. metering, protection.

classes.name: FaultIndicator
classes.documentation: A FaultIndicator is typically only an indicator (which may or may not be remotely monitored), and not a piece of equipment that actually initiates a protection event. It is used for FLISR (Fault Location, Isolation and Restoration) purposes, assisting with the dispatch of crews to "most likely" part of the network (i.e. assists with determining circuit section where the fault most likely happened).

classes.name: PostLineSensor
classes.documentation: A sensor used mainly in overhead distribution networks as the source of both current and voltage measurements.

classes.name: PotentialTransformer
classes.documentation: Instrument transformer (also known as Voltage Transformer) used to measure electrical qualities of the circuit that is being protected and/or monitored. Typically used as voltage transducer for the purpose of metering, protection, or sometimes auxiliary substation supply. A typical secondary voltage rating would be 120V.

attributes.name: accuracyClass
attributes.documentation: PT accuracy classification.

attributes.name: nominalRatio
attributes.documentation: Nominal ratio between the primary and secondary voltage.

attributes.name: ptClass
attributes.documentation: Potential transformer (PT) classification covering burden.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Potential transformer construction type.

classes.name: PotentialTransformerKind
classes.documentation: The construction kind of the potential transformer.

literals.name: inductive
literals.documentation: The potential transformer is using induction coils to create secondary voltage.

literals.name: capacitiveCoupling
literals.documentation: The potential transformer is using capacitive coupling to create secondary voltage.

classes.name: Sensor
classes.documentation: This class describe devices that transform a measured quantity into signals that can be presented at displays, used in control or be recorded.

classes.name: SurgeArrester
classes.documentation: Shunt device, installed on the network, usually in the proximity of electrical equipment in order to protect the said equipment against transient voltage transients caused by lightning or switching activity.

classes.name: WaveTrap
classes.documentation: Line traps are devices that impede high frequency power line carrier signals yet present a negligible impedance at the main power frequency.

subPackages.name: Meas
subPackages.documentation: Contains entities that describe dynamic measurement data exchanged between applications.

classes.name: Accumulator
classes.documentation: Accumulator represents an accumulated (counted) Measurement, e.g. an energy value.

attributes.name: maxValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range maximum for any of the MeasurementValue.values. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs or of telemetered raw values.

classes.name: AccumulatorLimit
classes.documentation: Limit values for Accumulator measurements.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value to supervise against. The value is positive.

classes.name: AccumulatorLimitSet
classes.documentation: An AccumulatorLimitSet specifies a set of Limits that are associated with an Accumulator measurement.

classes.name: AccumulatorReset
classes.documentation: This command resets the counter value to zero.

classes.name: AccumulatorValue
classes.documentation: AccumulatorValue represents an accumulated (counted) MeasurementValue.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value to supervise. The value is positive.

classes.name: Analog
classes.documentation: Analog represents an analog Measurement.

attributes.name: maxValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range maximum for any of the MeasurementValue.values. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs or of telemetered raw values.

attributes.name: minValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range minimum for any of the MeasurementValue.values. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs or of telemetered raw values.

attributes.name: normalValue
attributes.documentation: Normal measurement value, e.g., used for percentage calculations.

attributes.name: positiveFlowIn
attributes.documentation: If true then this measurement is an active power, reactive power or current with the convention that a positive value measured at the Terminal means power is flowing into the related PowerSystemResource.

classes.name: AnalogControl
classes.documentation: An analog control used for supervisory control.

attributes.name: maxValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range maximum for any of the Control.value. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs.

attributes.name: minValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range minimum for any of the Control.value. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs.

classes.name: AnalogLimit
classes.documentation: Limit values for Analog measurements.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value to supervise against.

classes.name: AnalogLimitSet
classes.documentation: An AnalogLimitSet specifies a set of Limits that are associated with an Analog measurement.

classes.name: AnalogValue
classes.documentation: AnalogValue represents an analog MeasurementValue.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value to supervise.

classes.name: Command
classes.documentation: A Command is a discrete control used for supervisory control.

attributes.name: normalValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value for Control.value e.g. used for percentage scaling.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value representing the actuator output.

classes.name: Control
classes.documentation: Control is used for supervisory/device control. It represents control outputs that are used to change the state in a process, e.g. close or open breaker, a set point value or a raise lower command.

attributes.name: controlType
attributes.documentation: Specifies the type of Control. For example, this specifies if the Control represents BreakerOpen, BreakerClose, GeneratorVoltageSetPoint, GeneratorRaise, GeneratorLower, etc.

attributes.name: operationInProgress
attributes.documentation: Indicates that a client is currently sending control commands that has not completed.

attributes.name: timeStamp
attributes.documentation: The last time a control output was sent.

attributes.name: unitMultiplier
attributes.documentation: The unit multiplier of the controlled quantity.

attributes.name: unitSymbol
attributes.documentation: The unit of measure of the controlled quantity.

classes.name: Discrete
classes.documentation: Discrete represents a discrete Measurement, i.e. a Measurement representing discrete values, e.g. a Breaker position.

attributes.name: maxValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range maximum for any of the MeasurementValue.values. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs or of telemetered raw values.

attributes.name: minValue
attributes.documentation: Normal value range minimum for any of the MeasurementValue.values. Used for scaling, e.g. in bar graphs or of telemetered raw values.

attributes.name: normalValue
attributes.documentation: Normal measurement value, e.g., used for percentage calculations.

classes.name: DiscreteValue
classes.documentation: DiscreteValue represents a discrete MeasurementValue.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: The value to supervise.

classes.name: IOPoint
classes.documentation: The class describe a measurement or control value. The purpose is to enable having attributes and associations common for measurement and control.

classes.name: Limit
classes.documentation: Specifies one limit value for a Measurement. A Measurement typically has several limits that are kept together by the LimitSet class. The actual meaning and use of a Limit instance (i.e., if it is an alarm or warning limit or if it is a high or low limit) is not captured in the Limit class. However the name of a Limit instance may indicate both meaning and use.

classes.name: LimitSet
classes.documentation: Specifies a set of Limits that are associated with a Measurement. A Measurement may have several LimitSets corresponding to seasonal or other changing conditions. The condition is captured in the name and description attributes. The same LimitSet may be used for several Measurements. In particular percentage limits are used this way.

attributes.name: isPercentageLimits
attributes.documentation: Tells if the limit values are in percentage of normalValue or the specified Unit for Measurements and Controls.

classes.name: Measurement
classes.documentation:
A Measurement represents any measured, calculated or non-measured non-calculated quantity. Any piece of equipment may contain Measurements, e.g. a substation may have temperature measurements and door open indications, a transformer may have oil temperature and tank pressure measurements, a bay may contain a number of power flow measurements and a Breaker may contain a switch status measurement. 
The PSR - Measurement association is intended to capture this use of Measurement and is included in the naming hierarchy based on EquipmentContainer. The naming hierarchy typically has Measurements as leaves, e.g. Substation-VoltageLevel-Bay-Switch-Measurement.
Some Measurements represent quantities related to a particular sensor location in the network, e.g. a voltage transformer (VT) or potential transformer (PT) at a busbar or a current transformer (CT) at the bar between a breaker and an isolator. The sensing position is not captured in the PSR - Measurement association. Instead it is captured by the Measurement - Terminal association that is used to define the sensing location in the network topology. The location is defined by the connection of the Terminal to ConductingEquipment. 
If both a Terminal and PSR are associated, and the PSR is of type ConductingEquipment, the associated Terminal should belong to that ConductingEquipment instance.
When the sensor location is needed both Measurement-PSR and Measurement-Terminal are used. The Measurement-Terminal association is never used alone.

attributes.name: measurementType
attributes.documentation:
Specifies the type of measurement.  For example, this specifies if the measurement represents an indoor temperature, outdoor temperature, bus voltage, line flow, etc.
When the measurementType is set to "Specialization", the type of Measurement is defined in more detail by the specialized class which inherits from Measurement.

attributes.name: phases
attributes.documentation:
Indicates to which phases the measurement applies and avoids the need to use 'measurementType' to also encode phase information (which would explode the types). The phase information in Measurement, along with 'measurementType' and 'phases' uniquely defines a Measurement for a device, based on normal network phase. Their meaning will not change when the computed energizing phasing is changed due to jumpers or other reasons.
If the attribute is missing three phases (ABC) shall be assumed.

attributes.name: unitMultiplier
attributes.documentation: The unit multiplier of the measured quantity.

attributes.name: unitSymbol
attributes.documentation: The unit of measure of the measured quantity.

classes.name: MeasurementValue
classes.documentation: The current state for a measurement. A state value is an instance of a measurement from a specific source. Measurements can be associated with many state values, each representing a different source for the measurement.

attributes.name: sensorAccuracy
attributes.documentation: The limit, expressed as a percentage of the sensor maximum, that errors will not exceed when the sensor is used under  reference conditions.

attributes.name: timeStamp
attributes.documentation: The time when the value was last updated.

classes.name: MeasurementValueQuality
classes.documentation: Measurement quality flags. Bits 0-10 are defined for substation automation in IEC 61850-7-3. Bits 11-15 are reserved for future expansion by that document. Bits 16-31 are reserved for EMS applications.

classes.name: MeasurementValueSource
classes.documentation: MeasurementValueSource describes the alternative sources updating a MeasurementValue. User conventions for how to use the MeasurementValueSource attributes are defined in IEC 61970-301.

classes.name: Quality61850
classes.documentation: Quality flags in this class are as defined in IEC 61850, except for estimatorReplaced, which has been included in this class for convenience.

attributes.name: badReference
attributes.documentation: Measurement value may be incorrect due to a reference being out of calibration.

attributes.name: estimatorReplaced
attributes.documentation: Value has been replaced by State Estimator. estimatorReplaced is not an IEC61850 quality bit but has been put in this class for convenience.

attributes.name: failure
attributes.documentation: This identifier indicates that a supervision function has detected an internal or external failure, e.g. communication failure.

attributes.name: oldData
attributes.documentation: Measurement value is old and possibly invalid, as it has not been successfully updated during a specified time interval.

attributes.name: operatorBlocked
attributes.documentation: Measurement value is blocked and hence unavailable for transmission.

attributes.name: oscillatory
attributes.documentation: To prevent some overload of the communication it is sensible to detect and suppress oscillating (fast changing) binary inputs. If a signal changes in a defined time twice in the same direction (from 0 to 1 or from 1 to 0) then oscillation is detected and the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" is set. If it is detected a configured numbers of transient changes could be passed by. In this time the validity status "questionable" is set. If after this defined numbers of changes the signal is still in the oscillating state the value shall be set either to the opposite state of the previous stable value or to a defined default value. In this case the validity status "questionable" is reset and "invalid" is set as long as the signal is oscillating. If it is configured such that no transient changes should be passed by then the validity status "invalid" is set immediately in addition to the detail quality identifier "oscillatory" (used for status information only).

attributes.name: outOfRange
attributes.documentation: Measurement value is beyond a predefined range of value.

attributes.name: overFlow
attributes.documentation: Measurement value is beyond the capability of being  represented properly. For example, a counter value overflows from maximum count back to a value of zero.
