classes.documentation:
Load whose behaviour is described by reference to a standard model <font color="#0f0f0f">or by definition of a user-defined model.</font>
A standard feature of dynamic load behaviour modelling is the ability to associate the same behaviour to multiple energy consumers by means of a single load definition.  The load model is always applied to individual bus loads (energy consumers).

classes.name: LoadAggregate
classes.documentation:
Aggregate loads are used to represent all or part of the real and reactive load from one or more loads in the static (power flow) data. This load is usually the aggregation of many individual load devices and the load model is an approximate representation of the aggregate response of the load devices to system disturbances.
Standard aggregate load model comprised of static and/or dynamic components.  A static load model represents the sensitivity of the real and reactive power consumed by the load to the amplitude and frequency of the bus voltage. A dynamic load model can be used to represent the aggregate response of the motor components of the load.

classes.name: LoadMotor
classes.documentation: Aggregate induction motor load. This model is used to represent a fraction of an ordinary load as "induction motor load". It allows a load that is treated as an ordinary constant power in power flow analysis to be represented by an induction motor in dynamic simulation. This model is intended for representation of aggregations of many motors dispersed through a load represented at a high voltage bus but where there is no information on the characteristics of individual motors. Either a "one-cage" or "two-cage" model of the induction machine can be modelled. Magnetic saturation is not modelled. This model treats a fraction of the constant power part of a load as a motor. During initialisation, the initial power drawn by the motor is set equal to Pfrac times the constant P part of the static load. The remainder of the load is left as a static load. The reactive power demand of the motor is calculated during initialisation as a function of voltage at the load bus. This reactive power demand can be less than or greater than the constant Q component of the load. If the motor's reactive demand is greater than the constant Q component of the load, the model inserts a shunt capacitor at the terminal of the motor to bring its reactive demand down to equal the constant Q reactive load. If an induction motor load model and a static load model are both present for a load, the motor Pfrac is assumed to be subtracted from the power flow constant P load before the static load model is applied. The remainder of the load, if any, is then represented by the static load model.

subPackages.name: UserDefinedModels
subPackages.documentation:
This subclause contains user-defined dynamic model classes to support the exchange of both proprietary and explicitly defined user-defined models.  
<u>Proprietary models</u> represent behaviour which, while not defined by a standard model class, is mutually understood by the sending and receiving applications based on the name passed in the .name attribute of the appropriate xxxUserDefined class.  Proprietary model parameters are passed as general attributes using as many instances of the ProprietaryParameterDynamics class as there are parameters.
<u>Explicitly defined models</u> describe dynamic behaviour in detail in terms of control blocks and their input and output signals.  Note that the classes to support explicitly defined modelling are not currently defined - it is future work intended to also be supported by the family of xxxUserDefined classes.
Both types of user-defined models use the family of xxxUserDefined classes, which allow a user-defined model to be used:
- as the model for an individual standard function block (such as a turbine-governor or power system stabilizer) in a standard interconnection model whose other function blocks could be either standard or user-defined.  For an illustration of this form of usage for a proprietary model, see the ExampleFunctionBlockProprietaryModel diagram in subclause 5.5.
- as the complete representation of a dynamic behaviour model (for an entire synchronous machine, for example) where standard function blocks and standard interconnections are not used at all. For an illustration of this form of usage for a proprietary model, see the ExampleCompleteProprietaryModel diagram in subclause 5.5.

subPackages.name: InfIEC61970
subPackages.documentation:
This package and its subpackages contain informative (unstable) elements of the model, expected to evolve a lot or to be removed, and not published as IEC document yet. Some portions of it will be reworked and moved to normative packages as the need arises, and some portions may be removed.

A generic container of a version of instance data. The MRID can be used in an audit trail, not in reusable script intended to work with new versions of data.
A dataset could be serialized multiple times and in multiple technologies, yet retain the same identity.

attributes.name: description
attributes.documentation: The description is a free human readable text describing or naming the object. It may be non unique and may not correlate to a naming hierarchy.

attributes.name: mRID
attributes.documentation:
Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID,  as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552 Edition 1, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

classes.documentation: A limit calculation model used to compute an operational limit based on external input such as temperature. These are intended to be shared among operational limits with the same calculation form that apply to a piece of equipment..

classes.documentation: Specifies an operational  limit is calculated by scaling another operational limit.

attributes.name: limitScalingPercent
attributes.documentation: The associated source limit is scaled by this value to compute the limit of the dependency model.

classes.name: OperatonalLimitTypeScaling
classes.documentation: One operational limit type scales values of another operational limit type when under the same operational limit set.    This applies to any operational limit assigned to the target operational limit type and without other limit dependency models.

attributes.name: scalingPercent
attributes.documentation: The percentage scaling of the source limit to compute the target limit.  Applys to operational limits within an operaitonal limit set when both source and target operational limit types exist.

classes.name: ScheduledVoltageLimitValue

classes.name: SeriesEquipmentDependentLimit
classes.documentation:
Limit based on most restrictive series equipment limit.
A specification of  of equipment that determines the calculated operational limit values based upon other equipment and their ratings.  The most restrictive limit connected in series within the group is used.   The physical connection based on switch status for example may also impact which elements in the group are considered. Any equipment in the group that are presently connected in series with the equipment of the directly associated operational limit are used.   This provides a means to indicate which potentially series equipment limits are considered for a computed operational limit. The operational limit of the same operational limit type is assumed to be used from the grouped equipment.   It is also possible to make assumptions or calculations regarding how flow might split if the equipment is not simply in series.

The IEC 61968 subpackages of the CIM are developed, standardized and maintained by the UCA community including its working groups and task forces.
Currently, normative parts of the model support the needs of information exchange defined in IEC 61968-3, IEC 61968-4, IEC 61968-5, IEC 61968-6, IEC 61968-8, IEC 61968-9 and in IEC 61968-13.

attributes.name: detectionLimit
attributes.documentation: Detection limit of related analog value if different from detection limit of test standard or if there is no test standard. The detection limit (also known as lower limit of detection or limit of detection (LOD), is the lowest quantity of a substance that can be distinguished from the absence of that substance (a blank value) within a stated confidence limit (generally 1%).

attributes.name: precision
attributes.documentation: Precision of related analog value if different from precision of test standard or if there is no test standard. Precision is a measure of how closely individual measurements agree with one another. Expressed as 'plus or minus' the value of this attribute.

attributes.name: reportingTemperature
attributes.documentation: Reporting temperature of related analog value if different from reporting temperature of test standard or if there is no test standard. Reporting temperature is what gas volumes are normalized to. Different reporting temperatures are used by different sources. For example, ASTM specifies 0°C, whereas IEC specifies 20°C. Online monitors often have their own unique reporting temperatures.

literals.name: acidNumber
literals.documentation: Acid neutralization number (in milligram of KOH/gram).

literals.name: interfacialTension
literals.documentation: Interfacial tension (in dyne/centimetre or milliNewton/metre, which are the same).

literals.name: dielectricBreakdown
literals.documentation: Dielectric breakdown, for electrode gap size and temperature specified by selected standard  (in kV).

literals.name: powerFactorPercent
literals.documentation: Fluid power factor at specified temperature (in percent). Commonly used in US. (Note: Fluid power factor is very similar to fluid dissapation factor, but fluid power factor is cosine of the phase angle between an AC voltage applied to oil and the resulting current (where dissipation factor is the tangent). For values up to 0.005, fluid power factor and dissapation factor are very close. There is a conversion equation between the two).

literals.name: dissipationFactor
literals.documentation: Fluid dissipation factor in absolute value, not a percentage. (Multiplying this value by 100 would result in dissipation factor percent).

literals.name: dissipationFactorPercent
literals.documentation: Fluid dissipation factor (in percent). Commonly used in Asia. Dissipation factor is also known as loss factor or tan delta.

literals.name: oxidationInhibitorDBP
literals.documentation: 2,6-ditertiary-butyl phenol (DBP) oxidation inhibitor concentration (in percent by weight).

literals.name: oxidationInhibitorDBPC
literals.documentation: 2,6-ditertiarybutyl para-cresol (DBPC) oxidation inhibitor concentration (in percent by weight).

literals.name: oxidationInhibitorD2668
literals.documentation: 2,6-ditertiary-butyl para-cresol and 2,6-ditertiary-butyl phenol concentration (in percent by weight).

literals.name: additiveDBDS
literals.documentation: Dibenzyl disulfide (DBDS) concentration (in ppm, specificially in milligram/kilogram).

literals.name: specificGravity
literals.documentation: Specific gravity corrected to 15°C. Also known as relative density. It is a ratio of density of tested oil to density of water at a specific temperature.

literals.name: firePoint
literals.documentation: Fire point (in °C). Fire point is when fire is sustained (oil catches fire). Can only be done by means of open cup test, which is commonly used in US.

literals.name: flashPointOpenCup
literals.documentation: Flash point (in °C) determined via open cup test. Flash point occurs when enough vapors have accumulated to sustain a flash. Open cup is used in US.

literals.name: flashPointClosedCup
literals.documentation: Flash point (in °C) determined via closed cup test. Flash point occurs when enough vapors have accumulated to sustain a flash. Closed cup is used in Europe.

literals.name: pourPoint
literals.documentation: Pour point (in °C). The pour point of a liquid is the temperature at which it becomes semi solid and loses its flow characteristics.

literals.name: pourPointAutomatic
literals.documentation: Pour point (in °C) determined by automatic method. The pour point of a liquid is the temperature at which it becomes semi solid and loses its flow characteristics.

literals.name: kinematicViscosity
literals.documentation: Kinematic viscosity (in millimetre2/second). Kinematic viscosity is the ratio of - absolute (or dynamic) viscosity to density.

literals.name: staticElectrification
literals.documentation: Static electrification tendency (in microcoulombs per metre3). Also called static charging tendency and electrostatic charging tendency (ECT).

literals.name: passivatorIrgamet39
literals.documentation: Irgamet 39 metal passivator content (in ppm, specifically milligram/kilogram).

literals.name: passivatorTTA
literals.documentation: Metal passivator TTA (Irgamet39 in solid form) content (in milligram/kilogram).

literals.name: carbonyl
literals.documentation: Concentration of carbonyl compounds (aldehydes and ketones) determined using infrared spectroscopy (in percent).

literals.name: aromatics
literals.documentation: Concentration of aromatic compounds determined using infrared spectroscopy (in percent).

literals.name: sludge
literals.documentation: Sludge (in percent by mass). Typically performed on new oil,but can be done on used oil.

literals.name: solubleAcids
literals.documentation: Soluble acids  (in milligram of KOH/gram). Typically performed on new oil,but can be done on used oil.

literals.name: volatileAcids
literals.documentation: Volatile acids (in milligram of KOH/gram). Typically performed on new oil,but can be done on used oil.

literals.name: totalAcids
literals.documentation: Total acids (soluble plus volatile) (in milligram of KOH/gram). Typically performed on new oil,but can be done on used oil.

literals.name: inductionTime
literals.documentation: Oxidation induction time (in hours). Typically performed on new oil,but can be done on used oil.

literals.name: inhibitor61125MethodC
literals.documentation: Amount of inhibitor used in oxidation stablity test performed according to IEC 61125, method C. This value should accompany values resulting from testing according to IEC 61125, method  C to allow interpretation.

literals.name: duration61125MethodC
literals.documentation: Duration of oxidation stablity test performed according to IEC 61125, method C. This value should accompany values resulting from testing according to IEC 61125, method C to allow interpretation. Standard specified values are: 164, 332, and 500, but others can be used if agreed upon.

literals.name: petroleumOrigin
literals.documentation: Characterization of the carbon-type composition of insulating oils by petroleum origin.

literals.name: colorNumber
literals.documentation:
Fluid color index number.  Color numbers are expressed in 0.5 intervals and value specified is  "less-than". For example, a value of '2.5' means the color index number is between 2.0 and 2.5.
Possible values: 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0.

literals.name: colorNumberPlatinumCobaltScale
literals.documentation:
Fluid color index on the platinum cobalt scale. 
Possible values: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450.

literals.name: corrosiveSulphurByD1275
literals.documentation:
Corrosive sulphur test result using bare copper strip test.
Possible values: corrosive, nonCorrosive.

literals.name: corrosiveSulphurBy62535
literals.documentation:
Corrosive sulphur test result using covered (copper) conductor deposition test.
Possible values: potentiallyCorrosive, nonCorrosive.

literals.name: corrosiveSulphurBy51353
literals.documentation:
Corrosive sulphur test result using silver strip test.
Possible values: absent, present.

literals.name: tarnishLevel
literals.documentation:
Tarnish level indicated by corrosive sulphur test.
Possible values: 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 2C, 2D, 2E, 3A, 3B, 4A, 4B, 4C.

literals.name: sludgePrecipitation
literals.documentation:
Sludge precipitation test results.
Possible values: present, notPresent.

literals.name: carbon4

literals.name: isobutane
literals.documentation: isoC4 (C4H10) concentration (in ppm, specifically in microlitre/litre). Isobutane is also known as methylpropane.

literals.name: equivalentTCGPercent
literals.documentation:
Equivalent Total Combustible Gas (ETCG) percent.
An estimate, calculated from the dissolved-gas concentrations and the oil sample temperature, of what the TCG would be in a gas space in equilibrium with the oil. ETCG reflects what the TCG would be in air spaces near the oil.

literals.name: totalHeatGas
literals.documentation: Sum of concentrations of methane, ethane, and ethylene (in ppm, specifically in microlitre/litre). Used in some diagnostic gas ratios, especially THG/acetylene, which compares “heat gas” to “arcing gas.”

literals.name: totalDissolvedCombustibleGas
literals.documentation: Total dissolved combustible gas concentration (in ppm, specifically in microlitre/litre). Calculated by adding the ppm of combustible gasses: hydrogen (H2), methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), ethylene (C2H4), acetylene (C2H2), and carbon monoxide (CO).

literals.name: totalPartialPressure
literals.documentation:
Total partial pressure (in Pa).
Calculated value reflecting total of partial pressures of all combustible gasses.

literals.name: estimatedSafeHandlingLimit
literals.documentation:
Estimated Safe Handling Limit (ESHL) (in percent). Estimated safe handling limit is an estimate of the lower flammability limit (LFL) of the combustible gas mixture which the dissolved gas in the oil would give off by the oil if exposed to air. 
Expressed in percent like the equivalent total combustible gas percent, it is calculated from the dissolved-gas concentrations, the oil sample temperature, and the lower flammability limits of the individual combustible gases.

literals.name: hydran
literals.documentation:
Measured composite of dissolved fault gas concentrations (in ppm, specifically in microlitre/litre). Relative sensitivity
- H2: 100 % of concentration
- CO: 15 ± 4 % of concentration
- C2H2: 8 ± 2 % of concentration
- C2H4: 1.5 ± 0.5 % of concentration.

literals.name: hydranPredicted
literals.documentation:
Predicted hydran value (in ppm, specifically in microlitre/litre), calculated based on individual measured dissolved gas concentrations.
- H2: 100 % of concentration
- CO: 15 ± 4 % of concentration
- C2H2: 8 ± 2 % of concentration
- C2H4: 1.5 ± 0.5 % of concentration

classes.documentation: The DER curve data class provides the nominal, maximum and minimum values for a DER Monitorable parameter for a series of time intervals defined by the DER DispatchSchedule.

attributes.name: intervalNumber
attributes.documentation: The sequence number of a time interval defined by the DispatchSchedule.

attributes.name: maxYValue
attributes.documentation: The maximum value of the DERMonitorableParameter during the time interval.

attributes.name: minYValue
attributes.documentation: The minimum value of the DERMonitorableParameter during the time interval.

attributes.name: nominalYValue
attributes.documentation: The nominal value of the DERMonitorableParameter during the time interval.

attributes.name: timeStamp
attributes.documentation: The start time of the interval

classes.name: DERFunction
classes.documentation: Specifies the list of functions that are supported.

attributes.name: connectDisconnect
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the connect/disconnect function is supported.

attributes.name: maxRealPowerLimiting
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the maxRealPowerLimiting function is supported.

attributes.name: rampRateControl
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the rampRateControl function is supported.

attributes.name: reactivePowerDispatch
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the reactivePowerDispatch function is supported.

attributes.name: realPowerDispatch
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the realPowerDispatch function is supported.

attributes.name: voltageRegulation
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the voltageRegulation function is supported.

attributes.name: voltVarCurveFunction
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the voltVARCurveFunction is supported.

attributes.name: voltWattCurveFunction
attributes.documentation: If set to TRUE, the voltWattCurveFunction is supported.

classes.name: DERGroupDispatch
classes.documentation: Specifies the capabilities of the DER Group that are to be dispatched according to a schedule.  Each dispatch identifies a DER Group and the specific monitorable parameter to be dispatched over a specific time interval.

classes.name: DERGroupForecast
classes.documentation: Specifies the forecasted values of the DERMonitorableParameters for a DER Group over a specific time interval.

attributes.name: predictionCreationDate
attributes.documentation: The timestamp for when the DER Group forecast was created

classes.name: DERMonitorableParameter
classes.documentation: To define the DER monitorable parameters that will be forecasted and dispatched for a DER Group.  Each parameter is represented as a Y Value at a point in time or on a curve as a function of time, which is represented on the X axis.

attributes.name: DERParameter
attributes.documentation: Defines the specific engineering value being forecasted or dispatched.

attributes.name: flowDirection
attributes.documentation: Kind of flow direction for reading/measured  values proper to some commodities such as, for example, energy, power, demand.

attributes.name: yMultiplier
attributes.documentation: The UnitMultiplier that is applied to the DERMonitorableParameter.

attributes.name: yUnit
attributes.documentation: The DERUnitSymbol that is applied to the DERMonitorableParameter

attributes.name: yUnitInstalledMax
attributes.documentation: The maximum value of the DERMonitorableParameter based on the installed capacity.

attributes.name: yUnitInstalledMin
attributes.documentation: The minimum value of the DERMonitorableParameter based on the installed capacity.

classes.name: DERParameterKind
classes.documentation: Specifies the DER parameters related to the unit of power, ramp rate and regulation flows.

literals.name: apparentPower
literals.documentation: The combination of reactive power and active power, and is the product of voltage and current without reference to the phase angle.

literals.name: activePower
literals.documentation: The amount of power being used, measured in Watts.

literals.name: reactivePower
literals.documentation: The measure of reactance, measured in Vars.

literals.name: highFilterBiDirectionalRegulation
literals.documentation: AC voltage regulation of high frequency

literals.name: lowFilterBiDirectionalRegulation
literals.documentation: Used to filter out the sinosuidal disturbances to the grid.

literals.name: increasingRampRate
literals.documentation: An indication of whether the ramp rate associated with a curve is positive.

literals.name: decreasingRampRate
literals.documentation: An indication of whether the ramp rate associated with a curve is negative.

literals.name: voltage
literals.documentation: The measure of difference in potential between two points, measured in Volts.

classes.name: DispatchSchedule
classes.documentation: Specifies the characteristics of the time schedule over which DERMonitorableParameters are dispatched.

attributes.name: confidence
attributes.documentation: A value set by the system, function, algorithm or person creating a prediction as to how accurate the prediction is.

attributes.name: curveStyleKind
attributes.documentation: Used to specify whether the values over an interval are constant (constantYValue) or linearly interpolated (straightLineYValues)

attributes.name: numberOfIntervals
attributes.documentation: Used to specify the number of intervals when requesting a forecast or a dispatch.

attributes.name: startTime
attributes.documentation: The start time of the first interval in the dispatch schedule

attributes.name: timeIntervalDuration
attributes.documentation: The length of time for each interval in the dispatch schedule.

attributes.name: timeIntervalUnit
attributes.documentation: The unit of measure for the time axis of the dispatch schedule.

classes.name: TimeIntervalKind
classes.documentation: Specifies the unit of time for the intervals in the schedule.

classes.name: DERUnitSymbol
classes.documentation: The units defined for usage in DER related contexts.  This class is a subset plus possible additions of the UnitSymbol Class in the CIM Domain Package.

literals.name: degC
literals.documentation:
Relative temperature in degrees Celsius.
In the SI unit system the symbol is єC. Electric charge is measured in coulomb that has the unit symbol C. To distinguish degree Celsius form coulomb the symbol used in the UML is degC. Reason for not using єC is the special character є is difficult to manage in software.

literals.name: W
literals.documentation: Real power in Watt (J/s). Electrical power may have real and reactive components. The real portion of electrical power (IІR or VIcos(phi)), is expressed in Watts. (See also apparent power and reactive power.)

literals.name: VA
literals.documentation: Apparent power in Volt Ampere (See also real power and reactive power.)

literals.name: VAr
literals.documentation:
Reactive power in Volt Ampere reactive. The “reactive” or “imaginary” component of electrical power (VIsin(phi)). (See also real power and apparent power).
Note: Different meter designs use different methods to arrive at their results. Some meters may compute reactive power as an arithmetic value, while others compute the value vectorially. The data consumer should determine the method in use and the suitability of the measurement for the intended purpose.

literals.name: VAh

literals.name: VArh

literals.name: WPers

literals.name: VPerVA
literals.documentation: Power factor, PF, the ratio of the active power to the apparent power. Note: The sign convention used for power factor will differ between IEC meters and EEI (ANSI) meters. It is assumed that the data consumers understand the type of meter being used and agree on the sign convention in use at any given utility.

literals.name: WPerA
literals.documentation: Active power per current flow, watt per Ampere.

literals.name: VPerVAr
literals.documentation: Power factor, PF, the ratio of the active power to the apparent power. Note: The sign convention used for power factor will differ between IEC meters and EEI (ANSI) meters. It is assumed that the data consumers understand the type of meter being used and agree on the sign convention in use at any given utility.

literals.name: ohmPerm
literals.documentation: Electric resistance per length in ohm per metre ((V/A)/m).

attributes.name: crsUrn
attributes.documentation:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) for the coordinate reference system (crs) used to define 'Location.PositionPoints'.
An example would be the European Petroleum Survey Group (EPSG) code for a coordinate reference system, defined in URN under the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) namespace as: urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::XXXX, where XXXX is an EPSG code (a full list of codes can be found at the EPSG Registry web site http://www.epsg-registry.org/). To define the coordinate system as being WGS84 (latitude, longitude) using an EPSG OGC, this attribute would be urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::4.3.2.6
A profile should limit this code to a set of allowed URNs agreed to by all sending and receiving parties.

classes.name: Outage
classes.documentation:
Document describing details of an active or planned outage in a part of the electrical network.
A non-planned outage may be created upon:
- a breaker trip,
- a fault indicator status change,
- a meter event indicating customer outage,
- a reception of one or more customer trouble calls, or
- an operator command, reflecting information obtained from the field crew.
Outage restoration may be performed using a switching plan which complements the outage information with detailed switching activities, including the relationship to the crew and work.
A planned outage may be created upon:
- a request for service, maintenance or construction work in the field, or
- an operator-defined outage for what-if/contingency network analysis.

attributes.name: actualPeriod
attributes.documentation: Actual outage period; end of the period corresponds to the actual restoration time.

attributes.name: communityDescriptor
attributes.documentation: a name to denote the community - this could be a name or a code of some kind.

attributes.name: customersRestored
attributes.documentation: number of customers that have been restored in the area.

attributes.name: estimatedPeriod
attributes.documentation: Estimated outage period for a planned outage. The start of the period is the start of the planned outage and the end of the period corresponds to the end of the planned outage.

attributes.name: metersAffected
attributes.documentation: The updated number of meters affected by the outage as reported by the OMS within the utility.  It is assumed this number will be updated repeatedly until the full outage is resolved.

attributes.name: originalCustomersServed
attributes.documentation: the total number of customers that are served in the area (both outaged and not outaged).

attributes.name: originalMetersAffected
attributes.documentation: The original number of meters that were affected as reported by the OMS within the utility. That is, this is the total number of meters that were out at the beginning of the outage.

attributes.name: outageKind
attributes.documentation: Defines if the outage has been verified or is only estimated

attributes.name: statusKind
attributes.documentation: defines the status of the crew as in dispatched or arrived, etc.

As such it is treated as a forced outage and is probably classified as "trouble" with a Trouble Ticket as well as a work/service order.  The primary difference between this and an unplanned outage is the reason for the outage.  If an animal caused this and perished as a result, the utility may have other actions that are required to be taken by the EPA or other groups with whom the utility has an agreement.

literals.documentation: the outage may not be real since it has not been verified - it is only thought to be an outage.

literals.name: partiallyRestored
literals.documentation: Some of the usage points affected by the outage have been restored but other usage points are still out of power.

literals.name: restored
literals.documentation: All usage points associated with the outage have been restored

literals.name: closed
literals.documentation: The outage has been fully restored, the crews have been released and the outage is shown as closed

attributes.name: reason
attributes.documentation: The reason for the planned outage.

classes.name: PlannedOutageNotification
classes.documentation: This class will be used to generate call ahead lists for customers who will be affected by a planned outage.

classes.name: RevisionHistory
classes.documentation: History of changes made to a switching plan step after the switching plan has been approved.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of change, either void or added.

attributes.name: revisionAuthor
attributes.documentation: Person who made the change

attributes.name: revisionDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time of the change

attributes.name: revisionReason
attributes.documentation: Reason for making the change

classes.name: RevisionKind
classes.documentation: List of the kinds of revisions that can be made to a SwitchingStep.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform

classes.name: SwitchingEvent
classes.documentation: Event indicating the completion (success or fail) of any switching action (jumper action, cut action, tag action, etc).  The switching action may or may not be a consequential event in response to a request to complete the action.

classes.name: SwitchingOrder
classes.documentation: Transmits a switching plan to a crew in order for the plan to be executed.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.documentation: Free-form comment associated with the switching order.

attributes.name: plannedExecutionInterval
attributes.documentation: The planned start and end time for the switching order.

classes.name: SwitchingPlanRequest
classes.documentation: A document used to request that a switching plan be created for a particular purpose.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.documentation: Free-form text to describe the request

attributes.name: equipmentToBeIsolated
attributes.documentation: free-form list of the equipment to be isolated by the switching

attributes.name: forwardSwitchingDateTimeInterval
attributes.documentation: The date when the switching to isolate equipment is performed.

attributes.name: groundingPoints
attributes.documentation: free-form list of equipment to be grounded or other actions to be taken in order to accomplish the required grounding.

attributes.name: isolationArea
attributes.documentation: free-form description of the area to be isolated by the switching

attributes.name: isolationPoints
attributes.documentation: free-form list of equipment to be operated or other actions to be taken in order to accomplish the required isolation.

attributes.name: outageDateTimeInterval
attributes.documentation: The window of time during which one or more customers will be de-energized during execution of the switching plan.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.documentation: The purpose of this switching plan request.

attributes.name: reverseSwitchingDateTimeInterval
attributes.documentation: The date when the switching to energize equipment is performed.

attributes.name: switchingRequestDetails
attributes.documentation: The details of this switching plan request.

classes.name: SwitchingStep
classes.documentation: Atomic switching step; can be part of a switching step group, or part of a switching plan.

attributes.name: isFreeSequence
attributes.documentation: For a step, if isFreeSequence is set to false or is not specified, all of the steps in the group must be executed in the order defined by the sequenceNumber attribute. The sequenceNumber for a step has a different meaning when there are two or more sequential steps that have the isFreeSequence attribute set to true. Execution must still be performed in sequenceNumber order until a set of two or more steps that have isFreeSequence set to true is encountered. In this case, these steps can be executed in any sequence, until a step is encountered that has isFreeSequence set to false. All of the steps preceding this step must be executed before the step can be executed.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: Order of this activity in the sequence of activities within the switching plan.

attributes.name: subStepSequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: Supports compound switching steps that are made up of several sub steps.

classes.name: TroubleOrder
classes.documentation: Trouble order sends an incident to a crew to initiate a response to an unplanned outage.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.documentation: Free-form comment associated with the trouble order.

attributes.name: plannedExecutionInterval
attributes.documentation: The planned start and end time for the trouble order.

classes.name: VerificationAction
classes.documentation: Verification of a switch position or other condition as a switching step

attributes.name: verificationCondition
attributes.documentation: freeform description of the condition to be verified

classes.name: ClearanceAction
classes.documentation: Action on clearance document as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Clearance action to perform.

classes.name: ClearanceActionKind
classes.documentation: Type of clearance action.

classes.name: ClearanceDocument
classes.documentation: Safety document used to authorise work on conducting equipment in the field. Tagged equipment is not allowed to be operated.

attributes.name: mustBeDeenergised
attributes.documentation: If true, the equipment must be deenergised.

attributes.name: mustBeGrounded
attributes.documentation: If true, the equipment must be grounded.

classes.name: CutAction
classes.documentation: Action on cut as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform.

classes.name: EnergySourceAction
classes.documentation: Action on energy source as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform.

classes.name: FieldSafetySupervisor
classes.documentation: Crew member on work site responsible for all local safety measures for the work crew doing maintenance, construction and repair in a substation or on a power line/cable.

classes.name: GroundAction
classes.documentation: Action on ground as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform.

classes.name: GenericAction
classes.documentation: An arbitrary switching step.

classes.name: Incident
classes.documentation: Description of a problem in the field that may be reported in a trouble ticket or come from another source. It may have to do with an outage.

attributes.name: cause
attributes.documentation: Cause of this incident.

classes.name: JumperAction
classes.documentation: Action on jumper as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform.

classes.name: OperationalTag
classes.documentation: Operational tag placed on a power system resource or asset in the context of switching plan execution or other work in the field.

classes.name: OperationalRestriction
classes.documentation:
A document that can be associated with equipment to describe any sort of restrictions compared with the original manufacturer's specification or with the usual operational practice e.g. temporary maximum loadings, maximum switching current, do not operate if bus couplers are open, etc.
In the UK, for example, if a breaker or switch ever mal-operates, this is reported centrally and utilities use their asset systems to identify all the installed devices of the same manufacturer's type. They then apply operational restrictions in the operational systems to warn operators of potential problems. After appropriate inspection and maintenance, the operational restrictions may be removed.

attributes.name: activePeriod
attributes.documentation: Interval during which this restriction is applied.

attributes.name: restrictedValue
attributes.documentation: Restricted (new) value; includes unit of measure and potentially multiplier.

classes.name: OperationalUpdatedRating
classes.documentation: Lowered capability because of deterioration or inadequacy (sometimes referred to as derating or partial outage) or other kind of operational rating change.

attributes.name: changeType
attributes.documentation: Type of operational updated rating, e.g. a derate, a rerate or a return to normal.

classes.name: OperationsSafetySupervisor
classes.documentation: Operator with responsibility that the work in high voltage installation is executed in a safe manner and according to safety regulation.

classes.name: UnplannedOutage
classes.documentation:
Document describing the consequence of an unplanned outage in a part of the electrical network. For the purposes of this model, an unplanned outage refers to a state where energy is not delivered; such as, customers out of service, a street light is not served, etc.
A unplanned outage may be created upon:
- impacts the SAIDI calculation
- a breaker trip,
- a fault indicator status change,
- a meter event indicating customer outage,
- a reception of one or more customer trouble calls, or
- an operator command, reflecting information obtained from the field crew.
Outage restoration may be performed using a switching plan which complements the outage information with detailed switching activities, including the relationship to the crew and work.

attributes.name: cause
attributes.documentation:
The cause of this outage.  This is the cause that is used to present to external entities.  That is, the cause is weather, equipment failure, etc.
Note: At present, this is a free string text; it could be replaced with an enumeration in the future.

attributes.name: causeKind
attributes.documentation: The possible cause that could be associated with this unplanned outage.

attributes.name: reportedStartTime
attributes.documentation: The earliest start time of the Outage - as reported by some system or individual

classes.name: OutagePlan
classes.documentation: Document containing the definition of planned outages of equipment and/or usage points. It will reference switching plans that are used to execute the planned outage.

attributes.name: approvedDateTime
attributes.documentation: The date and time the outage plan was approved

attributes.name: cancelledDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and Time the planned outage was canceled.

attributes.name: plannedPeriod
attributes.documentation: planned start and end time of the planned outage.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.documentation: Purpose of  this outage plan, such as whether it is to replace equipment or perform maintenance or repairs or to reconfigure network topology.

classes.name: PSREvent
classes.documentation: Event recording the change in operational status of a power system resource (PSR); may be for an event that has already occurred or for a planned activity.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of event.

classes.name: PSREventKind
classes.documentation: Kind of power system resource (PSR) event.

literals.name: inService
literals.documentation: Power system resource state change to in service.

literals.name: outOfService
literals.documentation: Power system resource state change to out of service.

literals.name: pendingAdd
literals.documentation: Power system resource state change to pending add.

literals.name: pendingRemove
literals.documentation: Power system resource state change to pending remove.

literals.name: pendingReplace
literals.documentation: Power system resource state change to pending replace.

literals.name: other
literals.documentation: Other power system resource state change.

literals.name: unknown
literals.documentation: Unknown power system resource state change.

classes.name: SafetyDocument
classes.documentation: Document restricting or authorising works on electrical equipment (for example a permit to work, sanction for test, limitation of access, or certificate of isolation), defined based upon organisational practices.

attributes.name: issuedDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time this safety document has been issued.

attributes.name: releasedDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time this safety document has been released.

classes.name: ServicePointOutageSummary
classes.documentation: Summary counts of service points affected by an outage. These counts are sometimes referred to as total and critical customer count.

attributes.name: criticalCount
attributes.documentation: Number of critical service (delivery) points affected by an outage.

attributes.name: totalCount
attributes.documentation: Number of all service (delivery) points affected by an outage.

classes.name: SwitchAction
classes.documentation: Action on switch as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Switching action to perform.

classes.name: SwitchActionKind
classes.documentation: Kind of action on switch.

classes.name: SwitchingPlan
classes.documentation:
A sequence of grouped or atomic steps intended to:
- de-energise equipment or part of the network for safe work, and/or
- bring back in service previously de-energised equipment or part of the network.

attributes.name: approvedDateTime
attributes.documentation: The date and time the switching plan was approved

attributes.name: cancelledDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and Time the switching plan was cancelled.

attributes.name: plannedPeriod
attributes.documentation: the planned start and end times for the switching plan.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.documentation: Purpose of  this plan, such as whether it is to move the state from normal to some abnormal condition, or to restore the normal state after an abnormal condition, or to perform some kind of optimisation such as correction of overload, voltage control, etc.

attributes.name: rank
attributes.documentation: Ranking in comparison to other switching plans.

classes.name: SwitchingAction
classes.documentation: Atomic switching action.

attributes.name: executedDateTime
attributes.documentation: Actual date and time of this switching step.

attributes.name: issuedDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time when the crew was given the instruction to execute the action; not applicable if the action is performed by operator remote control.

attributes.name: phases
attributes.documentation: Phases of the Switching Action

attributes.name: plannedDateTime
attributes.documentation: Planned date and time of this switching step.

classes.name: SwitchingStepGroup
classes.documentation: A logical step, grouping atomic switching steps that are important to distinguish when they may change topology (e.g. placing a jumper between two cuts).

attributes.name: description
attributes.documentation: Descriptive information concerning the switching step group.

attributes.name: isFreeSequence
attributes.documentation: If true, the sequence number serves for presentation purposes only, and the activity itself may be executed at any time.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.documentation: Describes the overall purpose of the steps in this switching step group.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: Order of this activity in the sequence of activities within the switching plan.

classes.name: TagAction
classes.documentation: Action on operation tag as a switching step.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of tag action.

classes.name: TagActionKind
classes.documentation: Kind of action on tag.

classes.name: TempEquipActionKind
classes.documentation: Kind of action on temporary equipment (such as cut, jumper, ground, energy source).

literals.name: place
literals.documentation: Place the jumper (close) or the cut (open).

literals.name: remove
literals.documentation: Remove the jumper (open) or the cut (close).

literals.name: connect
literals.documentation: Connect the temp equipment to its terminal

literals.name: disconnect
literals.documentation: Disconnect the temp equipment from its terminal

subPackages.name: Assets
subPackages.documentation: This package contains the core information classes that support asset management applications that deal with the physical and lifecycle aspects of various network resources (as opposed to power system resource models defined in IEC61970::Wires package, which support network applications).

classes.name: AnalyticKind
classes.documentation: Possible kinds of analytics.

classes.name: AssetGroupKind
classes.documentation: Possible kinds of asset groups.

literals.name: analysisGroup
literals.documentation: Group is used for analysis purposes.

literals.name: inventoryGroup
literals.documentation: Group is used for inventory purposes.

literals.name: complianceGroup
literals.documentation: Group is used for compliance purposes.

literals.name: functionalGroup
literals.documentation: Group is used for functional purposes, for example assets which are grouped together because they are part of a for a particular function - such as a group of feeders.

classes.name: AcceptanceTest
classes.documentation: Acceptance test for assets.

attributes.name: dateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time the asset was last tested using the 'type' of test and yielding the current status in 'success' attribute.

attributes.name: success
attributes.documentation: True if asset has passed acceptance test and may be placed in or is in service. It is set to false if asset is removed from service and is required to be tested again before being placed back in service, possibly in a new location. Since asset may go through multiple tests during its lifecycle, the date of each acceptance test may be recorded in 'Asset.ActivityRecord.status.dateTime'.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of test or group of tests that was conducted on 'dateTime'.

classes.name: Analytic
classes.documentation: An algorithm or calculation for making an assessment about an asset or asset grouping for lifecycle decision making.

attributes.name: bestValue
attributes.documentation: Value that indicates best possible numeric value.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of analytic this analytic is.

attributes.name: scaleKind
attributes.documentation: The scoring scale kind.

attributes.name: worstValue
attributes.documentation: Value that indicates worst possible numeric value.

classes.name: InspectionDataSet
classes.documentation: Documents the result of one inspection, for a given attribute of an asset.

attributes.name: locationCondition
attributes.documentation: Description of the conditions of the location where the asset resides.

classes.name: AnalyticScore
classes.documentation: An indicative scoring by an analytic that can be used to characterize the health of or the risk associated with one or more assets.  The analytic score reflects the results of an execution of an analytic against an asset or group of assets.

attributes.name: calculationDateTime
attributes.documentation: Timestamp of when the score was calculated.

attributes.name: effectiveDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date-time for when the score applies.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Asset health score value.

classes.name: MaintenanceDataSet
classes.documentation: The result of a maintenance activity, a type of Procedure, for a given attribute of an asset.

attributes.name: conditionAfter
attributes.documentation: Condition of asset just following maintenance procedure.

attributes.name: conditionBefore
attributes.documentation: Description of the condition of the asset just prior to maintenance being performed.

attributes.name: maintCode
attributes.documentation: Code for the type of maintenance performed.

classes.name: Asset
classes.documentation: Tangible resource of the utility, including power system equipment, various end devices, cabinets, buildings, etc. For electrical network equipment, the role of the asset is defined through PowerSystemResource and its subclasses, defined mainly in the Wires model (refer to IEC61970-301 and model package IEC61970::Wires). Asset description places emphasis on the physical characteristics of the equipment fulfilling that role.

attributes.name: acceptanceTest
attributes.documentation: Information on acceptance test.

attributes.name: critical
attributes.documentation: True if asset is considered critical for some reason (for example, a pole with critical attachments).

attributes.name: electronicAddress
attributes.documentation: Electronic address.

attributes.name: initialCondition
attributes.documentation: Condition of asset at last baseline. Examples include new, rebuilt, overhaul required, other. Refer to inspection data for information on the most current condition of the asset.

attributes.name: initialLossOfLife
attributes.documentation:
Percentage of initial life expectancy that has been lost as of the last life expectancy baseline. Represents 
(initial life expectancy - current life expectancy) / initial life expectancy.

attributes.name: inUseDate
attributes.documentation: In use dates for this asset.

attributes.name: inUseState
attributes.documentation: Indication of whether asset is currently deployed (in use), ready to be put into use or not available for use.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of asset. Used in description of asset components in asset instance templates.

attributes.name: lifecycleDate
attributes.documentation:
<was lifecycle>
Lifecycle dates for this asset.

attributes.name: lifecycleState
attributes.documentation: Current lifecycle state of asset.

attributes.name: lotNumber
attributes.documentation: Lot number for this asset. Even for the same model and version number, many assets are manufactured in lots.

attributes.name: position
attributes.documentation: Position of asset or asset component. May often be in relation to other assets or components.

attributes.name: purchasePrice
attributes.documentation: Purchase price of asset.

attributes.name: retiredReason
attributes.documentation: Reason asset retired.

attributes.name: serialNumber
attributes.documentation: Serial number of this asset.

attributes.name: status
attributes.documentation: Status of this asset.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Utility-specific classification of Asset and its subtypes, according to their corporate standards, practices, and existing IT systems (e.g., for management of assets, maintenance, work, outage, customers, etc.).

attributes.name: utcNumber
attributes.documentation: Uniquely tracked commodity (UTC) number.

classes.name: AggregateScore
classes.documentation: An aggregated indicative scoring by an analytic, which is based on other analytic scores, that can be used to characterize the health of or the risk associated with one or more assets.

classes.name: AssetContainer
classes.documentation: Asset that is aggregation of other assets such as conductors, transformers, switchgear, land, fences, buildings, equipment, vehicles, etc.

classes.name: AssetGroup
classes.documentation: A grouping of assets created for a purpose such as fleet analytics, inventory or compliance management.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of asset group this asset group is.

classes.name: AssetFunction
classes.documentation: Function performed by an asset.

attributes.name: configID
attributes.documentation: Configuration specified for this function.

attributes.name: firmwareID
attributes.documentation: Firmware version.

attributes.name: hardwareID
attributes.documentation: Hardware version.

attributes.name: password
attributes.documentation: Password needed to access this function.

attributes.name: programID
attributes.documentation: Name of program.

classes.name: AssetDeployment
classes.documentation: Deployment of asset deployment in a power system resource role.

attributes.name: breakerApplication
attributes.documentation: Type of network role breaker is playing in this deployment (applies to breaker assets only).

attributes.name: deploymentDate
attributes.documentation: Dates of asset deployment.

attributes.name: deploymentState
attributes.documentation: Current deployment state of asset.

attributes.name: facilityKind
attributes.documentation: Kind of facility (like substation or pole or building or plant or service center) at which asset deployed.

attributes.name: likelihoodOfFailure
attributes.documentation: Likelihood of asset failure on a scale of 1(low) to 100 (high).

attributes.name: transformerApplication
attributes.documentation: Type of network role transformer is playing in this deployment (applies to transformer assets only).

classes.name: AssetInfo
classes.documentation:
Set of attributes of an asset, representing typical datasheet information of a physical device that can be instantiated and shared in different data exchange contexts:
- as attributes of an asset instance (installed or in stock)
- as attributes of an asset model (product by a manufacturer)
- as attributes of a type asset (generic type of an asset as used in designs/extension planning).

classes.name: TestDataSet
classes.documentation: Test results, usually obtained by a lab or other independent organisation.

attributes.name: conclusion
attributes.documentation: Conclusion drawn from test results.

attributes.name: specimenID
attributes.documentation: Identifier of specimen used in inspection or test.

attributes.name: specimenToLabDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time the specimen was received by the lab.

classes.name: AssetLocationHazard
classes.documentation: Potential hazard related to the location of an asset. Examples are trees growing under overhead power lines, a park being located by a substation (i.e., children climb fence to recover a ball), a lake near an overhead distribution line (fishing pole/line contacting power lines), dangerous neighbour, etc.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of hazard.

classes.name: AssetHealthEvent
classes.documentation: An asset health-related event that is created by an analytic. The event is a record of a change in asset health.

attributes.name: actionRecommendation
attributes.documentation: Recommendation for action.

attributes.name: actionTimeline
attributes.documentation: Time horizon for action.

attributes.name: effectiveDateTime
attributes.documentation: The date and time when the event is effective.

classes.name: Cabinet
classes.documentation: Enclosure that offers protection to the equipment it contains and/or safety to people/animals outside it.

classes.name: HealthScore
classes.documentation: Score that is indicative of the health of one or more assets.

classes.name: AssetOrganisationRole
classes.documentation: Role an organisation plays with respect to asset.

classes.name: AssetOwner
classes.documentation: Owner of the asset.

classes.name: RiskScore
classes.documentation: Score that is indicative of the risk associated with one or more assets.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: The risk kind, such as CustomerRisk, FinancialRisk, SafetyRisk, etc.

classes.name: AssetTestLab
classes.documentation: Test lab that performs various types of testing related to assets.

classes.name: AssetUser
classes.documentation: Organisation that is a user of the asset.

classes.name: DuctBank
classes.documentation: A duct contains individual wires in the layout as specified with associated wire spacing instances; number of them gives the number of conductors in this duct.

attributes.name: circuitCount
attributes.documentation: Number of circuits in duct bank. Refer to associations between a duct (ConductorAsset) and an ACLineSegment to understand which circuits are in which ducts.

classes.name: AssetTestSampleTaker
classes.documentation: Identity of person/organization that took sample.

classes.name: FACTSDevice
classes.documentation: FACTS device asset.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of FACTS device.

classes.name: ComMedia
classes.documentation: Communication media such as fibre optic cable, power-line, telephone, etc.

classes.name: Bushing
classes.documentation: Bushing asset.

classes.name: Facility
classes.documentation: A facility may contain buildings, storage facilities, switching facilities, power generation, manufacturing facilities, maintenance facilities, etc.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of this facility.

classes.name: CorporateStandardKind
classes.documentation: Kind of corporate standard.

literals.name: standard
literals.documentation: Asset model is used as corporate standard.

literals.name: underEvaluation
literals.documentation: Asset model usage is under evaluation.

literals.name: other
literals.documentation: Other kind of corporate standard for the asset model.

classes.name: DiagnosisDataSet
classes.documentation: The result of a problem (typically an asset failure) diagnosis. Contains complete information like what might be received from a lab doing forensic analysis of a failed asset.

attributes.name: effect
attributes.documentation: Effect of problem.

attributes.name: failureMode
attributes.documentation: Failuer mode, for example: Failure to Insulate; Failure to conduct; Failure to contain oil; Failure to provide ground plane; Other.

attributes.name: finalCause
attributes.documentation: Cause of problem determined during diagnosis.

attributes.name: finalCode
attributes.documentation: Code for diagnosed probem type.

attributes.name: finalOrigin
attributes.documentation: Origin of problem determined during diagnosis.

attributes.name: finalRemark
attributes.documentation: Remarks pertaining to findings during problem diagnosis.

attributes.name: phaseCode
attributes.documentation: Phase(s) diagnosed.

attributes.name: preliminaryCode
attributes.documentation: Code for problem type determined during preliminary assessment.

attributes.name: preliminaryDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time preliminary assessment of problem was performed.

attributes.name: preliminaryRemark
attributes.documentation: Remarks pertaining to preliminary assessment of problem.

attributes.name: rootCause
attributes.documentation: Root cause of problem determined during diagnosis.

attributes.name: rootOrigin
attributes.documentation: Root origin of problem determined during diagnosis.

attributes.name: rootRemark
attributes.documentation: Remarks pertaining to root cause findings during problem diagnosis.

classes.name: FailureEvent
classes.documentation: An event where an asset has failed to perform its functions within specified parameters. This class is intended to reflect the failure itself. Additional information resulting from forensic analysis could be captured by a diagnosis data set.

attributes.name: breakerFailureReason
attributes.documentation: Reason for breaker failure.

attributes.name: corporateCode
attributes.documentation: Code for asset failure.

attributes.name: failureClassification
attributes.documentation: Classification of failure.

attributes.name: failureDateTime
attributes.documentation: Time and date of asset failure.

attributes.name: failureIsolationMethod
attributes.documentation: How the asset failure was isolated from the system.

attributes.name: failureMode
attributes.documentation: What asset failed to be able to do.

attributes.name: faultLocatingMethod
attributes.documentation: The method used for locating the faulted part of the asset. For example, cable options include: Cap Discharge-Thumping, Bridge Method, Visual Inspection, Other.

attributes.name: location
attributes.documentation: Failure location on an object.

attributes.name: rootCause
attributes.documentation: Root cause of asset failure.

attributes.name: transformerFailureReason
attributes.documentation: Reason for transformer failure.

classes.name: FailureIsolationMethodKind
classes.documentation: How the failure has been isolated.

literals.name: burnedInTheClear
literals.documentation: Isolated by equipment burning in the clear.

classes.name: LifecycleDate
classes.documentation: Dates for asset lifecycle state changes. May have multiple lifecycle dates for this device and a compound type allows a query to return multiple dates.

attributes.name: installationDate
attributes.documentation: Date current installation was completed, which may not be the same as the in-service date. Asset may have been installed at other locations previously. Ignored if asset is (1) not currently installed (e.g., stored in a depot) or (2) not intended to be installed (e.g., vehicle, tool).

attributes.name: manufacturedDate
attributes.documentation: Date the asset was manufactured.

attributes.name: purchaseDate
attributes.documentation: Date the asset was purchased. Note that even though an asset may have been purchased, it may not have been received into inventory at the time of purchase.

attributes.name: receivedDate
attributes.documentation: Date the asset was received and first placed into inventory.

attributes.name: removalDate
attributes.documentation: Date when the asset was last removed from service. Ignored if (1) not intended to be in service, or (2) currently in service.

attributes.name: retiredDate
attributes.documentation: Date the asset is permanently retired from service and may be scheduled for disposal. Ignored if asset is (1) currently in service, or (2) permanently removed from service.

classes.name: Maintainer
classes.documentation: Organisation that maintains assets.

classes.name: FinancialInfo
classes.documentation: Various current financial properties associated with a particular asset. Historical properties may be determined by ActivityRecords associated with the asset.

attributes.name: account
attributes.documentation: The account to which this actual material item is charged.

attributes.name: actualPurchaseCost
attributes.documentation: The actual purchase cost of this particular asset.

attributes.name: costDescription
attributes.documentation: Description of the cost.

attributes.name: costType
attributes.documentation: Type of cost to which this Material Item belongs.

attributes.name: financialValue
attributes.documentation: Value of asset as of 'valueDateTime'.

attributes.name: plantTransferDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time asset's financial value was put in plant for regulatory accounting purposes (e.g., for rate base calculations). This is sometime referred to as the "in-service date".

attributes.name: purchaseDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time asset was purchased.

attributes.name: purchaseOrderNumber
attributes.documentation: Purchase order identifier.

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.documentation: The quantity of the asset if per unit length, for example conductor.

attributes.name: valueDateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time at which the financial value was last established.

subPackages.name: Metering
subPackages.documentation: This package contains the core information classes that support end device applications with specialized classes for metering and premises area network devices, and remote reading functions. These classes are generally associated with the point where a service is delivered to the customer.

classes.name: AccumulationKind
classes.documentation: Kind of accumulation behaviour for read / measured values from individual end points.

literals.name: none
literals.documentation: Not applicable, or implied by the unit of measure.

literals.name: bulkQuantity
literals.documentation:
A value from a register which represents the bulk quantity of a commodity. This quantity is computed as the integral of the commodity usage rate. This value is typically used as the basis for the dial reading at the meter, and as a result, will roll over upon reaching a maximum dial value. 
Note 1: With the metering system, the roll-over behaviour typically implies a roll-under behavior so that the value presented is always a positive value (e.g. unsigned integer or positive decimal.) However, when communicating data between enterprise applications a negative value might occur in a case such as net metering.
Note 2: A 'bulkQuantity' refers primarily to the dial reading and not the consumption over a specific period of time.

literals.name: continuousCumulative
literals.documentation:
The sum of the previous billing period values and the present period value.
Note: 'continuousCumulative' is commonly used in conjunction with 'demand', and it  would represent the cumulative sum of the previous billing period maximum demand values (as occurring with each demand reset) summed with the present period maximum demand value (which has yet to be reset.)

literals.name: cumulative
literals.documentation:
The sum of the previous billing period values.
Note: 'cumulative' is commonly used in conjunction with “demand.” Each demand reset causes the maximum demand value for the present billing period (since the last demand reset) to accumulate as an accumulative total of all maximum demands. So instead of 'zeroing' the demand register, a demand reset has the effect of adding the present maximum demand to this accumulating total.

literals.name: deltaData
literals.documentation:
The difference between the value at the end of the prescribed interval and the beginning of the interval. This is used for incremental interval data. 
Note: One common application would be for load profile data, another use might be to report the number of events within an interval (such as the number of equipment energisations within the specified period of time.)

literals.name: indicating
literals.documentation:
As if a needle is swung out on the meter face to a value to indicate the current value.
Note: An 'indicating' value is typically measured over hundreds of milliseconds or greater, or may imply a “pusher” mechanism to capture a value. Compare this to 'instantaneous' which is measured over a shorter period of time.

literals.name: summation
literals.documentation:
A form of accumulation which is selective with respect to time. 
Note : 'summation' could be considered a specialisation of 'bulkQuantity' as it selectively accumulates pulses over a timing pattern (while 'bulkQuantity' accumulates pulses all of the time).

literals.name: timeDelay
literals.documentation: A form of computation which introduces a time delay characteristic to the data value.

literals.name: instantaneous
literals.documentation:
Typically measured over the fastest period of time allowed by the definition of the metric (usually milliseconds or tens of milliseconds.)
Note: 'instantaneous' was moved to attribute #3 in Ed.2 of IEC 61968-9, from attribute #1 in Ed.1 of IEC 61968-9.

literals.name: latchingQuantity
literals.documentation:
When this description is applied to a metered value, it implies that the value is a time-independent cumulative quantity much like a 'bulkQuantity', except that it latches upon the maximum value upon reaching that value. Any additional accumulation (positive or negative) is discarded until a reset occurs. 
Note: A 'latchingQuantity' may also occur in the downward direction – upon reaching a minimum value. The terms 'maximum' or 'minimum' (for 'aggregate') will usually be included when this type of accumulation behaviour is present. 
When this description is applied to an encoded value (UOM= 'Code'), it implies that the value has one or more bits which are latching. The condition that caused the bit to be set may have long since evaporated.
In either case, the timestamp that accompanies the value may not coincide with the moment the value was initially set.
In both cases a system will need to perform an operation to clear the latched value.

literals.name: boundedQuantity
literals.documentation: A time-independent cumulative quantity much like a 'bulkQuantity' or a 'latchingQuantity', except that the accumulation stops at the maximum or minimum values. When the maximum is reached, any additional positive accumulation is discarded, but negative accumulation may be accepted (thus lowering the counter.) Likewise, when the negative bound is reached, any additional negative accumulation is discarded, but positive accumulation is accepted (thus increasing the counter.)

literals.name: electricityPrimaryMetered
literals.documentation: It is possible for a meter to be outfitted with an external VT and/or CT. The meter might not be aware of these devices, and the display not compensate for their presence. Ultimately, when these scalars are applied, the value that represents the service value is called the “primary metered” value. The “index” in sub-category 3 mirrors those of sub-category 0.

literals.name: coolingFluid

literals.name: autonomousDst

classes.name: FlowDirectionKind
classes.documentation: Kind of flow direction for reading/measured  values proper to some commodities such as, for example, energy, power, demand.

literals.name: forward
literals.documentation: "Delivered," or "Imported" as defined 61968-2. Forward Active Energy is a positive kWh value as one would naturally expect to find as energy is supplied by the utility and consumed at the service. Forward Reactive Energy is a positive VArh value as one would naturally expect to find in the presence of inductive loading. In polyphase metering, the forward energy register is incremented when the sum of the phase energies is greater than zero:

literals.name: lagging
literals.documentation:
Typically used to describe that a power factor is lagging the reference value. 
Note 1: When used to describe VA, “lagging” describes a form of measurement where reactive power is considered in all four quadrants, but real power is considered only in quadrants I and IV.
Note 2: When used to describe power factor, the term “Lagging” implies that the PF is negative. The term “lagging” in this case takes the place of the negative sign. If a signed PF value is to be passed by the data producer, then the direction of flow enumeration zero (none) should be used in order to avoid the possibility of creating an expression that employs a double negative. The data consumer should be able to tell from the sign of the data if the PF is leading or lagging. This principle is analogous to the concept that “Reverse” energy is an implied negative value, and to publish a negative reverse value would be ambiguous.
Note 3: Lagging power factors typically indicate inductive loading.

literals.name: leading
literals.documentation:
Typically used to describe that a power factor is leading the reference value.
Note: Leading power factors typically indicate capacitive loading.

literals.name: net
literals.documentation:
|Forward| - |Reverse|, See 61968-2.

Note: In some systems, the value passed as a “net” value could become negative. In other systems the value passed as a “net” value is always a positive number, and rolls-over and rolls-under as needed.

literals.name: q1plusQ2
literals.documentation: Reactive positive quadrants. (The term “lagging” is preferred.)

literals.name: q1plusQ4
literals.documentation: Quadrants 1 and 4 usually represent forward active energy

literals.name: q2plusQ3
literals.documentation: Quadrants 2 and 3 usually represent reverse active energy

literals.name: q3plusQ4
literals.documentation: Reactive negative quadrants. (The term “leading” is preferred.)

literals.name: reverse
literals.documentation: Reverse Active Energy is equivalent to "Received," or "Exported" as defined in 61968-2. Reverse Active Energy is a positive kWh value as one would expect to find when energy is backfed by the service onto the utility network. Reverse Reactive Energy is a positive VArh value as one would expect to find in the presence of capacitive loading and a leading Power Factor. In polyphase metering, the reverse energy register is incremented when the sum of the phase energies is less than zero: Note: The value passed as a reverse value is always a positive value. It is understood by the label “reverse” that it represents negative flow.

literals.name: total
literals.documentation: |Forward| + |Reverse|, See 61968-2. The sum of the commodity in all quadrants Q1+Q2+Q3+Q4. In polyphase metering, the total energy register is incremented when the absolute value of the sum of the phase energies is greater than zero:

literals.name: totalByPhase
literals.documentation: In polyphase metering, the total by phase energy register is incremented when the sum of the absolute values of the phase energies is greater than zero: In single phase metering, the formulas for “Total” and “Total by phase” collapse to the same expression. For communication purposes however, the “Total” enumeration should be used with single phase meter data.

classes.name: MacroPeriodKind
classes.documentation: Kind of macro period for calculations on read / measured values.

literals.name: billingPeriod
literals.documentation: Captured during the billing period starting at midnight of the first day of the billing period (as defined by the billing cycle day). If during the current billing period, it specifies a period from the start of the current billing period until "now".

literals.name: daily
literals.documentation: Daily period starting at midnight. If for the current day, this specifies the time from midnight to "now".

literals.name: monthly
literals.documentation: Monthly period starting at midnight on the first day of the month. If within the current month, this specifies the period from the start of the month until "now."

literals.name: seasonal
literals.documentation: A season of time spanning multiple months. E.g. "Summer," "Spring," "Fall," and "Winter" based cycle. If within the current season, it specifies the period from the start of the current season until "now."

literals.name: weekly
literals.documentation: Weekly period starting at midnight on the first day of the week and ending the instant before midnight the last day of the week. If within the current week, it specifies the period from the start of the week until "now."

literals.name: specifiedPeriod
literals.documentation: For the period defined by the start and end of the TimePeriod element in the message.

classes.name: MeasurementKind

literals.name: apparentPowerFactor

literals.name: currentAngle
literals.documentation: A phase current zerocross timing measurement releative to a reference voltage zerocross

literals.name: currentImbalance
literals.documentation: A measurement of the departure of a phase current relative to the average current of all phases

literals.name: date
literals.documentation: A measurement of the date and/or time in a clock, or a time stamp indicating when data was captured, when a maximum or minimum occurred, or to commemorate some other important aspect of a measurement

literals.name: demand
literals.documentation: The measurement of maximum power flow which is computed as energy usage over time, the dimensions of which are defined by a tariff

literals.name: distance
literals.documentation: A linear distance or range radius

literals.name: distortionVoltAmp
literals.documentation: A measurement in which a V<sup>2</sup> I<sup>2</sup> term has both real and reactive components removed leaving only distortion. For example, distortion VAh = Sqrt( (V<sup>2</sup>h)(I<sup>2</sup>h) – (Wh)<sup>2</sup> – (VArh)<sup>2</sup>)

literals.name: energization
literals.documentation: Pertaining to the presence of voltage

literals.name: energy
literals.documentation: Scalar quantity which may be increased or decreased in a system when it receives or produces work, respectively

literals.name: energizationLoadSide
literals.documentation: Measuring the presence or absence of voltage on the load side of an electricity meter

literals.name: ieee1366ASAI
literals.documentation: A measurement of IEEE-1366 Average Service Availability Index

literals.name: ieee1366ASIDI
literals.documentation: A measurement of the IEEE-1366 Average Service Interruption Duration Index

literals.name: ieee1366ASIFI

literals.name: ieee1366CAIFI

literals.name: ieee1366CEMSMIn

literals.name: ieee1366CTAIDI

literals.name: ieee1366MAIFI
literals.documentation: A measurement of the IEEE-1366 Momentary Average Interruption Frequency Index

literals.name: ieee1366MAIFIe
literals.documentation: A measurement of the IEEE-1366 Momentary Average event Interruption Frequency Index

literals.name: ieee1366SAIDI
