literals.name: ieee1366SAIFI
literals.documentation: IEEE-1366 System Average Interruption Frequency Index

literals.name: lineLoss
literals.documentation: An energy, power, voltage, or current loss attributed to transmission or distribution line impedance

literals.name: loss
literals.documentation: A quantity lost due to “technical” reasons (such as line loss) or “non-technical” reasons (such as theft.)

literals.name: negativeSequence
literals.documentation: A quantity that has a rotation sequence which is opposite to that of the power system

literals.name: phasorPowerFactor

classes.documentation: Kind of randomisation to be applied to control the timing of end device control commands and/or the definition of demand response and load control events. Value other than 'none' is typically used to mitigate potential deleterious effects of simultaneous operation of multiple devices.

literals.name: start
literals.documentation: Start time of an event or control action affecting one or more multiple devices is randomised.

literals.name: end
literals.documentation: End time of an event or control action affecting one or more devices is randomised to prevent simultaneous operation.

literals.name: startAndEnd
literals.documentation: Both the start time and the end time of an event or control action affecting one or more devices are randomised to prevent simultaneous operation.

literals.name: default
literals.documentation: Randomisation of start and/or end times involving the operation of one or more devices is controlled by default settings for the device(s).

literals.name: none
literals.documentation: Neither the start time nor the end time of an event or control action affecting one or more devices is randomised.

literals.name: connected
literals.documentation: The usage point is connected to the network and able to receive or send the applicable commodity (electricity, gas, water, etc.).

literals.name: physicallyDisconnected
literals.documentation: The usage point has been disconnected from the network at a point upstream of the meter. The usage point is unable to receive or send the applicable commodity (electricity, gas, water, etc.). A physical disconnect is often achieved by utilising a field crew.

literals.name: logicallyDisconnected
literals.documentation: The usage point has been disconnected through operation of a disconnect function within the meter present at the usage point.  The usage point is unable to receive or send the applicable commodity (electricity, gas, water, etc.)  A logical disconnect can often be achieved without utilising a field crew.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.documentation: Duration of the end device control action or the business event that is the subject of the end device control.

attributes.name: durationIndefinite
attributes.documentation: True if 'duration' is indefinite.

attributes.name: interval
attributes.documentation: Start and end time of an interval during which end device control actions are to be executed.

attributes.name: randomisation
attributes.documentation: Kind of randomisation to be applied to the end device control actions to be executed.

classes.name: RationalNumber
classes.documentation: Rational number = 'numerator' / 'denominator'.

attributes.name: denominator
attributes.documentation: Denominator. Value 1 indicates the number is a simple integer.

attributes.name: numerator
attributes.documentation: Numerator.

classes.name: ReadingInterharmonic
classes.documentation: Interharmonics are represented as a rational number 'numerator' / 'denominator', and harmonics are represented using the same mechanism and identified by 'denominator'=1.

attributes.name: denominator
attributes.documentation: Interharmonic denominator. Value 0 means not applicable. Value 2 is used in combination with 'numerator'=1 to represent interharmonic 1/2. Finally, value 1 indicates the harmonic of the order specified with 'numerator'.

attributes.name: numerator
attributes.documentation: Interharmonic numerator. Value 0 means not applicable. Value 1 is used in combination with 'denominator'=2 to represent interharmonic 1/2, and with 'denominator'=1 it represents fundamental frequency. Finally, values greater than 1 indicate the harmonic of that order (e.g., 'numerator'=5 is the fifth harmonic).

classes.name: BaseReading
classes.documentation: Common representation for reading values. Note that a reading value may have multiple qualities, as produced by various systems ('ReadingQuality.source').

attributes.name: reportedDateTime
attributes.documentation: (used only when there are detailed auditing requirements) Date and time at which the reading was first delivered to the metering system.

attributes.name: source
attributes.documentation: System that originally supplied the reading (e.g., customer, AMI system, handheld reading system, another enterprise system, etc.).

attributes.name: timePeriod
attributes.documentation: Start and end of the period for those readings whose type has a time attribute such as 'billing', seasonal' or 'forTheSpecifiedPeriod'.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Value of this reading.

classes.name: Channel
classes.documentation: A single path for the collection or reporting of register values over a period of time. For example, a register which measures forward energy can have two channels, one providing bulk quantity readings and the other providing interval readings of a fixed interval size.

attributes.name: isVirtual
attributes.documentation: If true, the data is being calculated by an enterprise system rather than metered directly.

classes.name: ComFunction
classes.documentation: Communication function of communication equipment or a device such as a meter.

attributes.name: amrAddress
attributes.documentation: Communication ID number (e.g. serial number, IP address, telephone number, etc.) of the AMR module which serves this meter.

attributes.name: amrRouter
attributes.documentation: Communication ID number (e.g. port number, serial number, data collector ID, etc.) of the parent device associated to this AMR module.

attributes.name: direction
attributes.documentation: Kind of communication direction.

attributes.name: technology
attributes.documentation: Kind of communication technology.

classes.name: ComModule
classes.documentation: An asset having communications capabilities that can be paired with a meter or other end device to provide the device with communication ability, through associated communication function. An end device that has communications capabilities through embedded hardware can use that function directly (without the communication module), or combine embedded communication function with additional communication functions provided through an external communication module (e.g. zigbee).

attributes.name: amrSystem
attributes.documentation: Automated meter reading (AMR) system communicating with this com module.

attributes.name: supportsAutonomousDst
attributes.documentation: If true, autonomous daylight saving time (DST) function is supported.

attributes.name: timeZoneOffset
attributes.documentation: Time zone offset relative to GMT for the location of this com module.

classes.name: DemandResponseProgram
classes.documentation: Demand response program.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of demand response program; examples are CPP (critical-peak pricing), RTP (real-time pricing), DLC (direct load control), DBP (demand bidding program), BIP (base interruptible program). Note that possible types change a lot and it would be impossible to enumerate them all.

attributes.name: validityInterval
attributes.documentation: Interval within which the program is valid.

classes.name: EndDeviceAction
classes.documentation: Action/command performed by an end device on a device other than the end device.

attributes.name: command
attributes.documentation: Command text.

attributes.name: duration
attributes.documentation: Amount of time the action of this control is to remain active.

attributes.name: durationIndefinite
attributes.documentation: True if the action of this control is indefinite.

attributes.name: startDateTime
attributes.documentation: Start date and time for action of this control.

classes.name: EndDeviceControl
classes.documentation: Instructs an end device (or an end device group) to perform a specified action.

attributes.name: drProgramLevel
attributes.documentation: Level of a demand response program request, where 0=emergency. Note: Attribute is not defined on DemandResponseProgram as it is not its inherent property (it serves to control it).

attributes.name: drProgramMandatory
attributes.documentation: Whether a demand response program request is mandatory. Note: Attribute is not defined on DemandResponseProgram as it is not its inherent property (it serves to control it).

attributes.name: issuerID
attributes.documentation: Unique identifier of the business entity originating an end device control.

attributes.name: issuerTrackingID
attributes.documentation: Identifier assigned by the initiator (e.g. retail electric provider) of an end device control action to uniquely identify the demand response event, text message, or other subject of the control action. Can be used when cancelling an event or text message request or to identify the originating event or text message in a consequential end device event.

attributes.name: priceSignal
attributes.documentation: (if applicable) Price signal used as parameter for this end device control.

attributes.name: primaryDeviceTiming
attributes.documentation: Timing for the control actions performed on the device identified in the end device control.

attributes.name: reason
attributes.documentation: Reason for the control action that allows to determine how to continue processing. For example, disconnect meter command may require different processing by the receiving system if it has been issued for a network-related reason (protection) or for a payment-related reason.

attributes.name: scheduledInterval
attributes.documentation: (if control has scheduled duration) Date and time interval the control has been scheduled to execute within.

attributes.name: secondaryDeviceTiming
attributes.documentation: Timing for the control actions performed by devices that are responding to event related information sent to the primary device indicated in the end device control.  For example, load control actions performed by a PAN device in response to demand response event information sent to a PAN gateway server.

classes.name: EndDeviceControlType
classes.documentation: Detailed description for a control produced by an end device. Values in attributes allow for creation of recommended codes to be used for identifying end device controls as follows: <type>.<domain>.<subDomain>.<eventOrAction>.

attributes.name: domain
attributes.documentation: High-level nature of the control.

attributes.name: eventOrAction
attributes.documentation: The most specific part of this control type. It is mainly in the form of a verb that gives action to the control that just occurred.

attributes.name: subDomain
attributes.documentation: More specific nature of the control, as a further sub-categorisation of 'domain'.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of physical device from which the control was created. A value of zero (0) can be used when the source is unknown.

classes.name: EndDeviceEvent
classes.documentation: Event detected by a device function associated with the end device.

attributes.name: issuerID
attributes.documentation: Unique identifier of the business entity originating an end device control.

attributes.name: issuerTrackingID
attributes.documentation: Identifier assigned by the initiator (e.g. retail electric provider) of an end device control action to uniquely identify the demand response event, text message, or other subject of the control action. Can be used when cancelling an event or text message request or to identify the originating event or text message in a consequential end device event.

attributes.name: userID
attributes.documentation: (if user initiated) ID of user who initiated this end device event.

classes.name: EndDeviceEventDetail
classes.documentation: Name-value pair, specific to end device events.

attributes.name: name
attributes.documentation: Name.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Value, including unit information.

classes.name: EndDeviceEventType
classes.documentation: Detailed description for an event produced by an end device. Values in attributes allow for creation of recommended codes to be used for identifying end device events as follows: <type>.<domain>.<subDomain>.<eventOrAction>.

attributes.name: domain
attributes.documentation: High-level nature of the event. By properly classifying events by a small set of domain codes, a system can more easily run reports based on the types of events that have occurred or been received.

attributes.name: eventOrAction
attributes.documentation: The most specific part of this event type. It is mainly in the form of a verb that gives action to the event that just occurred.

attributes.name: subDomain
attributes.documentation: More specific nature of the event, as a further sub-categorisation of 'domain'.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of physical device from which the event was created. A value of zero (0) can be used when the source is unknown.

classes.name: EndDeviceFunction
classes.documentation: Function performed by an end device such as a meter, communication equipment, controllers, etc.

attributes.name: enabled
attributes.documentation: True if the function is enabled.

classes.name: EndDeviceGroup
classes.documentation: Abstraction for management of group communications within a two-way AMR system or the data for a group of related end devices. Commands can be issued to all of the end devices that belong to the group using a defined group address and the underlying AMR communication infrastructure. A DERGroup and a PANDeviceGroup is an EndDeviceGroup.

attributes.name: status
attributes.documentation: Current status information relevant to a group.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of this group.

attributes.name: version
attributes.documentation: version of this group

classes.name: EndDeviceInfo
classes.documentation: End device data.

attributes.name: capability
attributes.documentation: Inherent capabilities of the device (i.e., the functions it supports).

attributes.name: isSolidState
attributes.documentation: If true, this is a solid state end device (as opposed to a mechanical or electromechanical device).

attributes.name: phaseCount
attributes.documentation: Number of potential phases the end device supports, typically 0, 1 or 3.

attributes.name: ratedCurrent
attributes.documentation: Rated current.

attributes.name: ratedVoltage
attributes.documentation: Rated voltage.

classes.name: IntervalReading
classes.documentation:
Data captured at regular intervals of time. Interval data could be captured as incremental data, absolute data, or relative data. The source for the data is usually a tariff quantity or an engineering quantity. Data is typically captured in time-tagged, uniform, fixed-length intervals of 5 min, 10 min, 15 min, 30 min, or 60 min.
Note: Interval Data is sometimes also called "Interval Data Readings" (IDR).

classes.name: Meter
classes.documentation: Physical asset that performs the metering role of the usage point. Used for measuring consumption and detection of events.

attributes.name: connectionCategory
attributes.documentation: A code used to specify the connection category, e.g. low voltage, where the meter operates.

attributes.name: formNumber
attributes.documentation: Meter form designation per ANSI C12.10 or other applicable standard. An alphanumeric designation denoting the circuit arrangement for which the meter is applicable and its specific terminal arrangement.

classes.name: MeterMultiplier
classes.documentation: Multiplier applied at the meter.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of multiplier.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Multiplier value.

classes.name: MeterReading
classes.documentation: Set of values obtained from the meter.

attributes.name: isCoincidentTrigger
attributes.documentation: If true, this meter reading is the meter reading for which other coincident meter readings are requested or provided.

attributes.name: valuesInterval
attributes.documentation: Date and time interval of the data items contained within this meter reading.

classes.name: MeterWorkTask
classes.documentation: Work task involving meters.

classes.name: MetrologyRequirement
classes.documentation: A specification of the metering requirements for a particular point within a network.

attributes.name: reason
attributes.documentation: Reason for this metrology requirement being specified.

classes.name: PanDemandResponse
classes.documentation: PAN control used to issue action/command to PAN devices during a demand response/load control event.

attributes.name: appliance
attributes.documentation: Appliance being controlled.

attributes.name: avgLoadAdjustment
attributes.documentation:
Used to define a maximum energy usage limit as a percentage of the client implementations specific average energy usage. The load adjustment percentage is added to 100% creating a percentage limit applied to the client implementations specific average energy usage. A -10% load adjustment percentage will establish an energy usage limit equal to 90% of the client implementations specific average energy usage. Each load adjustment percentage is referenced to the client implementations specific average energy usage. There are no cumulative effects.
The range of this field is -100% to +100% with a resolution of 1. A -100% value equals a total load shed. A +100% value will limit the energy usage to the client implementations specific average energy usage.

attributes.name: cancelControlMode
attributes.documentation: Encoding of cancel control.

attributes.name: cancelDateTime
attributes.documentation: Timestamp when a canceling of the event is scheduled to start.

attributes.name: cancelNow
attributes.documentation: If true, a canceling of the event should start immediately.

attributes.name: coolingOffset
attributes.documentation: Requested offset to apply to the normal cooling setpoint at the time of the start of the event. It represents a temperature change that will be applied to the associated cooling set point. The temperature offsets will be calculated per the local temperature in the thermostat. The calculated temperature will be interpreted as the number of degrees to be added to the cooling set point. Sequential demand response events are not cumulative. The offset shall be applied to the normal setpoint.

attributes.name: coolingSetpoint
attributes.documentation: Requested cooling set point. Temperature set point is typically defined and calculated based on local temperature.

attributes.name: criticalityLevel
attributes.documentation: Level of criticality for the action of this control. The action taken by load control devices for an event can be solely based on this value, or in combination with other load control event fields supported by the device.

attributes.name: dutyCycle
attributes.documentation: Maximum "on" state duty cycle as a percentage of time. For example, if the value is 80, the device would be in an "on" state for 80% of the time for the duration of the action.

attributes.name: enrollmentGroup
attributes.documentation: Provides a mechanism to direct load control actions to groups of PAN devices. It can be used in conjunction with the PAN device types.

attributes.name: heatingOffset
attributes.documentation: Requested offset to apply to the normal heating setpoint at the time of the start of the event. It represents a temperature change that will be applied to the associated heating set point. The temperature offsets will be calculated per the local temperature in the thermostat. The calculated temperature will be interpreted as the number of degrees to be subtracted from the heating set point. Sequential demand response events are not cumulative. The offset shall be applied to the normal setpoint.

attributes.name: heatingSetpoint
attributes.documentation: Requested heating set point. Temperature set point is typically defined and calculated based on local temperature.

classes.name: PanDisplay
classes.documentation: PAN action/command used to issue the displaying of text messages on PAN devices.

attributes.name: confirmationRequired
attributes.documentation: If true, the requesting entity (e.g. retail electric provider) requires confirmation of the successful display of the text message.

attributes.name: priority
attributes.documentation: Priority associated with the text message to be displayed.

attributes.name: textMessage
attributes.documentation: Text to be displayed by a PAN device.

attributes.name: transmissionMode
attributes.documentation: Transmission mode to be used for this PAN display control.

classes.name: PanPricing
classes.documentation: PAN action/command used to issue pricing information to a PAN device.

attributes.name: providerID
attributes.documentation: Unique identifier for the commodity provider.

classes.name: PanPricingDetail
classes.documentation: Detail for a single price command/action.

attributes.name: alternateCostDelivered
attributes.documentation: Alternative measure of the cost of the energy consumed. An example might be the emissions of CO2 for each kWh of electricity consumed providing a measure of the environmental cost.

attributes.name: alternateCostUnit
attributes.documentation: Cost unit for the alternate cost delivered field. One example is kg of CO2 per unit of measure.

attributes.name: currentTimeDate
attributes.documentation: Current time as determined by a PAN device.

attributes.name: generationPrice
attributes.documentation: Price of the commodity measured in base unit of currency per 'unitOfMeasure'.

attributes.name: generationPriceRatio
attributes.documentation: Ratio of 'generationPrice' to the "normal" price chosen by the commodity provider.

attributes.name: price
attributes.documentation: Price of the commodity measured in base unit of currency per 'unitOfMeasure'.

attributes.name: priceRatio
attributes.documentation: Ratio of 'price' to the "normal" price chosen by the commodity provider.

attributes.name: priceTier
attributes.documentation: Pricing tier as chosen by the commodity provider.

attributes.name: priceTierCount
attributes.documentation: Maximum number of price tiers available.

attributes.name: priceTierLabel
attributes.documentation: Label for price tier.

attributes.name: rateLabel
attributes.documentation: Label of the current billing rate specified by commodity provider.

attributes.name: registerTier
attributes.documentation: Register tier accumulating usage information.

attributes.name: unitOfMeasure
attributes.documentation: Defines commodity as well as its base unit of measure.

classes.name: PendingCalculation
classes.documentation: When present, a scalar conversion that needs to be applied to every IntervalReading.value contained in IntervalBlock. This conversion results in a new associated ReadingType, reflecting the true dimensions of IntervalReading values after the conversion.

attributes.name: multiplyBeforeAdd
attributes.documentation: Whether scalars should be applied before adding the 'offset'.

attributes.name: offset
attributes.documentation: (if applicable) Offset to be added as well as multiplication using scalars.

attributes.name: scalarDenominator
attributes.documentation: (if scalar is rational number) When 'IntervalReading.value' is multiplied by 'scalarNumerator' and divided by this value, it causes a unit of measure conversion to occur, resulting in the 'ReadingType.unit'.

attributes.name: scalarFloat
attributes.documentation: (if scalar is floating number) When multiplied with 'IntervalReading.value', it causes a unit of measure conversion to occur, according to the 'ReadingType.unit'.

attributes.name: scalarNumerator
attributes.documentation: (if scalar is integer or rational number)  When the scalar is a simple integer, and this attribute is presented alone and multiplied with 'IntervalReading.value', it causes a unit of measure conversion to occur, resulting in the 'ReadingType.unit'. It is never used in conjunction with 'scalarFloat', only with 'scalarDenominator'.

classes.name: Reading
classes.documentation: Specific value measured by a meter or other asset, or calculated by a system. Each Reading is associated with a specific ReadingType.

attributes.name: position
attributes.documentation: A sequential value representing the relative position within a given time interval.

attributes.name: reason
attributes.documentation: Reason for this reading being taken.

attributes.name: valueMissing
attributes.documentation: The indication of whether or not the quantity of this reading is missing.

classes.name: ReadingQuality
classes.documentation: Quality of a specific reading value or interval reading value. Note that more than one quality may be applicable to a given reading. Typically not used unless problems or unusual conditions occur (i.e., quality for each reading is assumed to be good unless stated otherwise in associated reading quality type). It can also be used with the corresponding reading quality type to indicate that the validation has been performed and succeeded.

attributes.name: comment
attributes.documentation: Elaboration on the quality code.

attributes.name: source
attributes.documentation: System acting as the source of the quality code.

attributes.name: timeStamp
attributes.documentation: Date and time at which the quality code was assigned or ascertained.

classes.name: ReadingQualityType
classes.documentation: Detailed description for a quality of a reading value, produced by an end device or a system. Values in attributes allow for creation of the recommended codes to be used for identifying reading value quality codes as follows: <systemId>.<category>.<subCategory>.

attributes.name: category
attributes.documentation: High-level nature of the reading value quality.

attributes.name: subCategory
attributes.documentation: More specific nature of the reading value quality, as a further sub-categorisation of 'category'.

attributes.name: systemId
attributes.documentation: Identification of the system which has declared the issue with the data or provided commentary on the data.

classes.name: ReadingType
classes.documentation: Detailed description for a type of a reading value. Values in attributes allow for the creation of recommended codes to be used for identifying reading value types as follows: <macroPeriod>.<aggregate>.<measuringPeriod>.<accumulation>.<flowDirection>.<commodity>.<measurementKind>.<interharmonic.numerator>.<interharmonic.denominator>.<argument.numerator>.<argument.denominator>.<tou>.<cpp>.<consumptionTier>.<phases>.<multiplier>.<unit>.<currency>.

attributes.name: accumulation
attributes.documentation: Accumulation behaviour of a reading over time, usually 'measuringPeriod', to be used with individual endpoints (as opposed to 'macroPeriod' and 'aggregate' that are used to describe aggregations of data from individual endpoints).

attributes.name: aggregate
attributes.documentation: Salient attribute of the reading data aggregated from individual endpoints. This is mainly used to define a mathematical operation carried out over 'macroPeriod', but may also be used to describe an attribute of the data when the 'macroPeriod' is not defined.

attributes.name: argument
attributes.documentation:
Argument used to introduce numbers into the unit of measure description where they are needed (e.g., 4 where the measure needs an argument such as CEMI(n=4)). Most arguments used in practice however will be integers (i.e., 'denominator'=1).
Value 0 in 'numerator' and 'denominator' means not applicable.

attributes.name: commodity
attributes.documentation: Commodity being measured.

attributes.name: consumptionTier
attributes.documentation:
In case of common flat-rate pricing for power, in which all purchases are at a given rate, 'consumptionTier'=0. Otherwise, the value indicates the consumption tier, which can be used in conjunction with TOU or CPP pricing.
Consumption tier pricing refers to the method of billing in which a certain "block" of energy is purchased/sold at one price, after which the next block of energy is purchased at another price, and so on, all throughout a defined period. At the start of the defined period, consumption is initially zero, and any usage is measured against the first consumption tier ('consumptionTier'=1). If this block of energy is consumed before the end of the period, energy consumption moves to be reconed against the second consumption tier ('consumptionTier'=2), and so on. At the end of the defined period, the consumption accumulator is reset, and usage within the 'consumptionTier'=1 restarts.

attributes.name: cpp
attributes.documentation: Critical peak period (CPP) bucket the reading value is attributed to. Value 0 means not applicable. Even though CPP is usually considered a specialised form of time of use 'tou', this attribute is defined explicitly for flexibility.

attributes.name: currency
attributes.documentation: Metering-specific currency.

attributes.name: flowDirection
attributes.documentation: Flow direction for a reading where the direction of flow of the commodity is important (for electricity measurements this includes current, energy, power, and demand).

attributes.name: interharmonic
attributes.documentation: Indication of a "harmonic" or "interharmonic" basis for the measurement. Value 0 in 'numerator' and 'denominator' means not applicable.

attributes.name: macroPeriod
attributes.documentation: Time period of interest that reflects how the reading is viewed or captured over a long period of time.

attributes.name: measurementKind
attributes.documentation: Identifies "what" is being measured, as refinement of 'commodity'. When combined with 'unit', it provides detail to the unit of measure. For example, 'energy' with a unit of measure of 'kWh' indicates to the user that active energy is being measured, while with 'kVAh' or 'kVArh', it indicates apparent energy and reactive energy, respectively. 'power' can be combined in a similar way with various power units of measure: Distortion power ('distortionVoltAmperes') with 'kVA' is different from 'power' with 'kVA'.

attributes.name: measuringPeriod
attributes.documentation:
Time attribute inherent or fundamental to the reading value (as opposed to 'macroPeriod' that supplies an "adjective" to describe aspects of a time period with regard to the measurement). It refers to the way the value was originally measured and not to the frequency at which it is reported or presented. For example, an hourly interval of consumption data would have value 'hourly' as an attribute. However in the case of an hourly sampled voltage value, the meterReadings schema would carry the 'hourly' interval size information.
It is common for meters to report demand in a form that is measured over the course of a portion of an hour, while enterprise applications however commonly assume the demand (in kW or kVAr) normalised to 1 hour. The system that receives readings directly from the meter therefore shall perform this transformation before publishing readings for use by the other enterprise systems. The scalar used is chosen based on the block size (not any sub-interval size).

attributes.name: multiplier
attributes.documentation: Metering-specific multiplier.

attributes.name: phases
attributes.documentation: Metering-specific phase code.

attributes.name: tou
attributes.documentation: Time of use (TOU) bucket the reading value is attributed to. Value 0 means not applicable.

attributes.name: unit
attributes.documentation: Metering-specific unit.

classes.name: Register
classes.documentation: A device that indicates or records units of the commodity or other quantity measured.

attributes.name: isVirtual
attributes.documentation: If true, the data it produces is  calculated or measured by a device other than a physical end device/meter. Otherwise, any data streams it produces are measured by the hardware of the end device/meter itself.

attributes.name: leftDigitCount
attributes.documentation: Number of digits (dials on a mechanical meter) to the left of the decimal place; default is normally 5.

attributes.name: rightDigitCount
attributes.documentation: Number of digits (dials on a mechanical meter) to the right of the decimal place.

attributes.name: touTier
attributes.documentation: Clock time interval for register to beging/cease accumulating time of usage (e.g., start at 8:00 am, stop at 5:00 pm).

attributes.name: touTierName
attributes.documentation: Name used for the time of use tier (also known as bin or bucket).  For example, "peak", "off-peak", "TOU Category A", etc.

classes.name: ServiceMultiplier
classes.documentation: Multiplier applied at the usage point.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of multiplier.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Multiplier value.

classes.name: SimpleEndDeviceFunction
classes.documentation: Simple end device function distinguished by 'kind'. Use this class for instances that cannot be represented by another end device function specialisations.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of this function.

classes.name: UsagePoint
classes.documentation: Logical or physical point in the network to which readings or events may be attributed. Used at the place where a physical or virtual meter may be located; however, it is not required that a meter be present.

attributes.name: amiBillingReady
attributes.documentation: Tracks the lifecycle of the metering installation at a usage point with respect to readiness for billing via advanced metering infrastructure reads.

attributes.name: checkBilling
attributes.documentation: True if as a result of an inspection or otherwise, there is a reason to suspect that a previous billing may have been performed with erroneous data. Value should be reset once this potential discrepancy has been resolved.

attributes.name: connectionCategory
attributes.documentation: A code used to specify the connection category, e.g., low voltage or low pressure, where the usage point is defined.

attributes.name: connectionState
attributes.documentation: State of the usage point with respect to connection to the network.

attributes.name: disconnectionMethod
attributes.documentation: Is an indication of how the usage point is physically connected or disconnected.

attributes.name: estimatedLoad
attributes.documentation: Estimated load.

attributes.name: grounded
attributes.documentation: True if grounded.

attributes.name: isSdp
attributes.documentation: If true, this usage point is a service delivery point, i.e., a usage point where the ownership of the service changes hands.

attributes.name: isVirtual
attributes.documentation: If true, this usage point is virtual, i.e., no physical location exists in the network where a meter could be located to collect the meter readings. For example, one may define a virtual usage point to serve as an aggregation of usage for all of a company's premises distributed widely across the distribution territory. Otherwise, the usage point is physical, i.e., there is a logical point in the network where a meter could be located to collect meter readings.

attributes.name: minimalUsageExpected
attributes.documentation: If true, minimal or zero usage is expected at this usage point for situations such as premises vacancy, logical or physical disconnect. It is used for readings validation and estimation.

attributes.name: nominalServiceVoltage
attributes.documentation: Nominal service voltage.

attributes.name: outageRegion
attributes.documentation: Outage region in which this usage point is located.

attributes.name: phaseCode
attributes.documentation: Phase code. Number of wires and specific nominal phases can be deduced from enumeration literal values. For example, ABCN is three-phase, four-wire, s12n (splitSecondary12N) is single-phase, three-wire, and s1n and s2n are single-phase, two-wire.

attributes.name: phaseCount
attributes.documentation: Number of potential phases the Usage Point supports, typically 0, 1 or 3.

attributes.name: physicalConnectionCapacity
attributes.documentation: Quantitative information about the maximum physical capacity of the connection for the usage point.

attributes.name: ratedCurrent
attributes.documentation: Current flow that this usage point is configured to deliver.

attributes.name: ratedPower
attributes.documentation: Active power that this usage point is configured to deliver.

attributes.name: readCycle
attributes.documentation: Cycle day on which the meter for this usage point will normally be read.  Usually correlated with the billing cycle.

attributes.name: readRoute
attributes.documentation: Identifier of the route to which this usage point is assigned for purposes of meter reading. Typically used to configure hand held meter reading systems prior to collection of reads.

attributes.name: serviceDeliveryRemark
attributes.documentation: Remarks about this usage point, for example the reason for it being rated with a non-nominal priority.

attributes.name: servicePriority
attributes.documentation: Priority of service for this usage point. Note that usage points at the same service location can have different priorities.

classes.name: UsagePointGroup
classes.documentation: Abstraction for management of group communications within a two-way AMR system or the data for a group of related usage points. Commands can be issued to all of the usage points that belong to a usage point group using a defined group address and the underlying AMR communication infrastructure.

attributes.name: type
attributes.documentation: Type of this group.

classes.name: UsagePointLocation
classes.documentation: Location of an individual usage point.

attributes.name: accessMethod
attributes.documentation: Method for the service person to access this usage point location. For example, a description of where to obtain a key if the facility is unmanned and secured.

attributes.name: remark
attributes.documentation: Remarks about this location.

attributes.name: siteAccessProblem
attributes.documentation: Problems previously encountered when visiting or performing work at this location. Examples include: bad dog, violent customer, verbally abusive occupant, obstructions, safety hazards, etc.

subPackages.documentation:

Some are related to pending CIM issues, but the majority are drawn by hand from Metering-related XSDs that are in Part 9 document (Ed.1). Entry points into the schema are filled with green. Non-used associations are light grey.

subPackages.name: LoadControl
subPackages.documentation: This package is an extension of the Metering package and contains the information classes that support specialised applications such as demand-side management using load control equipment. These classes are generally associated with the point where a service is delivered to the customer.

classes.name: ConnectDisconnectFunction
classes.documentation: A function that will disconnect and reconnect the customer's load under defined conditions.

attributes.name: eventCount
attributes.documentation: Running cumulative count of connect or disconnect events, for the lifetime of this function or until the value is cleared.

attributes.name: isConnected
attributes.documentation: True if this function is in the connected state.

attributes.name: isDelayedDiscon
attributes.documentation: If set true, the switch may disconnect the service at the end of a specified time delay after the disconnect signal has been given. If set false, the switch may disconnect the service immediately after the disconnect signal has been given. This is typically the case for over current circuit-breakers which are classified as either instantaneous or slow acting.

attributes.name: isLocalAutoDisconOp
attributes.documentation: If set true and if disconnection can be operated locally, the operation happens automatically. Otherwise it happens manually.

attributes.name: isLocalAutoReconOp
attributes.documentation: If set true and if reconnection can be operated locally, then the operation happens automatically. Otherwise, it happens manually.

attributes.name: isRemoteAutoDisconOp
attributes.documentation: If set true and if disconnection can be operated remotely, then the operation happens automatically. If set false and if disconnection can be operated remotely, then the operation happens manually.

attributes.name: isRemoteAutoReconOp
attributes.documentation: If set true and if reconnection can be operated remotely, then the operation happens automatically. If set false and if reconnection can be operated remotely, then the operation happens manually.

attributes.name: rcdInfo
attributes.documentation: Information on remote connect disconnect switch.

classes.name: RemoteConnectDisconnectInfo
classes.documentation: Details of remote connect and disconnect function.

attributes.name: armedTimeout
attributes.documentation: Setting of the timeout elapsed time.

attributes.name: customerVoltageLimit
attributes.documentation: Voltage limit on customer side of RCD switch above which the connect should not be made.

attributes.name: energyLimit
attributes.documentation: Limit of energy before disconnect.

attributes.name: energyUsageStartDateTime
attributes.documentation: Start date and time to accumulate energy for energy usage limiting.

attributes.name: energyUsageWarning
attributes.documentation: Warning energy limit, used to trigger event code that energy usage is nearing limit.

attributes.name: isArmConnect
attributes.documentation: True if the RCD switch has to be armed before a connect action can be initiated.

attributes.name: isArmDisconnect
attributes.documentation: True if the RCD switch has to be armed before a disconnect action can be initiated.

attributes.name: isEnergyLimiting
attributes.documentation: True if the energy usage is limited and the customer will be disconnected if they go over the limit.

attributes.name: needsPowerLimitCheck
attributes.documentation: True if load limit has to be checked to issue an immediate disconnect (after a connect) if load is over the limit.

attributes.name: needsVoltageLimitCheck
attributes.documentation: True if voltage limit has to be checked to prevent connect if voltage is over the limit.

attributes.name: powerLimit
attributes.documentation: Load limit above which the connect should either not take place or should cause an immediate disconnect.

attributes.name: usePushbutton
attributes.documentation: True if pushbutton has to be used for connect.

subPackages.name: PaymentMetering
subPackages.documentation: This package is an extension of the Metering package and contains the information classes that support specialised applications such as prepayment metering. These classes are generally associated with the collection and control of revenue from the customer for a delivered service.

classes.name: AccountMovement
classes.documentation: Credit/debit movements for an account.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.documentation: Amount that was credited to/debited from an account. For example: payment received/interest charge on arrears.

attributes.name: dateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time when the credit/debit transaction was performed.

attributes.name: reason
attributes.documentation: Reason for credit/debit transaction on an account. Example: payment received/arrears interest levied.

classes.name: AccountingUnit
classes.documentation: Unit for accounting; use either 'energyUnit' or 'currencyUnit' to specify the unit for 'value'.

attributes.name: energyUnit
attributes.documentation: Unit of service.

attributes.name: monetaryUnit
attributes.documentation: Unit of currency.

attributes.name: multiplier
attributes.documentation: Multiplier for the 'energyUnit' or 'monetaryUnit'.

attributes.name: value
attributes.documentation: Value expressed in applicable units.

classes.name: BankAccountDetail
classes.documentation: Details of a bank account.

attributes.name: accountNumber
attributes.documentation: Operational account reference number.

attributes.name: bankName
attributes.documentation: Name of bank where account is held.

attributes.name: branchCode
attributes.documentation: Branch of bank where account is held.

attributes.name: holderID
attributes.documentation: National identity number (or equivalent) of account holder.

attributes.name: holderName
attributes.documentation: Name of account holder.

classes.name: Due
classes.documentation: Details on amounts due for an account.

attributes.name: arrears
attributes.documentation: Part of 'current' that constitutes the arrears portion.

attributes.name: charges
attributes.documentation: Part of 'current' that constitutes the charge portion: 'charges' = 'Charge.fixedPortion' + 'Charge.variablePortion'.

attributes.name: current
attributes.documentation: Current total amount now due: current = principle + arrears + interest + charges. Typically the rule for settlement priority is: interest dues, then arrears dues, then current dues, then charge dues.

attributes.name: interest
attributes.documentation: Part of 'current' that constitutes the interest portion.

attributes.name: principle
attributes.documentation: Part of 'current' that constitutes the portion of the principle amount currently due.

classes.name: LineDetail
classes.documentation: Details on an amount line, with rounding, date and note.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.documentation: Amount for this line item.

attributes.name: dateTime
attributes.documentation: Date and time when this line was created in the application process.

attributes.name: note
attributes.documentation: Free format note relevant to this line.

attributes.name: rounding
attributes.documentation: Totalised monetary value of all errors due to process rounding or truncating that is not reflected in 'amount'.

classes.name: ChargeKind
classes.documentation: Kind of charge.

literals.name: consumptionCharge
literals.documentation: The charge levied for the actual usage of the service, normally expressed in terms of a tariff. For example: usage x price per kWh = total charge for consumption.

literals.name: demandCharge
literals.documentation: The charge related to the usage within a defined time interval, normally expressed in terms of a tariff. For example: a maximum-demand tariff will levy an additional charge on top of the consumption charge if the usage exceeds a defined limit per hour.

literals.name: auxiliaryCharge
literals.documentation: Any other charge which is not a consumptionCharge or demandCharge. For example: debt recovery, arrears, standing charge or charge for another service such as street lighting.

literals.name: taxCharge
literals.documentation: Any charge that is classified as a tax of a kind. For example: VAT, GST, TV tax, etc.

classes.name: ChequeKind
classes.documentation: Kind of cheque.

literals.name: postalOrder
literals.documentation: Payment order used by institutions other than banks.

literals.name: bankOrder
literals.documentation: Payment order used by a bank.

classes.name: SupplierKind
classes.documentation: Kind of supplier.

literals.name: utility
literals.documentation: Entity that delivers the service to the customer.

literals.name: retailer
literals.documentation: Entity that sells the service, but does not deliver to the customer; applies to the deregulated markets.

literals.name: mdma
literals.documentation: Meter Data Management Agent (MDMA) reads meters, validates meter data, and estimates missing data to be used in various applications

literals.name: msp
literals.documentation: Managed service provider (MSP) delivers services, such as network, application, infrastructure and security, via ongoing and regular support and active administration

classes.name: TenderKind
classes.documentation: Kind of tender.

literals.name: cheque
literals.documentation: Payment method by means of a cheque.

literals.name: card
literals.documentation: Payment method by means of a credit or debit card.

literals.name: cash
literals.documentation: Payment method by means of cash.

literals.name: other
literals.documentation: Other payment method such as electronic finds transfer.

classes.name: TransactionKind
classes.documentation: Kind of transaction.

literals.name: auxiliaryChargePayment
literals.documentation: Payment against a specified auxiliary account.

literals.name: diversePayment
literals.documentation: Payment against an item other than an account.

literals.name: tokenSalePayment
literals.documentation: Payment for a credit token sale to a customer.

literals.name: tokenFreeIssue
literals.documentation: Issue of a free credit token where the donor is the supplier.

literals.name: tokenGrant
literals.documentation: Issue of a free credit token where the donor is a 3rd party.

literals.name: tokenExchange
literals.documentation: Exchange of a previously issued token for a new token.

literals.name: tokenCancellation
literals.documentation: Cancellation of a previously issued token.

literals.name: meterConfigurationToken
literals.documentation: Issue of token that will alter the meter configuration.

classes.name: AuxiliaryAccount
classes.documentation: Variable and dynamic part of auxiliary agreement, generally representing the current state of the account related to the outstanding balance defined in auxiliary agreement.

attributes.name: balance
attributes.documentation: The total amount currently remaining on this account that is required to be paid in order to settle the account to zero. This excludes any due amounts not yet paid.

attributes.name: due
attributes.documentation: Current amounts now due for payment on this account.

attributes.name: lastCredit
attributes.documentation: Details of the last credit transaction performed on this account.

attributes.name: lastDebit
attributes.documentation: Details of the last debit transaction performed on this account.

attributes.name: principleAmount
attributes.documentation: The initial principle amount, with which this account was instantiated.

classes.name: AuxiliaryAgreement
classes.documentation:
An ad-hoc auxiliary account agreement associated with a customer agreement, not part of the customer's account, but typically subject to formal agreement between customer and supplier (utility). Typically this is used to collect revenue owed by the customer for other services or arrears accrued with the utility for other services. It is typically linked to a prepaid token purchase transaction, thus forcing the customer to make a payment towards settlement of the auxiliary account balance whenever the customer needs to purchase a prepaid token for electricity.
The present status of the auxiliary agreement can be defined in the context of the utility's business rules, for example: enabled, disabled, pending, over recovered, under recovered, written off, etc.

attributes.name: arrearsInterest
attributes.documentation: The interest per annum to be charged prorata on 'AuxiliaryAccount.dueArrears' at the end of each 'payCycle'.

attributes.name: auxCycle
attributes.documentation: The frequency for automatically recurring auxiliary charges, where 'AuxiliaryAccount.initialCharge' is recursively added to 'AuxiliaryAccount.dueCurrent' at the start of each 'auxCycle'. For example: on a specified date and time; hourly; daily; weekly; monthly; 3-monthly; 6-monthly; 12-monthly; etc.

attributes.name: auxPriorityCode
attributes.documentation: The coded priority indicating the priority that this auxiliary agreement has above other auxiliary agreements (associated with the same customer agreement) when it comes to competing for settlement from a payment transaction or token purchase.

attributes.name: fixedAmount
attributes.documentation: The fixed amount that has to be collected from each vending transaction towards settlement of this auxiliary agreement. Note that there may be multiple tokens vended per vending transaction, but this is not relevant.

attributes.name: minAmount
attributes.documentation: The minimum amount that has to be paid at any transaction towards settling this auxiliary agreement or reducing the balance.

attributes.name: payCycle
attributes.documentation: The contractually expected payment frequency (by the customer). Examples are: ad-hoc; on specified date; hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. etc.

attributes.name: subType
attributes.documentation: Sub-classification of the inherited 'type' for this AuxiliaryAgreement.

attributes.name: vendPortion
attributes.documentation: The percentage of the transaction amount that has to be collected from each vending transaction towards settlement of this auxiliary agreement when payments are not in arrears. Note that there may be multiple tokens vended per vending transaction, but this is not relevant.

attributes.name: vendPortionArrear
attributes.documentation: The percentage of the transaction amount that has to be collected from each vending transaction towards settlement of this auxiliary agreement when payments are in arrears. Note that there may be multiple tokens vended per vending transaction, but this is not relevant.

classes.name: Card
classes.documentation: Documentation of the tender when it is a type of card (credit, debit, etc).

attributes.name: accountHolderName
attributes.documentation: Name of account holder.

attributes.name: cvNumber
attributes.documentation: The card verification number.

attributes.name: expiryDate
attributes.documentation: The date when this card expires.

attributes.name: pan
attributes.documentation: The primary account number.

classes.name: Cashier
classes.documentation: The operator of the point of sale for the duration of CashierShift. Cashier is under the exclusive management control of Vendor.

attributes.name: electronicAddress
attributes.documentation: Electronic address.

classes.name: CashierShift
classes.documentation: The operating shift for a cashier, during which the cashier may transact against the cashier shift, subject to vendor shift being open.

attributes.name: cashFloat
attributes.documentation: The amount of cash that the cashier brings to start the shift and that will be taken away at the end of the shift; i.e. the cash float does not get banked.

classes.name: Charge
classes.documentation: A charge element associated with other entities such as tariff structures, auxiliary agreements or other charge elements. The total charge amount applicable to this instance of charge is the sum of fixed and variable portion.

attributes.name: fixedPortion
attributes.documentation: The fixed portion of this charge element.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: The kind of charge to be applied.

attributes.name: variablePortion
attributes.documentation: The variable portion of this charge element, calculated as a percentage of the total amount of a parent charge.

classes.name: Cheque
classes.documentation: The actual tender when it is a type of cheque.

attributes.name: bankAccountDetail
attributes.documentation: Details of the account holder and bank.

attributes.name: chequeNumber
attributes.documentation: Cheque reference number as printed on the cheque.

attributes.name: date
attributes.documentation: Date when cheque becomes valid.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of cheque.

attributes.name: micrNumber
attributes.documentation: The magnetic ink character recognition number printed on the cheque.

classes.name: ConsumptionTariffInterval
classes.documentation: One of a sequence of intervals defined in terms of consumption quantity of a service such as electricity, water, gas, etc. It is typically used in association with TariffProfile to define the steps or blocks in a step tariff structure, where startValue simultaneously defines the entry value of this step and the closing value of the previous step. Where consumption is >= startValue it falls within this interval and where consumption is < startValue it falls within the previous interval.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: A sequential reference that defines the identity of this interval and its relative position with respect to other intervals in a sequence of intervals.

attributes.name: startValue
attributes.documentation: The lowest level of consumption that defines the starting point of this interval. The interval extends to the start of the next interval or until it is reset to the start of the first interval by TariffProfile.tariffCycle.

classes.name: MerchantAccount
classes.documentation: The operating account controlled by merchant agreement, against which the vendor may vend tokens or receipt payments. Transactions via vendor shift debit the account and bank deposits via bank statement credit the account.

attributes.name: currentBalance
attributes.documentation: The current operating balance of this account.

attributes.name: provisionalBalance
attributes.documentation: The balance of this account after taking into account any pending debits from VendorShift.merchantDebitAmount and pending credits from BankStatement.merchantCreditAmount or credits (see also BankStatement attributes and VendorShift attributes).

classes.name: MerchantAgreement
classes.documentation: A formal controlling contractual agreement between supplier and merchant, in terms of which the merchant is authorised to vend tokens and receipt payments on behalf of the supplier. The merchant is accountable to the supplier for revenue collected at point of sale.

classes.name: PointOfSale
classes.documentation: Logical point where transactions take place with operational interaction between cashier and the payment system; in certain cases the point of sale interacts directly with the end customer, in which case the cashier might not be a real person: for example a self-service kiosk or over the internet.

attributes.name: location
attributes.documentation: Local description for where this point of sale is physically located.

classes.name: Receipt
classes.documentation: Record of total receipted payment from customer.

attributes.name: isBankable
attributes.documentation: True if this receipted payment is manually bankable, otherwise it is an electronic funds transfer.

attributes.name: line
attributes.documentation: Receipted amount with rounding, date and note.

classes.name: ServiceSupplier
classes.documentation: Organisation that provides services to customers.

attributes.name: issuerIdentificationNumber
attributes.documentation: Unique transaction reference prefix number issued to an entity by the International Organization for Standardization for the purpose of tagging onto electronic financial transactions, as defined in ISO/IEC 7812-1 and ISO/IEC 7812-2.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of supplier.

classes.name: Shift
classes.documentation:
Generally referring to a period of operation or work performed. Whether the shift is open/closed can be derived from attributes 'activityInterval.start' and 'activityInterval.end'.
The grand total for receipts (i.e., cumulative total of all actual receipted amounts during this shift; bankable + non-bankable; excludes rounding error totals) can be derived from receipt:
=sum('Receipt.receiptAmount'); includes bankable and non-bankable receipts.
It also has to be reconciled against:
=sum('receiptsGrandTotalBankable' + 'receiptsGrandTotalNonBankable')
and against receipt summary:
=sum('ReceiptSummary.receiptsTotal').
The attributes with "GrandTotal" defined in this class may need to be used when the source data is periodically flushed from the system and then these cannot be derived.

attributes.name: activityInterval
attributes.documentation: Interval for activity of this shift.

attributes.name: receiptsGrandTotalBankable
attributes.documentation:
Total of amounts receipted during this shift that can be manually banked (cash and cheques for example). Values are obtained from Receipt attributes:
=sum(Receipt.receiptAmount) for all Receipt.bankable = true.

attributes.name: receiptsGrandTotalNonBankable
attributes.documentation:
Total of amounts receipted during this shift that cannot be manually banked (card payments for example). Values are obtained from Receipt attributes:
=sum(Receipt.receiptAmount) for all Receipt.bankable = false.

attributes.name: receiptsGrandTotalRounding
attributes.documentation:
Cumulative amount in error due to process rounding not reflected in receiptsGrandTotal. Values are obtained from Receipt attributes:
=sum(Receipt.receiptRounding).

attributes.name: transactionsGrandTotal
attributes.documentation:
Cumulative total of transacted amounts during this shift. Values are obtained from transaction:
=sum('Transaction.transactionAmount'). It also has to be reconciled against transaction summary:
=sum('TransactionSummary.transactionsTotal').

attributes.name: transactionsGrandTotalRounding
attributes.documentation:
Cumulative amount in error due to process rounding not reflected in transactionsGandTotal. Values are obtained from Transaction attributes:
=sum(Transaction.transactionRounding).

classes.name: TariffProfile
classes.documentation: A schedule of charges; structure associated with Tariff that allows the definition of complex tarif structures such as step and time of use when used in conjunction with TimeTariffInterval and Charge. Inherited 'status.value' is defined in the context of the utility's business rules, for example: active, inactive, etc.

attributes.name: tariffCycle
attributes.documentation: The frequency at which the tariff charge schedule is repeated. Examples are: once off on a specified date and time; hourly; daily; weekly; monthly; 3-monthly; 6-monthly; 12-monthly; etc. At the end of each cycle, the business rules are reset to start from the beginning again.

classes.name: Tender
classes.documentation:
Tender is what is "offered" by the customer towards making a payment and is often more than the required payment (hence the need for 'change'). The payment is thus that part of the Tender that goes towards settlement of a particular transaction.
Tender is modelled as an aggregation of Cheque and Card. Both these tender types can exist in a single tender bid thus 'accountHolderName' has to exist separately in each of Cheque and Card as each could have a different account holder name.

attributes.name: amount
attributes.documentation: Amount tendered by customer.

attributes.name: change
attributes.documentation: Difference between amount tendered by customer and the amount charged by point of sale.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of tender from customer.

classes.name: TimeTariffInterval
classes.documentation: One of a sequence of time intervals defined in terms of real time. It is typically used in association with TariffProfile to define the intervals in a time of use tariff structure, where startDateTime simultaneously determines the starting point of this interval and the ending point of the previous interval.

attributes.name: sequenceNumber
attributes.documentation: A sequential reference that defines the identity of this interval and its relative position with respect to other intervals in a sequence of intervals.

attributes.name: startTime
attributes.documentation: A real time marker that defines the starting time (typically it is the time of day) for this interval. The interval extends to the start of the next interval or until it is reset to the start of the first interval by TariffProfile.tariffCycle.

classes.name: Transaction
classes.documentation: The record of details of payment for service or token sale.

attributes.name: diverseReference
attributes.documentation: Formal reference for use with diverse payment (traffic fine for example).

attributes.name: donorReference
attributes.documentation: Reference to the entity that is the source of 'amount' (for example: customer for token purchase; or supplier for free issue token).

attributes.name: kind
attributes.documentation: Kind of transaction.

attributes.name: line
attributes.documentation: Transaction amount, rounding, date and note for this transaction line.

attributes.name: receiverReference
attributes.documentation: Reference to the entity that is the recipient of 'amount' (for example, supplier for service charge payment; or tax receiver for VAT).

attributes.name: reversedId
attributes.documentation: (if 'kind' is transactionReversal) Reference to the original transaction that is being reversed by this transaction.

attributes.name: serviceUnitsEnergy
attributes.documentation: Actual amount of service units that is being paid for.

attributes.name: serviceUnitsError
attributes.documentation: Number of service units not reflected in 'serviceUnitsEnergy' due to process rounding or truncating errors.

classes.name: Transactor
classes.documentation: The entity that ultimately executes the transaction and which is in control of the process; typically this is embodied in secure software running on a server that may employ secure hardware encryption devices for secure transaction processing.

classes.name: Vendor
classes.documentation: The entity that owns the point of sale and contracts with the cashier to receipt payments and vend tokens using the payment system. The vendor has a private contract with and is managed by the merchant which is a type of organisation. The vendor is accountable to the merchant for revenue collected, and the merchant is in turn accountable to the supplier.

classes.name: VendorShift
classes.documentation: The operating shift for a vendor during which the vendor may transact against the merchant's account. It aggregates transactions and receipts during the shift and periodically debits a merchant account. The totals in vendor shift should always be the sum of totals aggregated in all cashier shifts that were open under the particular vendor shift.

attributes.name: merchantDebitAmount
attributes.documentation: The amount that is to be debited from the merchant account for this vendor shift. This amount reflects the sum(PaymentTransaction.transactionAmount).

attributes.name: posted
attributes.documentation: If true, merchantDebitAmount has been debited from MerchantAccount; typically happens at the end of VendorShift when it closes.

subPackages.name: InfIEC61968
subPackages.documentation:
This package and its subpackages contain informative (unstable) elements of the model, expected to evolve a lot or to be removed, and not published as IEC document yet. Some portions of it will be reworked and moved to normative packages as the need arises, and some portions may be removed.
WG14 does not generate documentation for this informative portion of the model.

subPackages.name: Sandbox
subPackages.documentation:
This package contains informative classes (new and old) that we are working on in DCIM12 and that should be promoted to normative as soon as we deem them stable enough.
We did not rename existing Inf*** packages on purpose, because we sometimes refer to them and their classes in issues. Package below this sandbox will disappear, as soon as their content moves to normative.

classes.name: Text
classes.documentation: [Comments by Tanja & replies by Greg, early 2008] Usage in messages (with DCIM 9) of classes Diagram and Map: - Permit message uses both Diagram and Map (from GmlDiagramObject). - ServiceWork and Design messages use only Map. - Presentation message is a list of Diagram-s with links to about anything in the model 1) Diagram 1.a) Beautify the doc - say what the Diagram is in this model. [Greg] OK 2) Map According to the docs of attributes: 2.2) 'mapLocGrid' is said to be "Map grid number." Why is a number represented with a string? Cannot we use some of the attributes inherited from IdentifiedObject (e.g., localName or name)? [Greg] Seems reasonable. We could check with Mike Daniels and Phillip Jones (also Scott Neumann and Chris Macqueen were involved with this) for their thoughts. 2.3) Question: Does Map need to inherit from Diagram (including kind attribute)? The usage of both Diagram and Map in Permit message indicates to me that they are different. It would maybe be better to introduce a common superclass (e.g., Presentation, or whatever) and make these two inherit from it. Also, all three shown associations from Diagram should be moved to the new superclass and properly renamed. 2.4) Consider clearly documenting each class. [Greg] OK 2.5) Consider renaming GmlDiagramObject (e.g., GmlObject, GmlGeometry, GmlGraphicalObject, or whatever). [Greg] OK with me. Discuss with Phillip Jones. 3) DesignLocation It is said to be "a logical part of the design (e.g., pole and all equipment on a pole)". It is however not (subclass of) Location. 3.a) I would rename the class, but don't know how... Maybe DesignPart or DesignComponent. Update association ends' names. 3.b) If 1.a accepted, then rename DesignLocationCU the same way and update its doc and association end names. [Greg] We should discuss this with the Part 6 Team, particularly Chris Heineman & Ian Wells since they drove all of the modeling. 4) GmlDiagramObject It sounds strange to say GmlDiagramObject' IS-A Location; GmlDiagramObject rather HAS A Location. This just stroke me from this diagram, but will do more later, in GMLSupport package. [Greg] Discuss with Phillip Jones.

subPackages.name: InfAssets
subPackages.documentation:
The package is used to define asset-level models for objects. Assets may be comprised of other assets and may have relationships to other assets. Assets also have owners and values. Assets may also have a relationship to a PowerSystemResource in the Wires model. TODO: The following has been copied from a very old version of draft Part 11, so the references are wrong, but we store the knowledge here to reuse later: "Assets are the basic units which define a physical infrastructure. PowerSystemResources are logical objects meaningful to operations which are constructed from one or more Assets, although PowerSystemResources are not required to specifiy their component Assets. The Asset package is comprosed of several packages. The key concepts of an Asset are as follows:
  • Assets can have names, through inheritance to the Naming package
  • Assets are physical entities which have a lifecycle
  • One or more assets can be associated to create a PowerSystemResource
  • Assets can be grouped (aggregated) with other Assets
  • Assets are typically either 'point' or 'linear' assets, which relate to physical geometry
  • Assets have a close relationship to Work as a consequence of their lifecycle
The following sections describe the packages in the Assets package. The AssetBasics package defines the relationship between Asset and other classes, such as Organization, PowerSystemResource and Document. Point assets are those assets whose physical location can be described in terms of a single coordinate, such as a pole or a switch. Linear assets are those assets whose physical location is best described in terms of a line, plyline or polygon. Asset work triggers are used to determine when inspection and/or maintenance are required for assets".

classes.name: CoolingPowerRating
classes.documentation:
There are often stages of power which are associated with stages of cooling. For instance, a transformer may be rated 121kV on the primary, 15kV on the secondary and 4kV on the tertiary winding. These are voltage ratings and the power ratings are generally the same for all three windings and independent of the voltage ratings, there are instances where the tertiary may have a lower power rating.
For example, for three stages, the power rating may be 15/20/25 MVA and the cooling is OA/FA/FOA. The 15 MVA rating goes with the OA cooling (Oil and Air cooling). This is called the self cooled rating as there are no external cooling enhancements. The 20 MVA rating goes with the FA cooling (Forced Air cooling), this means that when the fans are running and thus enhancing the cooling characteristics, the transformer can operate at a power level of 20 MVA. The 25 MVA rating goes with the FOA cooling (Forced Oil and Air cooling), this means that when the fans and pumps are running and thus enhancing the cooling characteristics even more than before, the transformer can operate at a power level of 25 MVA. This 15/20/25 MVA does not state how the power is split between the various windings. It may be 25 MVA input on the primary, 25 MVA output on the secondary and 0 MVA output on the tertiary. It may also operate at 25 MVA input on the primary, 17 MVA output on the secondary and 8 MVA output on the tertiary.

classes.documentation:
[tanja] How to refactor test- and observation-related classes, to consolidate with DistributionWindingTest? What of this is per model, what is per asset? [tom] Any of these Observation classes will be per Asset, since they are done in field inspections of specific instances. To me, it would help if we had an Observation class between IdentifiedObject and the observation-related classes, to hold the status and some other common attributes of inspection tests. This idea would also apply to switches and other assets, although we are not looking at them right now. The DWTest classes were intended for the model-specific tests. If we try to splice in the instance-specific tests, it could lead to more confusion. [tanja] We also have some Procedure classes, with related data sets, so let's address instance-related stuff when needed (probably with Part 4 or 6?). [tanja, 2009-08-20]
  • What ElectricalInfo attributes (if any) are needed for BushingModel?
  • PowerRating is really not a good name for what the class is really used.
[tanja, 2010-01-31]
  • Reexamine relationships to PSR-related classes
[tanja, 2011-09-01]
  • Added hyperlinks to diagrams: The first three are normative, appearing in 61968-11. The last one shows informative xformer-related *Info classes (as this diagram is showing old xformer asset-related classes).
  • Renamed PowerRating to CoolingPowerRating.

subPackages.name: InfWork
subPackages.documentation:
The package covers all types of work, including inspection, maintenance, repair, restoration, and construction. It covers the full life cycle including request, initiate, track and record work. Standardized designs (compatible units) are used where possible.

TODO: The following has been copied from a very old version of draft Part 11, so the references are wrong, but we store the knowledge here to reuse later:
"The Work package is used to define classes related to work. There are several different aspects of work.
The Work Initiation (Work, Project, Request).
The Work Design package is used for managing designs (CompatibleUnit, Design, DesignLocation, WorkTask).
The Work Schedule package is used for the scheduling and coordination of work (AccessPermit, MaterialItem, OneCallRequest, Regulation).
The Work Closing package is used for tracking costs of work (CostType, LaborItem, WorkCostDetail, VehicleItem).
The Work Standards package is used for the definition of compatible units (CULaborItem, CUVehicleItem, CUGroup).
This package is used for inspection and maintenance (InspectionDataSet, Procedure).
The WorkService package defines Appointment class".

classes.name: TypeMaterial
classes.documentation:
Documentation for a generic material item that may be used for design, work and other purposes. Any number of MaterialItems manufactured by various vendors may be used to perform this TypeMaterial.
Note that class analagous to "AssetModel" is not used for material items. This is because in some cases, for example, a utility sets up a Master material record for a 3 inch long half inch diameter steel bolt and they do not necessarily care what specific supplier is providing the material item. As different vendors are used to supply the part, the Stock Code of the material item can stay the same. In other cases, each time the vendor changes, a new stock code is set up so they can track material used by vendor. Therefore a Material Item "Model" is not typically needed.

classes.name: CustomerBillingInfo
classes.documentation:
The creation of the monthly customer billing statements is the method employed to notify Customers of charges, adjustments and credits applied to their account for Services and Products. The actuall billing occurs through an ErpInvoice. The CustomerBillingInfo includes information from the payment, collection, meter reading, installed meter, service, site, customer, customer account, customer agreement, services and pricing subject areas. Each component price shows up as a separate line item on the ErpInvoice.
The Customer Billing Statement may include collection and account messages, marketing/civic event messages and bill inserts.
One Customer Billing Statement is produced for all Agreements under a CustomerAccount per billing cycle date defined in 'CustomerAccount.billingCycle'.
The history of CustomerBillingInfo, Invoices and Payments is to be maintained in associated ActivityRecords.

attributes.name: billingDate
attributes.documentation: Business date designated for the billing run which produced this CustomerBillingInfo.

attributes.name: dueDate
attributes.documentation: Calculated date upon which a customer billing amount is due, used in the invoicing process to determine when a Customer's Payment is delinquent. It takes into consideration the regulatory criteria and the Customer's requested due date. In the absence of a Customer requested due date, the due date is typically calculated from the regulated number of days and the 'billingDate'.
